declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbability_bootstrapBoundedLipschitzDistance
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.52: conditional convergence of the bootstrap empirical process. For iid real observations with distribution function `F`, the bounded Lipschitz distance between the conditional law of `√n (F*ₙ - Fₙ)` and the law of the `F`-Brownian bridge `B⁰ ∘ F` tends to zero in outer probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.studentized_bootstrap_mean_second_order_accuracy
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.60, for the studentized mean in dimension one (`d = 1`, `g = id`). Assume all moments are finite, the variance is positive, and Cramér's condition holds for `(X, X²)`. With `T = √n (X̄ - μ)/σ̂` and its resampling analogue `T* = √n (X̄* - X̄)/σ̂*`: the Kolmogorov distance between the conditional law of `T*` and the law of `T` is `O_P(n⁻¹)`; the Kolmogorov distance between the law of `T` and `N(0,1)` is `n^{-1/2} sup_x |p₁(x) φ(x)| + o(n^{-1/2})` with `p₁(x) = γ (2x² + 1)/6`, `γ` the skewness; and the one-sided percentile-`t` interval `(-∞, X̄ - n^{-1/2} σ̂ v̂_α]` has coverage `1 - α + O(n⁻¹)`. The coverage statements for the normal-theory, percentile, two-sided, and symmetric intervals are outside this scope.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoWeakly_of_forall_lipschitz

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_iff_mathlib

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_comp_of_continuous

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_tendstoInProbabilityConst_sub
declarations.doc: Slutsky-type perturbation: if `Xₙ` converges in law and `Yₙ - Xₙ` converges to `0` in probability, then `Yₙ` has the same limit law. No separability is assumed; the difference need not be measurable, since convergence in probability is measured by the outer measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_measureReal_lt_norm_le_of_tendstoInDistribution
declarations.doc: A sequence converging in law is bounded in probability in norm: for every `ε > 0` there is `M > 0` with `P(‖Zₙ‖ > M) ≤ ε` eventually.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_zero_of_forall_eventually_le

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_delta_method_remainder

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_add_zero

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_zero_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: Domination: if eventually, for almost every `ω`, `|Yₙ| ≤ |Xₙ|` whenever `|Uₙ| < δ`, and `Xₙ, Uₙ → 0` in probability, then `Yₙ → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_const_of_tendsto

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_const_mul_zero

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_mul_zero_of_isBoundedInProbability

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_sampleMean_of_iid

declarations.name: CKSD.SatisfiesCramerCondition
declarations.doc: Cramér's condition `limsup_{‖t‖→∞} |E e^{i⟨t,X⟩}| < 1`, in the equivalent form of a uniform bound by a constant `c < 1` outside a ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_edgeworth_expansion_smooth_function_of_means
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.50: Edgeworth expansion of order `j` for a smooth function of a vector mean. Here `A` has `j+2` continuous derivatives on a neighbourhood of the mean `m`, `A m = 0`, and `σ² = ∇A(m)ᵀ Σ ∇A(m)` is written as the variance of the linear statistic `DA(m) X`. Under a moment of order `j+2` and Cramér's condition, there are polynomials `p_r`, `1 ≤ r ≤ j`, of degree at most `3r-1` and of parity opposite to `r`, such that the distribution function of `√n A(X̄)/σ` equals `Φ + Σ_r n^{-r/2} p_r φ` up to `o(n^{-j/2})` uniformly. The identification of the coefficients of `p_r` through the moments of order at most `r+2` and the derivatives of `A` is outside this scope.

declarations.name: CKSD.saddlepoint_approximation_sampleAverage_density
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.55: the saddlepoint approximation to the density of a sample mean. The cumulant generating function `K = cgf id P` is finite near the origin, `ŝ` lies in the interior of its domain with `K'(ŝ) = x`, `P` has a density, and the normalized tilted characteristic function `t ↦ |E e^{(ŝ+it)X}| / E e^{ŝX}` is in `L^ν` for some `ν ≥ 1`. Then for `n > ν` the mean of `n` observations has a continuous density `fₙ`, bounded when the characteristic function of `X` is also in `L^ν`, and `fₙ(x) = (n/(2π K''(ŝ)))^{1/2} e^{n(K(ŝ)-ŝx)} (1 + O(1/n))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_sqrt_mul_sqrt_of_forall_two_mul_le
declarations.doc: A real number `x` with `2 x ≤ δ A + B / δ` for every `δ > 0` satisfies `x ≤ √A √B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_sum_sub_of_iid
declarations.doc: A triangular-array weak law: if `n ∫ φₙ² dP → 0`, then the centred sums `∑_{i<n} (φₙ(Xᵢ) - ∫ φₙ dP)` of an iid sequence tend to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_sum_sq_of_iid

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_two_mul_log_one_add_sub_le
declarations.doc: A one-term logarithmic expansion: for `|g| ≤ 1/2`, `|2 log (1 + g) - (2 g - g²)| ≤ 4 |g|³`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_mul_measureReal_lt_abs_of_integrable_sq
declarations.doc: Uniform integrability of a square-integrable function along `√n`: for `c > 0`, `n P(|s| > c √n) → 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_and_integral_eq_of_hasDensity
declarations.doc: For a law with a density, a real function is integrable iff its product with the density is integrable for the reference measure, and the integrals agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_and_integral_eq_one_of_hasDensity
declarations.doc: The density of a probability law is integrable with integral one.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_deriv_param
declarations.doc: The derivative in a real parameter of a family of measurable functions, differentiable in the parameter, is measurable in the observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_deriv_sub_taylor_le
declarations.doc: A second-order Taylor bound for the derivative of a `C³` function whose third derivative is bounded by `M` on a ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sub_taylor_two_le
declarations.doc: A second-order Taylor bound for a `C³` function whose third derivative is bounded by `M` on a ball: the remainder is at most `M |t - θ₀|³`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sub_div_le_of_score_equation
declarations.doc: Deterministic core of Cramér's argument: from the linearized score equation `Z + W B + q = 0` with `B` close to `-I` and a quadratic remainder `q`, the scaled error `W` is within `4 κ |Z| / I²` of `Z / I`.

declarations.name: CKSD.scalarWaldStatistic
declarations.doc: Wald statistic of a scalar simple null `θ = θ₀`, with information evaluated at the estimate: `n (T - θ₀)² I(T)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.scalarScoreStatistic
declarations.doc: Rao score statistic of a scalar simple null: `ℓₙ'(θ₀)² / (n I(θ₀))`, written with the derivative of the sample log likelihood.

declarations.name: CKSD.iid_infinitePi_eval
declarations.doc: The coordinate process of the infinite product of a probability law is iid with that law.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_fin_eq_pi_of_iid
declarations.doc: The first `n` observations of an iid sequence have the `n`-fold product law.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoWeakly_pi_of_tendstoInDistribution
declarations.doc: Convergence in law of statistics of the first `n` observations of an iid sequence gives weak convergence of their laws under the `n`-fold product measures.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityZero_pi_iff_of_iid
declarations.doc: Convergence to zero in probability under the `n`-fold product measures is convergence to zero in probability of the same statistics of the first `n` observations of an iid sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_fisherInformation

declarations.name: CKSD.deriv_sampleLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: The derivative of the sample log likelihood is the sum of the likelihood scores.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_likelihoodScore_eq_zero_of_isMax
declarations.doc: At a global maximizer of a sample log likelihood that is differentiable in the parameter, the sum of the likelihood scores vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.pi_eq_withDensity_exp_sum_log_sub
declarations.doc: For a family with strictly positive densities, the `n`-fold product law at `θ` has density `exp (∑ᵢ (log f θ xᵢ - log f θ₀ xᵢ))` with respect to the product law at `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianReal_map_sq_div_eq_noncentralChiSquared
declarations.doc: If `X ~ N(m, I)` with `I > 0`, then `X² / I` has the noncentral chi-squared law with one degree of freedom and noncentrality `m² / I`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianReal_withDensity_exp_eq
declarations.doc: Exponential tilting of a centred Gaussian law: the density `exp (h z - h² I / 2)` turns `N(0, I)` into `N(h I, I)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.noncentral_limit_of_tilt
declarations.doc: The joint limit law of the test statistic and the log likelihood ratio under the null, `(Z² / I, h Z - h² I / 2)` with `Z ~ N(0, I)`, tilted by the likelihood ratio, has the noncentral chi-squared first marginal of the local alternative, and the likelihood ratio has mean one.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_prodMk_zero
declarations.doc: Componentwise convergence to zero in probability gives convergence to zero of the pair.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihood_test_expansions_of_iid
declarations.doc: Second-order expansions behind the likelihood-ratio, Wald, and score tests of a scalar simple null, on one probability space carrying an iid sample. Under the hypotheses of `mle_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality`, with `aₙ = √n (Tₙ - θ₀)` and the normalized score `Zₙ`, the likelihood-ratio statistic, the score statistic `Zₙ² / I`, and every plug-in Wald statistic `aₙ² J(Tₙ)` with `J` continuous at `θ₀` and `J θ₀ = I` differ from `I aₙ²` by `o_P(1)`, and the log likelihood ratio at `θ₀ + h / √n` equals `h Zₙ - h² I / 2 + o_P(1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihood_tests_sub_score_sq_infinitePi
declarations.doc: Reduction of the scalar likelihood tests to the squared normalized score, on the coordinate process of the infinite product `P θ₀ ^ ℕ`. Under the hypotheses of `tendstoWeakly_likelihoodRatio_wald_score_chiSquared`, the three statistics are measurable, the normalized score `Zₙ` of the first `n` coordinates converges in law to `N(0, I(θ₀))`, each of the three statistics of the first `n` coordinates differs from `Zₙ² / I(θ₀)` by `o_P(1)`, and the log likelihood ratio of `θ₀ + h / √n` against `θ₀` equals `h Zₙ - h² I(θ₀) / 2 + o_P(1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoWeakly_likelihoodRatio_wald_score_chiSquared
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.11, null part, for a scalar parameter and the simple null `Θ₀ = {θ₀}` (so `q = k = 1`, `c(θ) = θ - θ₀`, and the restricted maximizer is `θ₀`). Under the hypotheses of 102.3 at `θ₀` with Fisher information continuous at `θ₀`, and for consistent global maximizers `T n` of the sample log likelihood, the likelihood-ratio, Wald, and score statistics each converge in law to `χ²₁` under `P θ₀`, and the Wald and score statistics differ from the likelihood-ratio statistic by `o_P(1)`. Composite nulls with `q < k` are outside this scope.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoWeakly_likelihoodRatio_wald_score_noncentralChiSquared
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.11, local-alternative part, in the scalar simple-null scope of `tendstoWeakly_likelihoodRatio_wald_score_chiSquared`. If in addition the model is DQM at `θ₀` with the likelihood score, then under `P (θ₀ + h / √n)` each of the three statistics converges in law to the noncentral `χ²₁` with noncentrality `h² I(θ₀)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.scalarWaldStatistic_self

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ball_measurable_dominating_integral_lt

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_mle_of_compact

declarations.name: CKSD.m_estimator_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality

declarations.name: CKSD.regression_m_estimator_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCriterion_add_const
