declarations.name: CKSD.regressionMObjective_zero
declarations.doc: The zero-sample convex regression objective has value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.mle_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.3, scalar smooth likelihood-score roots and their efficient expansion. `ell` is the per-observation log likelihood; the score/information moment identities and the local third-derivative envelope are explicit hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_inv_sqrt_smul_sum_sub_of_iid
declarations.doc: The multivariate central limit theorem for IID Euclidean random vectors with finite second moment, centered by their common expectation and scaled by the square root of the sample size. The limiting covariance may be singular.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sqrt_smul_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: The Euclidean sample-mean central limit theorem in CKSD's weak-convergence convention, with the population covariance matrix as the limiting Gaussian covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCDF_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The empirical distribution function as a normalised sum of indicators.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCDF_mono
declarations.doc: The empirical distribution function is monotone.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCDF_extremes
declarations.doc: The empirical distribution function is `1` at `∑ |Xᵢ|` and `0` below `-∑ |Xᵢ|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_empiricalCDF_of_sampleQuantile_lt
declarations.doc: Order characterisation of the left sample quantile, for `n ≥ 1` and `p ∈ (0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_empiricalCDF
declarations.doc: Measurability of the empirical distribution function at a fixed point.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sampleQuantile
declarations.doc: Measurability of the left sample quantile, for `p ∈ (0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_ite_le_eq_cdf
declarations.doc: The integral of the indicator of `(-∞, a]` is the distribution function at `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sqrt_mul_inv_natCast
declarations.doc: `√n / n = 1 / √n`, in the form used for normalised sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_sqrt_mul_cdf_sub
declarations.doc: Local increments of a distribution function differentiable at `q`: `√n (F(q + t/√n) - F(q)) → f t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_sqrt_mul_empiricalCDF_sub
declarations.doc: The local empirical process at `q`: `√n (Fₙ(q + t/√n) - Fₙ(q)) → f t` in probability when the distribution function is differentiable at `q` with derivative `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sqrt_mul_sub_empiricalCDF
declarations.doc: Central limit theorem for the empirical distribution function at a point `q` with `F(q) = p`: `√n (p - Fₙ(q)) / f` converges in law to `N(0, p(1-p)/f²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_sub_of_crossing
declarations.doc: Ghosh's crossing lemma: if `Wₙ` is bounded in probability and, for all `t` and `ε > 0`, the probabilities of the crossing events `{Vₙ ≤ t, Wₙ ≥ t + ε}` and `{Vₙ ≥ t + ε, Wₙ ≤ t}` tend to `0`, then `Vₙ - Wₙ → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_bahadur_remainder
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.7: the first-order Bahadur representation.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sampleQuantile
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.6: asymptotic normality of a sample quantile.

declarations.name: CKSD.centredCriterionModulus
declarations.doc: Local modulus of the centred criterion process `Mₙ - M` on the ball of radius `δ` about `θ₀`, as a nonnegative extended-real random quantity.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_le_outerExpectation_div
declarations.doc: Markov's inequality for outer expectations: a set on which `f ≥ t` has outer measure at most `E* f / t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_rate_m_estimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.25: the rate theorem for `M`-estimators. Suppose the deterministic criterion has quadratic separation `M θ - M θ₀ ≤ -c d(θ,θ₀)²` near `θ₀`, and that for every `n ≥ 1` and all `δ` in a fixed interval `(0, δ₀)`, the outer expectation of the local modulus of `Mₙ - M` is at most `C φₙ(δ)/√n` with a constant `C ≥ 0`, where `δ ↦ φₙ(δ)/δ^a` is decreasing on `(0,∞)` for a fixed `a < 2`. If `rₙ² φₙ(1/rₙ) ≤ √n`, the estimator maximizes `Mₙ` up to `O_P(rₙ⁻²)`, and it is consistent in outer probability, then `rₙ d(Tₙ, θ₀) = O_P(1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientScore_eq_self_of_inner_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A score orthogonal to every nuisance score is its own efficient score.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientInformationMatrix
declarations.doc: Efficient information matrix `Ĩ_ij = ⟨ℓ̃_i, ℓ̃_j⟩` of a vector of `L²` scores, where `ℓ̃` is the residual after projection on the nuisance tangent space generated by `scores`.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientInfluence
declarations.doc: Efficient influence function `Ĩ⁻¹ ℓ̃(x)`, evaluated at an observation through the chosen representatives of the efficient scores.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRegularAlongPaths
declarations.doc: Regularity of an estimator sequence along a family of one-dimensional submodels `t ↦ Q i t` whose parameter moves in direction `dir i`: under the product law at `t = 1/√n`, the law of `√n (Tₙ - (θ + dir i / √n))` converges to the same `L` for every `i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_convolution_of_isRegularAlongPaths
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.34, convolution part. For every direction `a ∈ ℝᵏ` and nuisance score `g` in a linear space `G ⊆ L²(P)`, the submodel `t ↦ Q (a, g) t` passes through `P` at `t = 0`, has parameter `θ + t a`, is dominated by `ν`, and is QMD at `0` with score `a ⬝ ℓ̇ + g`. The nuisance tangent space is the closure of `G`. If the efficient information matrix is positive definite, the limit law of every estimator sequence regular along these submodels is the convolution of `N(0, Ĩ⁻¹)` with a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.isRegularAlongPaths_gaussian_iff_asymptotically_linear
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.34, efficiency part, in the setting of `exists_convolution_of_isRegularAlongPaths`. A measurable estimator sequence is regular along all submodels with limit `N(0, Ĩ⁻¹)` if and only if it is asymptotically linear in the efficient influence function under `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoInProbabilityZeroENNReal
declarations.doc: Convergence to zero in (outer) probability of nonnegative extended-real random quantities. An infinite value counts as exceeding every threshold.

declarations.name: CKSD.missingDataObservation
declarations.doc: Observed part `(R, X, R Y)` of a full-data triple `(R, X, Y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.crossFittedAverage_missingMean_asymptotically_linear
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.39: asymptotic linearity of the cross-fitted augmented inverse-probability estimator of a missing mean. The full-data triples `(R, X, Y)` are iid with law `P`, the response is missing at random with propensity `π₀`, and `m₀` is the regression of `Y` on `X`, both expressed by their defining integral identities. The estimators `(m̂, π̂)` on fold `k` are computed from the observed data `(R, X, RY)` outside fold `k`. For all sufficiently large sample sizes, the fold sizes are at least a fixed fraction of `n`. On each fold the `L²(P_X)` errors of `m̂` and `π̂` tend to zero in probability, their product is `o_P(n^{-1/2})`, and the `L²(P)` distance between the estimated and true scores, with the nuisance estimates held fixed, tends to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.locationLaw
declarations.doc: Location law with density `η (x - θ)` with respect to Lebesgue measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.locationFisherInformation
declarations.doc: Fisher information for location, `∫ η'² / η`, with the convention `η'²/0 = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.locationScore
declarations.doc: Location score `-η'(x-θ)/η(x-θ)` of the location family at `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSymmetricFiniteInformationDensity
declarations.doc: A symmetric probability density on the line that is absolutely continuous with locally integrable derivative `η'`, chosen odd, and has finite Fisher information for location. Choosing an odd version of the derivative is no restriction: the odd part of any version of the derivative of an even absolutely continuous function is again a version.

declarations.name: CKSD.symmetricNuisanceScores
declarations.doc: Scores of symmetric nuisance perturbations at `P` about the centre `θ`: mean-zero `L²` functions that are even about `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_reflect_locationLaw
declarations.doc: The reflection `x ↦ 2θ - x` preserves a symmetric location law centred at `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientScore_locationScore_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.41, efficient-score part: in the symmetric location model, with nuisance tangent space the closed span of the mean-zero `L²` functions that are even about `θ` (the scores of symmetric perturbations of `η`), the location score is orthogonal to the nuisance tangent space, so it is the efficient score, and the efficient information is the Fisher information `I_η`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_adaptive_estimator_center_of_symmetry
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.41, adaptation part: there are measurable estimators, not depending on the symmetric density, that are asymptotically normal with the efficient variance `I_η⁻¹` at every symmetric density of finite Fisher information, regularly along local location alternatives `θ + h/√n`. Regularity along symmetric nuisance perturbations is outside this scope.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasQuadraticMeanDerivAt
declarations.doc: Quadratic-mean differentiability at a parameter, without a domain restriction, using Statlib.

declarations.name: CKSD.nuisanceTangentSpace
declarations.doc: Closed nuisance tangent space generated by a specified class of `L²` nuisance scores.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientScore
declarations.doc: Efficient score as the residual after projecting out the nuisance tangent space.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientInformation
declarations.doc: Efficient information for a scalar score.

declarations.name: CKSD.contaminationLaw
declarations.doc: Contamination path for a probability law and one contaminating observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.influenceFunction
declarations.doc: Influence function as the right derivative of a statistical functional along contamination.

declarations.name: CKSD.missingMeanScore
declarations.doc: Missing-at-random augmented inverse-probability score.

declarations.name: CKSD.SampleSplit
declarations.doc: A finite partition of a sample into labeled folds. Empty folds are allowed in the definition.

declarations.name: CKSD.SampleSplit.trainingIndices
declarations.doc: Training indices for a fold are all indices outside that fold.

declarations.name: CKSD.crossFittedAverage
declarations.doc: Cross-fitted average with nuisance estimates trained exclusively on the other folds.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: Log likelihood of a finite iid sample with a given single-observation density.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihoodRatioStatistic
declarations.doc: Likelihood-ratio statistic comparing two specified log-likelihood values.

declarations.name: CKSD.waldStatistic
declarations.doc: Wald quadratic statistic with the estimated covariance of the parameter estimate.

declarations.name: CKSD.scoreStatistic
declarations.doc: Score quadratic statistic with the information matrix of the whole sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.bootstrapLaw
declarations.doc: Conditional nonparametric bootstrap law of a statistic, given the observed sample. For `n=0` this uses the zero empirical measure convention of `empiricalMeasure`.

declarations.name: CKSD.studentizedStatistic
declarations.doc: Standardization using an estimated standard deviation, with division-by-zero value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.edgeworthApproximation
declarations.doc: Finite-order Edgeworth distribution-function approximation for supplied correction polynomials.

declarations.name: CKSD.saddlepointDensity
declarations.doc: Saddlepoint approximation to the sample-mean density, for a chosen solution of `K'(s)=x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientInformation_nonneg
declarations.doc: Efficient information is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.waldStatistic_self
declarations.doc: A zero displacement gives a zero Wald statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_uStatistic_of_nondegenerate
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.8: the nondegenerate U-statistic CLT, with its first projection.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_two_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The order-two ordered-injection sum is the sum over distinct ordered pairs.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_pair_ne_left
declarations.doc: The sum of a one-coordinate term over all distinct ordered pairs.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_two_sub_eq
declarations.doc: The order-two Hoeffding decomposition is a deterministic identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_pi_pair
declarations.doc: Distinct coordinates under a finite product law have the product of their laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_integral_kernel
declarations.doc: The conditional integral of a square-integrable real kernel is square integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_hoeffding_kernel_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A centered conditional kernel has zero first-coordinate integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_pair_mul_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A centered pair kernel is orthogonal to any square-integrable function not using its first coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.insertNth_eq_of_ne
declarations.doc: Inserting a different value at one coordinate leaves every other coordinate unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_pair_mul_pair
declarations.doc: Two centered symmetric pair kernels are orthogonal unless their unordered coordinate pairs coincide.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_pair_mul_single
declarations.doc: A centered symmetric pair kernel is orthogonal to each one-coordinate function.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_sum_pairs
declarations.doc: The sum of a square-integrable kernel over distinct coordinate pairs is square integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sum_pairs_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Degenerate pair sums have mean zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_pairs
declarations.doc: The second moment of a degenerate symmetric ordered-pair sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sum_pairs_mul_sum_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A degenerate pair sum is orthogonal to the sum of any square-integrable one-coordinate function.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_hoeffding_decomposition_and_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.29: order-two Hoeffding decomposition, including the exact variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_two_finite_rank_eq
declarations.doc: The finite-rank quadratic U-statistic is a difference between squared sample sums and sample sums of squares. The identity includes sample sizes zero and one.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_uStatistic_finite_rank_of_scores
declarations.doc: A finite-rank quadratic kernel has the Gaussian-chaos limit whenever its vector of normalized scores has the standard Gaussian limit.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_uStatistic_of_finite_rank_degenerate
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.30: finite-rank degenerate quadratic kernels have Gaussian-chaos limits.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_two_of_lipschitz_envelope
declarations.doc: Square integrability of a parameter family with a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope, at parameters within the Lipschitz radius.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_le_abs_centredSum_sub_le
declarations.doc: Chebyshev's inequality for the increments of the centred partial-sum process of a parameter family with a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_centredSum_sub_le
declarations.doc: Deterministic Lipschitz bound for the increments of the centred partial-sum process.

declarations.name: CKSD.dyadicGridPoint
declarations.doc: The left endpoint of the dyadic cell of level `j`, of width `δ / 2 ^ j`, containing `t` in the grid anchored at `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.dyadicGridPoint_index_mem
declarations.doc: The dyadic cell index of a point within `δ` of the anchor lies in `[-2 ^ j, 2 ^ j)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_dyadic_sub_le
declarations.doc: A dyadic grid point lies within `δ` of the anchor, as does the midpoint of its cell.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sub_dyadicGridPoint_le
declarations.doc: A point is within one cell width of its dyadic grid point.

declarations.name: CKSD.dyadicGridPoint_succ
declarations.doc: Consecutive dyadic levels: the finer grid point is the coarser one or the midpoint of its cell.

declarations.name: CKSD.dyadicGridPoint_zero
declarations.doc: The level-zero dyadic grid point of a point within `δ` of the anchor is `θ₀ - δ` or `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_dyadic_chain_le
declarations.doc: Dyadic chaining bound: if the increments of a real process indexed by `[θ₀ - δ, θ₀ + δ]` satisfy the Chebyshev bound `P(c ≤ |S a - S b|) ≤ L (a - b)² / c²`, then for any random parameter `t` the process at the dyadic grid point of `t` of any level stays within `c` of its value at `θ₀`, except on an event of probability at most `300 L δ² / c²` or where `|t - θ₀| ≥ δ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_centredSum_sub_of_lipschitz
declarations.doc: Stochastic equicontinuity of the empirical process of a scalar parameter family with a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope: evaluated at a consistent random parameter `Tₙ`, the normalised centred partial-sum increment `n^{-1/2} ∑ᵢ (ψ_{Tₙ} - ψ_{θ₀})(Xᵢ) - √n (P ψ_{Tₙ} - P ψ_{θ₀})` tends to `0` in probability. The proof is a dyadic chaining argument with Chebyshev's inequality at each level.

declarations.name: CKSD.z_estimator_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.4, the scalar Z-estimator theorem under a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope.

declarations.name: CKSD.poissonMass
declarations.doc: Poisson likelihood as a real nonnegative mass, for a nonnegative intensity.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisAcceptance
declarations.doc: Finite-state Metropolis acceptance, with acceptance one for a zero denominator.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisTransition
declarations.doc: Finite-state Metropolis transition, including rejected proposals on the diagonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.leapfrogStep
declarations.doc: One leapfrog step with identity mass matrix and a specified force.

declarations.name: CKSD.normalPosterior
declarations.doc: Posterior of a normal location with known variance, given a proper prior density. Likelihood factors independent of the parameter cancel in this normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.bridgeIterate
declarations.doc: Alternating terminal- and initial-law entropy projections, starting from `R`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bridgeIterate_zero
declarations.doc: The reference law is the zeroth iterate.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_half_bridge
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.77: the half-bridge has the prescribed marginal, by TauCeti's entropy projection.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_half_bridge
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.77: the half-bridge attains the marginal relative entropy, by TauCeti.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_half_bridge_of_minimum_entropy
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.77: finite-entropy uniqueness of the half-bridge, by TauCeti.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_bridgeIterate_step
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.77: the entropy Pythagorean identity for each step of the path-space iteration. It holds for every feasible competitor, without assuming it minimizes entropy.

declarations.name: CKSD.probabilityFlowVelocity
declarations.doc: Velocity `-f(T-t,x) + ½ g gᵀ(T-t) ∇ log p_{T-t}(x)` of the probability flow on `[0, T)`, and `0` outside.

declarations.name: CKSD.probabilityFlow_isContinuityEquation_and_map
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.63, probability-flow part: the time-reversed marginals `qₜ = p_{T-t}` of a diffusion with positive `C¹` densities solve the continuity equation with the probability-flow velocity on every `(0, T')`, `T' < T`, and when that velocity is Lipschitz the flow started from `p_T` has law `p_{T-t}`. The forward marginals are a weak Fokker–Planck solution with a finite initial second moment; the reverse-time stochastic equation is not part of this statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.varianceExplodingLaw
declarations.doc: The law `π * N(0, tI)` of `Y + √t ξ` with `Y ∼ π` and independent standard normal `ξ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.varianceExplodingScore
declarations.doc: Score `∇ log (π * N(0, tI))(x)`, written by Tweedie's formula as the ratio `∫ (y - x)/t · e^{-‖x-y‖²/2t} π(dy) / ∫ e^{-‖x-y‖²/2t} π(dy)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpmLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the DDPM sampler after `n` steps along the times `τ`, started from `N(0, TI)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_ddpmLaw_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: relative-entropy bound for the DDPM sampler under only a finite second moment, for steps `hₙ ≤ h̄(T - τₙ)` with `h̄ ≤ 1/2`, early stopping `δ = T - τ_N`, and the accumulated score error `ε²_sc = ∑ hₙ 𝔼_{π_{T-τₙ}} ‖ŝ_{T-τₙ} - ∇ log π_{T-τₙ}‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpm_geometric_schedule
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: the geometric step schedule. With `N` least such that `(1 - h̄)ᴺ T ≤ δ`, the times `τₙ = T - (1 - h̄)ⁿ T` for `n < N` and `τ_N = T - δ` satisfy the step hypothesis, and `N ≤ 1 + h̄⁻¹ log(T/δ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpm_parameter_choice
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: the parameter choice `T = m₂²/ε²`, `h̄ = ε²/(2d(1 + log(T/δ)))` turns the bound `m₂²/(2T) + 2h̄d(1 + log(T/δ))` into `3ε²/2`, is admissible (`h̄ ≤ 1/2`), and makes the schedule bound `1 + h̄⁻¹ log(T/δ)` equal to `1 + 2dε⁻²(1 + log(T/δ)) log(T/δ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.clm_apply_gradient_eq_sum
declarations.doc: A linear functional applied to a gradient, in Euclidean coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.gradient_log_eq_inv_smul
declarations.doc: The gradient of `log m` is `∇m / m` where `m` is differentiable and nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_fderiv_gradient_add_mul_laplacian_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Integration by parts on `ℝᵈ`: `∫ (∇f · ∇m + m Δf) = 0` for compactly supported `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isFokkerPlanckSolution_add_score_of_continuityEquation
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.76: smooth positive densities solving the continuity equation with velocity `v` also solve the Fokker–Planck equation of `dX = (v + ε∇ log μ)(X) dt + √(2ε) dW`, for every continuous `ε ≥ 0`. Both equations are taken in the weak integral form on `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_marginalPreservingDiffusion
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.76, constant noise level: if the drift `bₜ = vₜ + ε∇ log μₜ` is Lipschitz uniformly in `t ∈ [0, 1]` and `∫₀¹ ∫ ‖bₜ‖ dμₜ dt < ∞`, a solution of `Xₜ = X₀ + ∫₀ᵗ bₛ(Xₛ) ds + √(2ε) Wₜ` with `X₀ ∼ μ₀` independent of the Brownian motion has law `μₜ` for every `t ∈ [0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.stochasticInterpolant_score_and_velocity
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.76: stochastic interpolants. For `Xₜ = Iₜ(X₀, X₁) + γₜ Z` with standard normal `Z` independent of the coupling, at each `t ∈ (0, 1)` the law of `Xₜ` has a smooth positive density `mₜ` with `∇ log mₜ(Xₜ) = -γₜ⁻¹ 𝔼[Z | Xₜ]`, and `t ↦ 𝔼 φ(Xₜ)` has derivative `𝔼[∇φ(Xₜ) · vₜ(Xₜ)]` for every version `vₜ(Xₜ) = 𝔼[∂ₜIₜ + γ̇ₜ Z | Xₜ]` of the velocity, which is the weak form of the continuity equation.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsDirichletProcessLaw
declarations.doc: A law on probability measures is the law of a Dirichlet process with base measure `α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_measureReal_of_isDirichletProcess
declarations.doc: The mean of a cell of a Dirichlet process is its share of the base measure. TauCeti's Dirichlet mean is applied to the two-cell partition `{A, Aᶜ}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_isDirichletProcessLaw_posterior
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.15: conjugacy of the Dirichlet process. For every version of the posterior given `n` conditionally independent observations, the posterior is a.s. a Dirichlet process with base `α + ∑ δ_{xᵢ}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_integral_posterior_eq_polyaPredictiveLaw
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.15: the Blackwell–MacQueen predictive law is the posterior mean of the random measure, granted posterior conjugacy (`ae_isDirichletProcessLaw_posterior`).

declarations.name: CKSD.isDirichletProcess_stickBreaking
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.15: Sethuraman's stick-breaking representation. With independent `Beta(1, |α|)` fractions and independent atoms of law `α / |α|`, independent of each other, every measurable random probability measure agreeing a.s. with `∑ πₖ δ_{θₖ}` is a Dirichlet process.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_langevin_generator_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.37, the scalar Langevin generator has zero Gibbs expectation on smooth tests.

declarations.name: CKSD.dist_synchronous_langevin_le_exp
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.38, pathwise synchronous exponential estimate from a common additive forcing. The monotonicity coefficient may be any real number; a positive coefficient gives contraction.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_robbins_monro
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.40, almost-sure Robbins–Monro convergence under bounded conditional noise variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropy_le_exp_of_log_sobolev
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.41, the exponential estimate from dissipation and a log-Sobolev bound. A positive coefficient gives entropy decay; the estimate also holds for real coefficients.

declarations.name: CKSD.score_matching_risk_identity
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.64, scalar score-matching identity for compactly supported fitted scores.

declarations.name: CKSD.condExp_prod_of_condExp_slices
declarations.doc: Slice conditional expectations give the conditional expectation on the product space, when the conditioning map records the time as well as the observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.wasserstein_le_barycentric_velocity_action
declarations.doc: SYNOPSIS 104.72: action bounds for the barycentric velocity of an arbitrary straight coupling.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLangevinFlow
declarations.doc: The flow of laws of the overdamped Langevin diffusion: a weak Fokker–Planck solution with drift `-gradV` and covariance `2I` on `[0, T]` for every `T ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.chiSqDiv
declarations.doc: Chi-squared divergence `∫ (dμ/dν - 1)² dν` for `μ ≪ ν`, and `∞` otherwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.poincareInequality_iff_chiSqDiv_langevin_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: the Poincaré inequality with constant `C` is equivalent to exponential decay at rate `2/C` of the chi-squared divergence along every Langevin flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.logSobolevInequality_iff_klDiv_langevin_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `C` is equivalent to exponential decay at rate `2/C` of the relative entropy along every Langevin flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.wasserstein_sq_langevin_le_of_logSobolev
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: under a logarithmic Sobolev inequality, the Otto–Villani inequality gives `W₂²(μₜ, π) ≤ 2C e^{-2t/C} KL(μ₀‖π)` along every Langevin flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_one_add_mul_log_one_add_sub_le
declarations.doc: Second-order Taylor bound for `y log y` at `y = 1`: `|(1+s) log(1+s) - s - s²/2| ≤ 4|s|³` for `|s| ≤ 1/2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_comp_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: A continuous function of a bounded continuous real function is integrable under a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_le_of_logSobolevInequality_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: A logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `C` gives the Poincaré bound with constant `C` for bounded smooth test functions: apply it to `1 + εg` and expand the entropy to second order in `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_mul_arctan_inv_mul
declarations.doc: The truncations `R arctan(s/R)`, `R = n + 1`, converge to `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.poincareInequality_of_logSobolevInequality_general
declarations.doc: A logarithmic Sobolev inequality implies the Poincaré inequality with the same constant, for every probability measure on a real normed space. Unbounded test functions are reduced to the bounded case through the truncations `R arctan(f/R)` and dominated convergence.

declarations.name: CKSD.poincareInequality_of_logSobolevInequality
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: a logarithmic Sobolev inequality implies the Poincaré inequality with the same constant, for every probability measure on `ℝᵈ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.poincare_and_logSobolev_of_bounded_perturbation
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: Bakry–Émery and Holley–Stroock. If `V = V₀ + ψ` with `∇²V₀ ⪰ mI`, `m > 0`, and `a ≤ ψ ≤ b`, then the Gibbs law satisfies the Poincaré and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constant `e^{b-a}/m`.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinLaw
declarations.doc: The underlying measure of a law in the Wasserstein space `P₂(ℝᵈ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy
declarations.doc: Free energy `∫ ρ log ρ + ∫ V dρ` on the Wasserstein space, with the entropy relative to Lebesgue measure; it is `⊤` for laws without a density.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinDensity
declarations.doc: Real Lebesgue density of the absolutely continuous part of a Wasserstein law. This represents the whole law when that law is absolutely continuous with respect to volume.

declarations.name: CKSD.jko_scheme_tendsto_fokkerPlanck
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.43: the Jordan–Kinderlehrer–Otto theorem. Every JKO step for the free energy has a unique minimizer, and the piecewise-constant interpolations converge, weakly in `L¹` at every time and strongly in `L¹((0,T) × ℝᵈ)`, to a weak solution of `∂ₜρ = Δρ + ∇·(ρ∇V)` with datum `ρ₀`. Uniqueness of the limiting weak solution is not part of this statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.seqDistSq
declarations.doc: Squared `ℓ²` distance between real sequences, possibly infinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.inverseProblemSobolevBall
declarations.doc: The Sobolev ellipsoid `S^β(R) = {f : ∑ⱼ j^{2β} fⱼ² ≤ R²}`, with `j` running from `1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inverseProblemLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the observations `Yⱼ = κⱼ fⱼ + ε Zⱼ` with independent standard normal `Zⱼ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inverseProblemRisk
declarations.doc: Mean squared `ℓ²` risk of an estimator at the truth `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSeqPosterior
declarations.doc: Posterior under the prior with independent `fⱼ ∼ N(0, j^{-1-2β})`, in conjugate form: coordinate `j` is normal with mean `λⱼκⱼYⱼ / (κⱼ²λⱼ + ε²)` and variance `λⱼε² / (κⱼ²λⱼ + ε²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasPolynomialSingularValues
declarations.doc: Polynomially decaying singular values: `c₀⁻¹ j^{-a} ≤ κⱼ ≤ c₀ j^{-a}`, `j ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.minimax_rate_inverseProblem
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.20: the minimax `ℓ²` rate `ε^r`, `r = 2β/(2β+2a+1)`, over a Sobolev ellipsoid in the sequence form of a mildly ill-posed linear inverse problem. Estimators are measurable maps of the whole observation sequence, and the constants depend only on `a`, `β`, `R`, and `c₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_ofReal_sq_add_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: Second moment of an affine function under a normal law, in `ℝ≥0∞`: `∫⁻ ((c X - d)² + s) = (cμ - d)² + c² v + s` for `X ∼ N(μ, v)` and `s ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.rpow_neg_add_mul_rpow_neg_sub_one_le
declarations.doc: Tangent-line estimate for `t ↦ t^{-m}`: `x^{-m} + m x^{-m-1} ≤ (x - 1)^{-m}` for `m > 0`, `x > 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tsum_ofReal_rpow_add_le
declarations.doc: Shifted `p`-series tail bound by telescoping: `∑_{n ≥ 1} (T + n)^{-q} ≤ T^{1-q}/(q-1)` for `T > 0`, `q > 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_lintegral_seqDistSq_gaussianSeqPosterior
declarations.doc: Expected posterior squared `ℓ²` distance from the truth in the Gaussian sequence model: the sum over coordinates of squared bias, variance of the posterior mean, and posterior variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSeqPosterior_term_le
declarations.doc: Coordinatewise bounds for the Gaussian sequence posterior with `x = ε²` and `n = j + 1`: the squared relative bias is at most `c₀² x^r n^{2β}`, the variance of the posterior mean is at most the posterior variance, and the posterior variance is at most `c₀² 2^{1+2β} (T + n)^{-(1+2β)}` with `T = x^{-1/(2β+2a+1)}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tsum_gaussianSeqPosterior_risk_le
declarations.doc: Uniform bound on the expected posterior squared distance over the Sobolev ellipsoid: at most `(c₀² R² + c₀² 2^{1+2β}/β) (ε²)^r` with `r = 2β/(2β+2a+1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_gaussianSeqPosterior_contraction
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.20: uniform posterior contraction at the minimax rate for the Gaussian prior `fⱼ ∼ N(0, j^{-1-2β})` matched to the Sobolev smoothness, for every `M_ε → ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticGenerator
declarations.doc: Generator `p·∇ₓf - (∇V(x) + γp)·∇ₚf + γΔₚf` of the kinetic Langevin diffusion.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticGibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: The invariant law `π ⊗ N(0, I)` of the kinetic Langevin diffusion.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsKineticFokkerPlanckSolution
declarations.doc: Weak form of the kinetic Fokker–Planck equation on `[0, ∞)`, tested on smooth compactly supported functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.gradX
declarations.doc: Position gradient of a function on phase space.

declarations.name: CKSD.gradP
declarations.doc: Momentum gradient of a function on phase space.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticCouplingNorm
declarations.doc: The twisted norm `|||(x,p)|||² = ‖x‖² + ‖x + 2p/γ‖²` of synchronous coupling.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticH1Energy
declarations.doc: Weighted `H¹(𝛑)` energy `‖f‖² + β⁻¹‖∇ₓf‖² + ‖∇ₚf‖²` for `β > 0`, possibly infinite. Outside this temperature domain the integrand uses the totalized real inverse and `ENNReal.ofReal`, without an energy interpretation.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_hasDensity_kineticGibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: A smooth density and its logarithmic derivative for the kinetic Gibbs measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_kineticGenerator_eq_zero_of_fderiv_density
declarations.doc: Weighted divergence form of the kinetic generator has zero integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_kineticGenerator_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: invariance of `π ⊗ N(0, I)`, in the weak form `∫ Lf d𝛑 = 0` for smooth compactly supported `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_kineticGenerator_not_symmetric
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: the kinetic Langevin diffusion is not reversible: its generator is not symmetric in `L²(𝛑)` on smooth compactly supported functions, in every positive dimension.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticCouplingNorm_synchronous_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: contraction of synchronous coupling in the twisted norm at rate `α/γ`, for `αI ⪯ ∇²V ⪯ βI` and `γ ≥ √(2β)`. The differences of two copies driven by one Brownian motion solve the noiseless integral equations given as hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_kinetic_hypocoercive_decay_of_poincare
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: `L²` hypocoercivity under a Poincaré inequality with constant `1/α` and `β`-smoothness, with friction `γ = c₀√β`. The relative density `fₜ = d𝛑ₜ/d𝛑 - 1` is assumed continuously differentiable; the constants depend only on `c₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_kinetic_entropic_hypocoercive_decay
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: entropic hypocoercivity under a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `1/α`, with friction `γ = c₀√β`. The Lyapunov functional is the relative entropy plus a positive definite twisted Fisher information of the log-density `hₜ = log(d𝛑ₜ/d𝛑)`, assumed continuously differentiable. Here the rate constant `c'` may depend on `c₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSamplingPotential
declarations.doc: Standing sampling hypotheses on a potential: twice continuously differentiable, with gradient `gradV`, the gradient `β`-Lipschitz, and `e^{-V}` integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStronglyMonotoneGradient
declarations.doc: Strong monotonicity of the gradient, equivalent to `∇²V ⪰ αI` for a `C²` potential.

declarations.name: CKSD.ulaLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the unadjusted Langevin algorithm after `n` steps of size `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.unitUniform
declarations.doc: Uniform law on `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaStepLaw
declarations.doc: One step of the `1/2`-lazy Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm acting on laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ula_iteration_complexity
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.39: iteration complexity of the unadjusted Langevin algorithm under `αI ⪯ ∇²V ⪯ βI`, both in `W₂` at the last iterate and in relative entropy for the average of the laws of iterates `N+1, …, 2N`. The initial law has a finite second moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_klDiv_ula_le_of_logSobolev
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.45: Vempala–Wibisono bound for the unadjusted Langevin algorithm under a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `1/α` and `β`-smoothness, without convexity.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_wasserstein_ula_le_of_stronglyConvex
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.45: geometric `W₂` convergence of the unadjusted Langevin algorithm, up to a bias of order `β√(dh)/α`, under `αI ⪯ ∇²V ⪯ βI` and `h ≤ c/(βκ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_mala_mixing_time_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.47: mixing-time upper bound for the `1/2`-lazy Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm from an `M`-warm start (`μ₀ ≤ Mπ`), with `Λ = log max {κ, d, M/ε, c₂}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_mala_mixing_time_ge
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.47: matching lower bound for the `1/2`-lazy Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm: in high dimension, for every step size some target of condition number `κ` and some `M`-warm start need `c₃ κ √d (max {log κ, log d})⁻³ log(c₄/ε)` steps.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBrownianEuclidean
declarations.doc: A standard Brownian motion in `ℝᵈ`: independent coordinates, each a real Brownian motion.

declarations.name: CKSD.pathOn
declarations.doc: The path of `x` on `[0, T]`, as a continuous map, or `0` if `x` is not continuous there.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWassersteinLipschitzDrift
declarations.doc: Lipschitz continuity of a drift in position and in `W₁` of the measure, on probability measures with a finite first moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDInitialAndDrivers
declarations.doc: Independent identically distributed initial states and Brownian drivers, the initial states independent of the drivers.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsParticleSystem
declarations.doc: The `N`-particle system: particles `i < N` solve `Xⁱₜ = X₀ⁱ + ∫₀ᵗ b(Xⁱₛ, μᴺₛ) ds + Wⁱₜ` with continuous paths, `μᴺₛ` the empirical measure of the first `N` particles.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution
declarations.doc: A solution of the McKean–Vlasov equation `Yₜ = ξ + ∫₀ᵗ b(Yₛ, Law(Yₛ)) ds + Bₜ` with continuous paths.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_unique_mcKeanVlasov_and_particleSystem
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.51: well-posedness. Under a Lipschitz drift, the McKean–Vlasov equation has a solution, unique up to indistinguishability among solutions with integrable marginals, and every particle system has a pathwise unique solution.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoWeakly_particle_paths
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.51: propagation of chaos. For every horizon `T` and every `k`, the joint path law on `[0, T]` of the first `k` particles converges weakly to the `k`-fold product of the McKean–Vlasov path law.

declarations.name: CKSD.interactionDrift
declarations.doc: Drift `b₀(x) + ∫ K(x, y) μ(dy)` of an interaction model.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_lintegral_sup_particle_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.56: quantitative propagation of chaos for a bounded Lipschitz interaction, by synchronous coupling with independent nonlinear copies driven by the same initial values and Brownian motions. The constant depends only on `T`, the Lipschitz constants, and `sup |K|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldV
declarations.doc: Correlation `V(θ) = 𝔼[Y φ(X, θ)]` of a feature with the response.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldU
declarations.doc: Feature kernel `U(θ, θ') = 𝔼[φ(X, θ) φ(X, θ')]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldRisk
declarations.doc: Population risk `½ 𝔼(Y - f_ρ(X))²` of the mean-field predictor `f_ρ = ∫ φ(·, θ) ρ(dθ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldVelocity
declarations.doc: Velocity `-∇_θΨ(θ; ρ) = ∇V(θ) - ∫ ∇_θU(θ, θ') ρ(dθ')` of the mean-field gradient flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldRisk_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.53: the elementary expansion `R(ρ) = ½𝔼Y² - ∫ V dρ + ½ ∫∫ U dρ dρ` for a bounded measurable feature map.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_meanField_limit
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.53: mean-field limit of two-layer network training. With bounded Lipschitz gradients of `V` and `U`, the nonlinear continuity equation `∂ₜρ = ∇·(ρ∇_θΨ(·; ρ))` has a unique narrowly continuous probability solution with datum `ρ₀`, and the empirical measures of the time-scaled gradient flow from independent `ρ₀`-distributed initial particles converge to it in `W₁`, almost surely and uniformly on bounded time intervals.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisTransition_stochastic_and_detailed_balance
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.22, finite-state Metropolis–Hastings: stochasticity, balance and invariance for positive target weights, without a normalization requirement.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_finite_markov_chain_sum
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.24, stationary finite-state Markov chain CLT with a positive transition matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.pow_nonneg_stochastic_stationary
declarations.doc: Powers of a finite stochastic matrix are nonnegative, stochastic, and keep an invariant law.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sum_pow_sub_le_of_minorization
declarations.doc: Doeblin's bound: a minorization `K x y ≥ ε π y` by the invariant law gives geometric convergence of every row of `K ^ n` to `π`, uniformly over events.

declarations.name: CKSD.independence_sampler_totalVariationDistance_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.32, uniform convergence rate of a finite independence sampler.

declarations.name: CKSD.leapfrogStep_iterate_measurePreserving_and_reversible
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.35, reversibility and volume preservation of repeated leapfrog steps.

declarations.name: CKSD.eventually_abs_metropolisTransition_pow_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.31, finite-state form of total-variation convergence of Metropolis–Hastings. The target is positive; irreducibility is taken in the sufficient form `q x y > 0` for `x ≠ y`, and aperiodicity in the sufficient form that some proposed move has acceptance below one. The convergence is uniform over events, which is total-variation convergence.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_eq_sum_measureReal
declarations.doc: The integral of a function of a random variable with finitely many values is the sum of the values weighted by their probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_comp_of_fintype
declarations.doc: A function of a random variable with finitely many values is integrable under a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_finChainPrefix
declarations.doc: The prefix `(X 0, …, X n)` of a measurable finite-state process is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_comp_succ_eq_mulVec
declarations.doc: One-step Markov property of a finite-state chain given by its path probabilities: for a function `F` of the prefix `(X 0, …, X n)`, `𝔼[F · v(X (n+1))] = 𝔼[F · (K v)(X n)]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_markovIncrement_le
declarations.doc: Second moment of the martingale `∑_{i<n} (u(X (i+1)) - (K u)(X i))` of a finite-state chain: the increments are orthogonal, so a bound `B` on them gives `𝔼[Mₙ²] ≤ n B²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sub_mulVec_eq_of_offDiag_pos
declarations.doc: Poisson equation for a finite stochastic matrix with positive off-diagonal entries and a positive invariant law `π`: every `π`-centred `g` is `u - P u` for some `u`. The solution is `u = ½ ∑ₖ Lᵏ g` for the lazy chain `L = (I + P)/2`, which converges geometrically by Doeblin's bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_avg_of_tendsto_sum_sq_div
declarations.doc: For a bounded real sequence, convergence of the centred averages along the squares `(k+1)²` implies convergence of all averages, by monotonicity of the shifted partial sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_div_sq_of_integral_sq_le
declarations.doc: If `𝔼[Sₙ²] ≤ C n`, then `Sₙ / n → 0` almost surely along the squares `n = (k+1)²`, by Chebyshev's inequality and the Borel–Cantelli lemma.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisTransition_pos_of_ne
declarations.doc: Off-diagonal entries of the Metropolis transition are positive when the target is positive and the proposal is positive off the diagonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_sampleAverage_metropolis
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.31, finite-state ergodic theorem for Metropolis–Hastings from a fixed initial state. The chain is specified by its finite-dimensional path probabilities; irreducibility is taken in the sufficient form `q x y > 0` for `x ≠ y`. On a finite space every function is `π`-integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsDirichletProcess
declarations.doc: Finite-dimensional partition characterization of a Dirichlet process. `A` partitions a set of full base mass; this includes partitions with null cells after deleting them.

declarations.name: CKSD.dirichletPosteriorBase
declarations.doc: Posterior base measure after a finite sample from a Dirichlet process.

declarations.name: CKSD.polyaPredictiveLaw
declarations.doc: Blackwell–MacQueen one-step predictive law.

declarations.name: CKSD.stickBreakingWeight
declarations.doc: Infinite stick-breaking weights in their size-biased order.

declarations.name: CKSD.stickBreakingMeasure
declarations.doc: Random atomic measure associated to a sequence of atoms and stick-breaking fractions.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPosteriorKernel
declarations.doc: A chosen posterior kernel is a disintegration of the joint parameter-data law.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPosteriorConsistent
declarations.doc: Posterior consistency at a parameter, with data given as an infinite sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_isPosteriorConsistent_of_identifiable
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.17: Doob consistency for any posterior versions based on finite prefixes. The `n`th posterior is conditioned on exactly the first `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.logLikelihoodRatioSecondMoment
declarations.doc: Second log-likelihood-ratio moment, used in posterior contraction neighborhoods.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasPosteriorContractionRate
declarations.doc: Posterior contraction at a specified deterministic rate in a metric on parameters.

declarations.name: CKSD.dirichletPosteriorBase_empty
declarations.doc: The initial empty sample leaves the Dirichlet base measure unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.stickBreakingWeight_zero
declarations.doc: Zeroth stick-breaking weight.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel
declarations.doc: Feynman–Kac model with fixed observations encoded in its potentials.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.potential_pos
declarations.doc: The positive lower potential bound implies pointwise strict positivity.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.unnormalizedLaw
declarations.doc: Unnormalized Feynman–Kac measure at generation `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.filterLaw
declarations.doc: Normalized filtering law.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.particlePredictionLaw
declarations.doc: Bootstrap prediction law from the weighted particles at the current generation.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.particleLikelihood
declarations.doc: Bootstrap-particle likelihood estimate as a product of mean potentials.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBootstrapParticleSystem
declarations.doc: Bootstrap sampling: conditional on the entire past, next particles are independent draws from the weighted prediction law. This specifies a simulation protocol rather than its limits.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.lintegral_particlePredictionLaw
declarations.doc: Integral against the bootstrap prediction law: the potential-weighted average of the transition integrals from the current particles.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.isProbabilityMeasure_particlePredictionLaw
declarations.doc: With at least one particle, the bootstrap prediction law is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_sum_comp_eval_pi
declarations.doc: For `N` independent draws from a probability law `ν`, `𝔼[∑ᵢ φ(Zᵢ)] = N ∫ φ dν`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.lintegral_unnormalizedLaw_succ
declarations.doc: One step of the unnormalized Feynman–Kac recursion `γₙ₊₁(φ) = γₙ(Gₙ Qₙ φ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_mul_sum_bootstrap_succ
declarations.doc: One resampling step of the bootstrap filter: conditionally on the first `n + 1` generations, the sum of `φ` over the next generation has mean `N` times the prediction integral of `φ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_bootstrapWeight_mul_average
declarations.doc: Unbiasedness of the bootstrap particle approximation of the unnormalized Feynman–Kac measures: `𝔼[∏_{p<n} ηᵖ(Gₚ) · ηⁿ(φ)] = γₙ(φ)` for every measurable `φ ≥ 0`, where `ηᵖ` is the empirical measure of generation `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_particleLikelihood_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.58: unbiased likelihood estimate for multinomial resampling.

declarations.name: CKSD.gibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: Gibbs law normalized by its partition integral. Use under finite positive normalizer hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.diffusionGenerator
declarations.doc: Diffusion generator in Euclidean coordinates for drift `b` and infinitesimal covariance `A`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsFokkerPlanckSolution
declarations.doc: Weak integral formulation of the Fokker–Planck equation on `[0,T]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eulerMaruyamaStep
declarations.doc: Euler–Maruyama step with an already sampled standard Gaussian increment.

declarations.name: CKSD.langevinStepLaw
declarations.doc: Unadjusted Langevin one-step law, with noise variance `2h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaAcceptance
declarations.doc: Acceptance probability of Metropolis-adjusted Langevin with proposal variance `2h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpmStep
declarations.doc: DDPM update for variance-exploding Brownian noising, using the remaining time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.unnormalizedLaw_zero
declarations.doc: Feynman–Kac normalization starts from the specified prior law.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.particleLikelihood_zero
declarations.doc: The particle likelihood of an empty observation sequence is one.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_comp_eval_sub_le
declarations.doc: For `N` independent draws from a probability law `ν` and a bounded measurable `f` with `|f| ≤ C`, the centred sum satisfies `𝔼[(∑ᵢ f(Zᵢ) - N ∫ f dν)²] ≤ N C²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.integral_particlePredictionLaw
declarations.doc: Integral of a bounded measurable function against the bootstrap prediction law: the potential-weighted average of the transition integrals from the current particles.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.unnormalizedLaw_succ_univ
declarations.doc: Total mass recursion `γₙ₊₁(1) = γₙ(Gₙ)` of the unnormalized Feynman–Kac measures.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.unnormalizedLaw_univ_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The unnormalized Feynman–Kac measures have positive total mass.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.integral_unnormalizedLaw_succ
declarations.doc: Real-valued recursion `γₙ₊₁(f) = γₙ(Gₙ Qₙ f)` for bounded measurable `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.integral_filterLaw
declarations.doc: Integrals against the filtering law are normalized integrals against `γₙ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.integral_filterLaw_succ
declarations.doc: Filtering recursion `ηₙ₊₁(f) = ηₙ(Gₙ Qₙ f) / ηₙ(Gₙ)` for bounded measurable `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_bootstrap_succ
declarations.doc: Conditional sampling step of the bootstrap filter: integrating a function of the past and the next generation equals integrating it against the product prediction law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_bootstrap_succ_sub_le
declarations.doc: Conditional variance bound for one resampling step: with `|f| ≤ C`, `𝔼[(∑ᵢ f(ξₙ₊₁ⁱ) - N Φₙ(ηᴺₙ)(f))²] ≤ N C²`, where `Φₙ(ηᴺₙ)` is the prediction law.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_div_sub_div_le
declarations.doc: Elementary ratio estimate used for the Feynman–Kac selection step: if `v, v' ≥ a > 0` and `|u'| ≤ C v'`, then `(u/v - u'/v')² ≤ 2((u-u')² + C²(v-v')²)/a²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_integral_sq_particle_average_sub_le
declarations.doc: Mean-square error bound for the bootstrap particle filter: at each fixed time `n` there is a constant `K` such that `𝔼[(ηᴺₙ(f) - ηₙ(f))²] ≤ K C² / (N + 1)` for all `N` and all measurable `f` with `|f| ≤ C`, where `N + 1` is the number of particles.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_particle_average
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.55: fixed-time consistency of the multinomial bootstrap particle filter. The proof combines the mean-square bound `exists_integral_sq_particle_average_sub_le` with Markov's inequality.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.backwardOperator
declarations.doc: Backwards Feynman–Kac operator over `m` transitions starting at time `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.particleAverageAsymptoticVariance
declarations.doc: Asymptotic variance of a normalized bootstrap particle average.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.particleLikelihoodAsymptoticVariance
declarations.doc: Asymptotic variance of the normalized likelihood estimate.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.backwardOperator_one_of_potential_eq_one
declarations.doc: With unit potentials, the backwards operator preserves the constant one function.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.particleLikelihoodAsymptoticVariance_zero
declarations.doc: At time zero the likelihood estimate is deterministic and its asymptotic variance is zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.particleLikelihoodAsymptoticVariance_eq_zero_of_potential_eq_one
declarations.doc: Unit observation potentials give zero likelihood-estimation asymptotic variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_particle_average
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.59: bootstrap-particle central limit theorem at a fixed time.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_particle_likelihood
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.59: bootstrap-particle likelihood central limit theorem at a fixed time.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_uniform_particle_moment_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.60: uniform-in-time `Lᵖ` particle error bound for a fixed mixing model. The bound is uniform in time, particle number, and test functions with oscillation at most one; no model-independent value of the constant is claimed by this formulation.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.backwardOperator_zero
declarations.doc: A zero-step backwards operator is the identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.FeynmanKacModel.particleAverageAsymptoticVariance_nonneg
declarations.doc: Each particle-average asymptotic variance is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPolyaUrnProcess
declarations.doc: Pólya urn protocol, with predictive law conditional on the first `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.distinctObservationCount
declarations.doc: Number of distinct values among the first `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.distinctObservationCount_succ
declarations.doc: The distinct count increases by one exactly when the next observation is new.

declarations.name: CKSD.polyaPredictiveLaw_compl_range
declarations.doc: For an atomless base, the Pólya predictive law gives the complement of the observed values the mass `|α| / (|α| + n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_newObservation_polya
declarations.doc: Under a Pólya urn with atomless base `α`, the `n`-th observation is new with probability `|α| / (|α| + n)`: the predictive law gives the finitely many past values the mass of their atoms only, and `α` charges no finite set.

declarations.name: CKSD.distinctObservationCount_eq_sum_indicator
declarations.doc: The distinct count is the number of indices at which a new value is observed.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_distinctObservationCount_polya
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.16: expected number of distinct observations under an atomless Pólya base.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_indicator_newObservation_polya
declarations.doc: Conditionally on the first `n` observations of a Pólya urn with atomless base, the `n`-th observation is new with probability `|α| / (|α| + n)`: for a bounded measurable function `F` of the past, `𝔼[F · 1{new}] = |α| / (|α| + n) · 𝔼[F]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_distinctObservationCount_sub_le_polya
declarations.doc: Second moment of the centred distinct count of a Pólya urn: the increments of `Kₙ - ∑_{i<n} |α|/(|α|+i)` are orthogonal Bernoulli residuals, so its second moment is at most `∑_{i<n} |α|/(|α|+i)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_div_of_summable_integral_sq_div
declarations.doc: If `∑ₖ 𝔼[Zₖ²] / bₖ² < ∞`, then `Zₖ / bₖ → 0` almost surely, by Chebyshev's inequality and the Borel–Cantelli lemma.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_div_of_monotone_of_tendsto_subseq
declarations.doc: Monotone interpolation: if `u ≥ 0` and `L` are monotone, `u / L → l` along a strictly increasing sequence `sₖ`, and `L(sₖ₊₁) / L(sₖ) → 1`, then `u / L → l`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bounds_sum_div_add_log
declarations.doc: The sums `∑_{i<n} θ/(θ+i)` are `θ log(n+1)` up to a bounded error, by comparison with the harmonic numbers.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_distinctObservationCount_div_log_polya
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.16: logarithmic almost-sure growth of the number of distinct values. The logarithm uses `n+1`, which has the same asymptotics and avoids its initial zero argument.

declarations.name: CKSD.distinctObservationCount_zero
declarations.doc: No values have been observed before the first sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.volume_highest_density_region_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.10, volume minimality of a highest-density region.

declarations.name: CKSD.normal_posterior_mean_tweedie
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.14, Tweedie's formula for normal means under an arbitrary probability prior.

declarations.name: CKSD.poisson_posterior_mean_eq_mass_ratio
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.14, the algebraic Poisson mass-ratio identity for any prior measure. For a probability prior on positive intensities with finite first moment and positive marginal mass, the left side is the posterior mean; the equality itself needs none of these restrictions.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_robbins_estimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.14, almost-sure consistency of Robbins' count-ratio estimator.

declarations.name: CKSD.bernstein_von_mises_normal_location
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.1, Bernstein–von Mises for the scalar normal location model with any proper prior density continuous and positive at the true mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_exp_neg_inner_toEuclideanCLM_div_two
declarations.doc: Gaussian integral for a positive definite matrix `H`: `∫ exp(-⟪y, H y⟫/2) dy = (2π)^{d/2} / √(det H)`, from the normalization of TauCeti's multivariate normal density with covariance `H⁻¹`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_pos_mul_norm_sq_le_inner_toEuclideanCLM
declarations.doc: Coercivity of a positive definite quadratic form: `c ‖v‖² ≤ ⟪v, H v⟫` for some `c > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_abs_sub_half_fderiv_fderiv_le
declarations.doc: Second-order Taylor estimate at a critical point: for `C²` `f` with `f m = 0` and `Df(m) = 0`, `|f(m + h) - ½ D²f(m)(h, h)| ≤ ε ‖h‖²` for all small `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_pos_mul_norm_sub_sq_le_of_isCompact
declarations.doc: On a compact set where `f` is positive off `m`, a local quadratic lower bound at `m` extends to a global one: `c ‖x - m‖² ≤ f x` on `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_laplace_approximation
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.5, deterministic Laplace core on a compact parameter region. This states the analytic approximation; the random-likelihood and BIC conclusions of the source require its additional probabilistic hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.dominatedPosterior
declarations.doc: Posterior measure obtained by multiplying a prior by the finite-sample likelihood.

declarations.name: CKSD.statisticalHellingerDistance
declarations.doc: Real Hellinger adapter in the convention `h² = integral (sqrt p - sqrt q)²` for probability measures. For arbitrary measures an infinite squared divergence is totalized to zero by `ENNReal.toReal`; distance interpretations require finite divergence.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasUniformlyConsistentTests
declarations.doc: Existence of uniformly consistent tests against a fixed parameter set.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_posterior_compl_of_kl_support
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.18: Schwartz posterior consistency for a specified measurable neighborhood. Uniformly consistent tests and positive prior mass in each KL neighborhood are explicit.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasHellingerSieveCover
declarations.doc: Finite internal Hellinger cover of a sieve, with an explicit entropy cardinality bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_posterior_hellinger_contraction
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.19: posterior contraction under the Ghosal–Ghosh–van der Vaart sieve conditions. The finite-cover condition spells out the entropy bound without imposing a metric on labels.

declarations.name: CKSD.statisticalHellingerDistance_nonneg
declarations.doc: Statistical Hellinger distance is nonnegative by its definition.

declarations.name: CKSD.statisticalHellingerDistance_self
declarations.doc: The Hellinger adapter vanishes when its two laws agree, by Statlib.

declarations.name: CKSD.statisticalHellingerDistance_comm
declarations.doc: Symmetry of the Hellinger adapter follows from Statlib's symmetry theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.dominatedPosterior_empty
declarations.doc: Before any observations, a probability prior is its own dominated posterior.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsFlowOf
declarations.doc: `Φ` is the flow of `θ' = -h(θ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsInvariantSet
declarations.doc: A set invariant under the flow for all real times, `Φₜ(A) = A`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsInternallyChainTransitive
declarations.doc: Internally chain transitive invariant set: any two points of `A` are joined by `(ε, T)`-chains of points of `A`, each flowing for time at least `T` to within `ε` of the next.

declarations.name: CKSD.limitSet
declarations.doc: Limit set of a sequence: the set of its cluster points.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_of_limitSet_eq_singleton
declarations.doc: A bounded sequence in a proper metric space converges if its limit set is a singleton.

declarations.name: CKSD.stochasticApproxTime
declarations.doc: Interpolation times `tₙ = ∑_{k<n} aₖ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.stochasticApproxInterp
declarations.doc: Piecewise-linear interpolation of the iterates, linear on each `[tₙ, tₙ₊₁]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_isInternallyChainTransitive_limitSet
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.49: Benaïm's limit-set theorem. Under Robbins–Monro steps, martingale-difference noise with conditional second moment at most `K(1 + ‖θₙ‖²)`, a Lipschitz field, and a.s. bounded iterates, the limit set is a.s. a compact connected internally chain transitive invariant set.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_equilibrium_of_chainTransitive
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.49: if the only compact connected internally chain transitive invariant sets are equilibria, the iterates converge almost surely to a possibly random equilibrium.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_asymptotic_pseudotrajectory
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.49: the interpolated process is almost surely an asymptotic pseudotrajectory of the flow, uniformly on time windows of length `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.stochasticApproxTime_zero
declarations.doc: The interpolation times start at zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.totalVariationDistance_map_le_sqrt_klDiv
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.68: endpoint total variation is at most the square root of half the path entropy.

declarations.name: CKSD.weightedDegree
declarations.doc: Weighted degree of a vertex.

declarations.name: CKSD.graphVolume
declarations.doc: Weighted volume of a set of vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.cutWeight
declarations.doc: Weight crossing a cut, counted once.

declarations.name: CKSD.cheegerConstant
declarations.doc: Conductance, with nonempty proper cuts only.

declarations.name: CKSD.spectralGap
declarations.doc: The normalized Laplacian's spectral gap, via the degree-weighted Rayleigh principle.

declarations.name: CKSD.massRadius
declarations.doc: Radius needed to capture mass `u` around `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.distanceToMeasure
declarations.doc: Distance to a measure at mass `m`.

declarations.name: CKSD.squaredMMD
declarations.doc: Squared maximum mean discrepancy as the kernel double-integral expression.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCharacteristicKernel
declarations.doc: Separation of probability laws by vanishing squared discrepancy. Symmetry, positive definiteness, measurability, and integrability of the kernel are separate properties.

declarations.name: CKSD.unbiasedSquaredMMD
declarations.doc: Unbiased empirical MMD squared for equal sample sizes.

declarations.name: CKSD.distanceKernel
declarations.doc: The distance-induced kernel with base point zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.centeredDistance
declarations.doc: Doubly centered pairwise distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSmoothing
declarations.doc: Gaussian convolution as a pushforward of independent addition.

declarations.name: CKSD.laguerreCell
declarations.doc: Laguerre cell for the squared Euclidean cost.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual
declarations.doc: Semidiscrete transport dual functional.

declarations.name: CKSD.randomFourierFeatureKernel
declarations.doc: A finite random-Fourier-feature kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.essentialBottleneckEDist
declarations.doc: Bottleneck distance between essential parts: the best bijection of essential births, and `∞` when the numbers of essential bars differ.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist
declarations.doc: Bottleneck distance between full diagrams with finite parts `D, E` and essential parts `e, e'`. Finite and essential points are at infinite distance, so the two parts are matched separately.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinCost
declarations.doc: `q`-th power cost of a partial matching of finite parts together with a bijection of essential parts, with `ℓ^∞` distances between matched points and distance `(d - b)/2` of an unmatched point to the diagonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist
declarations.doc: The `q`-Wasserstein distance between full persistence diagrams, `∞` when the numbers of essential bars differ.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.ofReal_le_cost_of_relates
declarations.doc: The cost of a matching bounds the distance of each matched pair.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.ofReal_le_cost_of_not_left
declarations.doc: The cost of a matching bounds the diagonal distance of each unmatched left point.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.ofReal_le_cost_of_not_right
declarations.doc: The cost of a matching bounds the diagonal distance of each unmatched right point.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.cost_le
declarations.doc: A bound on all matched pairs and on all unmatched points bounds the cost.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.comp
declarations.doc: The composite of two partial matchings.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.cost_comp_le
declarations.doc: The cost of a composite matching is at most the sum of the costs.

declarations.name: CKSD.bottleneckEDist_triangle
declarations.doc: The triangle inequality for the bottleneck distance of finite-death diagrams.

declarations.name: CKSD.essentialBottleneckEDist_triangle
declarations.doc: The triangle inequality for the bottleneck distance of essential parts.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_triangle
declarations.doc: The triangle inequality for the bottleneck distance of full diagrams.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_le_lt_forall_lt_iff_le
declarations.doc: Below a level `x` and above `z < x`, there is a level `y` such that the values of a finite family below `x` are exactly those at most `y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_equiv_comp_eq_of_card_filter_eq
declarations.doc: Two finite families with equal fibre cardinalities are related by a bijection.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_eq_of_card_filter_le_eq
declarations.doc: Real families with the same distribution function have the same fibre cardinalities.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_birth_death_eq_add
declarations.doc: Inclusion–exclusion for the multiplicity of a point `(x, y)` of a finite-death diagram, in terms of the counts of bars containing `[a, b]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_equiv_of_card_eq
declarations.doc: Full diagrams with the same counts of bars containing each interval `[a, b]` agree up to reindexing: the counts determine the finite and the essential parts.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_eq_zero_of_card_eq
declarations.doc: Full diagrams with the same counts of bars containing each interval `[a, b]` are at bottleneck distance zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.leftTerm
declarations.doc: The distance of a left point to its partner, or to the diagonal when it is unmatched.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.rightTerm
declarations.doc: The distance of an unmatched right point to the diagonal, and zero for a matched one.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.leftTerm_of_relates
declarations.doc: The left term of a matched point is its distance to the partner.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.leftTerm_of_not
declarations.doc: The left term of an unmatched point is its distance to the diagonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.rightTerm_of_relates
declarations.doc: The right term of a matched point is zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.rightTerm_of_not
declarations.doc: The right term of an unmatched point is its distance to the diagonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinCost_eq
declarations.doc: The `q`-Wasserstein cost as a sum of left terms, right terms, and essential terms.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_dite_exists_eq
declarations.doc: Summing a function of the partner along a partial bijection.

declarations.name: CKSD.dite_rpow_eq
declarations.doc: A power of a conditional with zero default, for a positive exponent.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinCost_comp_rpow_le
declarations.doc: The cost of a composite matching, to the power `1/q`, is at most the sum of the costs of the two matchings, to the power `1/q` (Minkowski's inequality).

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_triangle
declarations.doc: The triangle inequality for the `q`-Wasserstein distance of full diagrams, `1 ≤ q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.shiftedEntropicCost
declarations.doc: A lower-bounded real transport cost represented in TauCeti's nonnegative cost convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.realSinkhornDivergence
declarations.doc: Debiased Sinkhorn divergence of a real cost, computed after a nonnegative shift.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropicTransportCost_shiftedEntropicCost_eq_add
declarations.doc: Lowering the shift by `b - a` raises every entropic cost by `b - a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropicTransportCost_shiftedEntropicCost_ne_top
declarations.doc: Entropic costs of a bounded shifted cost between probability measures are finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.realSinkhornDivergence_independent_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.44: the debiased divergence does not depend on the chosen valid lower bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.realSinkhornDivergence_nonneg
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.44: nonnegativity of a shifted real-cost Sinkhorn divergence, using TauCeti.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_eq_add_of_iff
declarations.doc: Counting a disjoint union of two filters.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_edist_zero_rpow_two_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: The second radial moment of a Gaussian law is the squared norm of its mean plus the trace of its covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianWassersteinLaw_toProbabilityMeasure
declarations.doc: The probability measure underlying the bundled quadratic-Wasserstein Gaussian law.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_gaussianWassersteinLaw
declarations.doc: Gaussian laws depend continuously on their positive semidefinite covariance in quadratic Wasserstein distance, with the mean fixed.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_gaussian_bures_expression
declarations.doc: The Gaussian Bures expression is continuous up to singular source covariances.

declarations.name: CKSD.wasserstein_multivariateGaussian_sq_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.46: the Gaussian Bures formula, allowing both covariances to be singular.

declarations.name: CKSD.cheeger_inequalities
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.1: Cheeger's inequalities for a finite weighted connected graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_dist_sq_of_integrable_dist_sq
declarations.doc: Squared distances to any point are integrable once they are integrable for one point.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_frechet_mean_of_midpoint_inequality
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.5, existence and uniqueness in a complete space satisfying the CAT(0) midpoint inequality.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_hausdorff_sampling_error
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.7, noiseless Hausdorff sampling rate from a uniform small-ball lower bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.centeringMatrix
declarations.doc: The centering matrix `J = I - 11ᵀ/n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.centeringMatrix_mul_mul_apply
declarations.doc: Entries of a doubly centered matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sub_sq_eq
declarations.doc: Expansion of a sum of squared deviations from a fixed value.

declarations.name: CKSD.centered_identity
declarations.doc: One-coordinate form of the double-centering identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.euclideanSpace_norm_sub_sq
declarations.doc: Squared Euclidean distance in coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.posSemidef_double_centering_iff_sq_euclidean_distances
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.8, Schoenberg's Euclidean-distance criterion by double centering.

declarations.name: CKSD.extrinsic_mean_iff_nearest_expectation
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.10: squared-distance comparisons over a set are equivalent to distance comparisons with the Euclidean expectation, for any fixed candidate point. Uses TauCeti's covariance-trace decomposition of the second moment about a point.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_projected_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.10, projected empirical-mean central limit theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_squaredMMD_null_finite_features
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.61, the null limit of MMD for a bounded finite-dimensional feature map.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_squaredMMD_alternative_finite_features
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.61, alternative MMD CLT for a bounded finite-dimensional feature map.

declarations.name: CKSD.energy_distance_nonneg_eq_zero_iff_and_eq_squaredMMD
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.62: nonnegativity, separation, and the kernel form of energy distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.distance_covariance_nonneg_eq_zero_iff_and_eq_squaredMMD
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.62: distance covariance detects independence and equals four times HSIC.

declarations.name: CKSD.squaredMMD_joint_prod_eq_zero_iff_indepFun
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.63, independence criterion for a characteristic product-space kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCharacteristicKernel_iff_spectral_measure_full_support
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.68(c), characteristicness iff the symmetric spectral measure has full support.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_coord_mul_coord
declarations.doc: Products of two coordinates are integrable under a law with finite second moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_coord

declarations.name: CKSD.intrinsicEDist
declarations.doc: The intrinsic (path-length) distance of a set: the infimum of the lengths of paths from `x` to `y` that stay in `M`, `∞` when there is none.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSampleWalk
declarations.doc: A walk from `x` through the sample `S` with steps of length at most `ε`, ending at `y`; the list records the vertices after `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.walkLength
declarations.doc: Euclidean length of the walk from `x` along `l`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleGraphEDist
declarations.doc: Shortest-path distance in the `ε`-neighbourhood graph on `S` with Euclidean edge lengths, `∞` between different components. Its graph interpretation applies to endpoints in `S`; the definition also permits an ambient starting point outside `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eventually_sampleGraphEDist_intrinsicEDist_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.4, convergence of graph geodesics. Let `M = j(N) ⊂ ℝ^D` be a compact connected smooth submanifold of positive reach, and let the samples `S n ⊆ M` be `δ n`-nets of `M` in its intrinsic distance. If `ε n → 0` and `δ n / ε n → 0`, then the shortest-path distances of the `ε n`-neighbourhood graphs converge to the intrinsic distances uniformly over pairs of sample points: for every `η > 0`, eventually `|d_{G_n}(x, y) - d_M(x, y)| ≤ η` for all `x, y ∈ S n` (stated as two one-sided bounds in `ℝ≥0∞`).

declarations.name: CKSD.intrinsicEDist_eq_edist_of_lengthPreserving
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.4, flat case. Let `φ` map `M` bijectively onto a convex set `Ω ⊆ ℝ^d`, with inverse `ψ` continuous on `Ω`, and preserve the lengths of paths in `M` (an isometry for the intrinsic length structure). Then `d_M(x, y) = ‖φ x - φ y‖` on `M`. Classical multidimensional scaling of the squared intrinsic distances of a finite sample then returns the points `φ(x_i)` up to a Euclidean isometry, by the Schoenberg criterion of Section 108.8.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isColumnLow_of_ne_zero

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftPart_eq_mul

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_mul_le

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_eq_of_isMatrixReduction

declarations.name: CKSD.isColumnLow_lowerLeftPart_iff

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_eq_card_of_isReducedMatrix

declarations.name: CKSD.pairingRankCombination
declarations.doc: The alternating rank combination of the pairing lemma, in the `0`-based indexing of `Fin m`: with `D^i_j` the submatrix of rows `i, …, m-1` and columns `0, …, j`, it is `rank D^i_j - rank D^{i+1}_j + rank D^{i+1}_{j-1} - rank D^i_{j-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.pairingRankCombination_eq_ite

declarations.name: CKSD.isColumnLow_iff_pairingRankCombination_eq_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.32, the pairing lemma: for every column reduction `R = D V` of a square matrix over a field, row `i` is the low of column `j` of `R` exactly when the alternating combination of ranks of lower-left submatrices of `D` equals `1`. In particular the pairing does not depend on the reduction (`isColumnLow_iff_of_isMatrixReduction`). The statement holds for every square matrix, so it covers boundary matrices over `ℤ/2` and signed boundary matrices over any field. Indices start at `0`; the homological reading of the pairs is `persistentBettiOfMatrix_eq_card_bars`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isColumnLow_iff_of_isMatrixReduction

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_dimColumnPart_eq_card

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow.col_eq_zero

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_map_add_finrank_inf_ker
declarations.doc: Rank–nullity for the restriction of a linear map to a subspace.
