declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_filteredChains

declarations.name: CKSD.map_filteredChains_eq_range

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_filteredCycles_inf_filteredBoundaries_add

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow.exists_and_iff
declarations.doc: A statement about the low of a column can be read off at any low of that column.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isColumnLow_iff
declarations.doc: A column has a low exactly when it is nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.persistentBettiOfMatrix_eq_card
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.32, the persistent Betti numbers of a reduced filtered boundary matrix count the bars `[i, j)` with `low_R(j) = i`, `i < a ≤ b ≤ j`, and the essential bars born before `a`. The inequality `a ≤ b` is not needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.persistentBettiOfMatrix_eq_card_bars
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.32, homological meaning of the pairing (indices from `0`; the subcomplex `K_a` consists of the first `a` simplices). If `low_R(j) = i`, then `σ_j` has dimension one more than `σ_i`, adding `σ_i` raises the Betti number in its dimension (`σ_i` is positive) and adding `σ_j` lowers the Betti number one dimension below its own (`σ_j` is negative). The bars are the pairs `[i, j)` with `low_R(j) = i` and the essential intervals `[j, ∞)` for zero columns `j` that are the low of no column: for `a ≤ b` the persistent Betti number in degree `p` counts exactly the bars of degree `p` that contain `[a - 1, b - 1]`, that is, born at an index below `a` and dying at an index of at least `b`. The restatement for monotone functions on simplices, with bars `[f(σ_i), f(σ_j))`, is a relabelling and is not stated separately.

declarations.name: CKSD.unifIntegrable_of_eventually_small_tails

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCechSimplex.isRipsSimplex
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.21, the first Čech/Rips inclusion in every pseudometric space.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRipsSimplex.mono

declarations.name: CKSD.persistenceTent_nonneg

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_intervalBasis_of_isPointwiseFiniteDimensional
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.18, existence (Crawley-Boevey's theorem): every pointwise finite-dimensional persistence module over `ℝ` with coefficients in a field is a direct sum of interval modules. The finite totally ordered case is Gabriel's theorem in type `A_n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.exists_equiv_support_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.18, uniqueness: the multiset of intervals of an interval decomposition of a pointwise finite-dimensional persistence module over `ℝ` is unique, that is, any two interval bases are related by a support-preserving bijection of their index sets.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap
declarations.doc: The comparison map `U_t → V_{t+ε}` attached to a partial matching `R` of the bars of two interval bases: a bar is sent to its partner when the partner is alive at `t + ε`, and to zero otherwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_basis
declarations.doc: Value of the comparison map on a basis vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_basis_of_rel

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_basis_of_not
declarations.doc: The comparison map kills unmatched bars.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.map_basis_apply
declarations.doc: Structure maps on basis vectors of an interval basis.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_natural
declarations.doc: Naturality of the comparison maps, under the compatibility condition `h1` on supports.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_comp_barMap

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.sumRel
declarations.doc: The partial matching of the bars of two full diagrams that combines a matching of finite parts with a bijection of essential parts.

declarations.name: CKSD.interleavingEDist_le_fullBottleneckEDist
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.20, the easy half of the isometry theorem: for persistence modules with finite closed-open interval bases, the interleaving distance is at most the bottleneck distance of the diagrams. A matching of cost `ε` gives an `ε`-interleaving bar by bar.

declarations.name: CKSD.interleavingEDist_eq_fullBottleneckEDist
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.20, the isometry theorem, for persistence modules of finite type with closed-open bars: if `U` and `V` decompose into finitely many interval modules over `[b, d)` and `[b, ∞)`, their interleaving distance equals the bottleneck distance of their diagrams (both are `∞` exactly when the numbers of essential bars differ). The general `q`-tame case, with diagrams defined from rank functions and intervals with arbitrary endpoint types, is not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Incidence numbers vanish unless the first set is obtained by deleting one vertex.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_empty_left

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_simplexIncidence_mul_simplexIncidence

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_apply_simplicialBoundary

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_of_subset_of_mem

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_mem_sublevelChains

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_insert_mul_self

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_insert_ne_zero

declarations.name: CKSD.twinHomotopy
declarations.doc: The chain homotopy of a twin pair `(v, w)`: it sends a simplex `σ` containing `w` but not `v` to `± (σ ∪ {v})`, with the sign of `σ` in the boundary of `σ ∪ {v}`, and the other simplices to zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.twinHomotopy_mem_sublevelChains
declarations.doc: The twin homotopy raises the dimension by one and preserves sublevel complexes.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_apply_of_twin
declarations.doc: The boundary of a chain vanishing on the simplices that contain `w` but not `v`, evaluated at such a simplex `σ`, only sees the simplex `σ ∪ {v}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_twinHomotopy_apply
declarations.doc: The boundary of the twin homotopy restores the coefficients on simplices containing `w` but not `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_zero_of_twin
declarations.doc: A chain vanishing on the simplices containing `w` but not `v`, whose boundary vanishes on those simplices as well, vanishes on all simplices containing `w`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_eq_of_twin
declarations.doc: Removing a twin: let `v ≠ w` be vertices such that adding `v` to a simplex containing `w` gives a simplex with the same filtration value. Then deleting all simplices containing `w` does not change the persistent Betti numbers of the sublevel filtration.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_map

declarations.name: CKSD.chainMap

declarations.name: CKSD.chainMap_apply_map

declarations.name: CKSD.chainMap_apply_of_notMem

declarations.name: CKSD.chainMap_injective

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_map_eq_of_subset_map

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_chainMap

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains_map

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_map

declarations.name: CKSD.subsetComplex

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_subsetComplex

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_top_complex

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_pullback
declarations.doc: Pullback invariance: for a map `π` of vertices with an order-embedded section `s`, the sublevel filtration `σ ↦ Φ (π σ)` of the full simplex on `V` has the same persistent Betti numbers as the sublevel filtration of `Φ` on the full simplex on `X`. The vertices outside the image of `s` are twins of vertices in the image and are removed one at a time.

declarations.name: CKSD.diam_image_le_diam_image_add

declarations.name: CKSD.isMonotoneOnFaces_ripsFiltrationValue_image

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_rips_le_ghDist
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.36, for finite metric spaces: the degree-`p` persistence diagrams of the Rips filtrations of two nonempty finite metric spaces, in the diameter-`2r` parameter, are within bottleneck distance `d_GH(X, Y)`. In the maximum-edge parameter the filtration values double, and the bound becomes `2 d_GH(X, Y)`. The linear orders on the points only orient simplices. Totally bounded spaces (where `q`-tameness is needed) and the Čech variants are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_inf_add_finrank_inf_le
declarations.doc: The rank inequality behind the nonnegativity of persistence multiplicities: for `Y ≤ X` and `U ≤ V`, `dim (Y ⊓ V) + dim (X ⊓ U) ≤ dim (X ⊓ V) + dim (Y ⊓ U)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_add_finrank_inf_le
declarations.doc: For `Y ≤ X`: `dim Y + dim (X ⊓ U) ≤ dim X + dim (Y ⊓ U)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_sum_sum_add_sum_of_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Two-variable telescoping of a function vanishing at the first index `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_sigma_fin
declarations.doc: Counting the elements of a sigma type over the fibres where a predicate holds.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_fin_ite_lt_eq_sum_range
declarations.doc: A sum over `Fin n` of the indices below `k ≤ n` is a sum over `range k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_fin_ite_le_eq_sum_range
declarations.doc: A sum over `Fin n` of the indices at least `k ≤ n` is a sum over `range (n - k)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence
declarations.doc: Signed incidence number of the face `τ` in the simplex `σ`: nonzero exactly when `τ` is a nonempty codimension-one face, with sign `(-1)^k` where the deleted vertex is the `k`th vertex of `σ` in increasing order (counting from `0`).

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary
declarations.doc: The simplicial boundary on chains, which are functions on finite vertex sets. Vertices have zero boundary (no augmentation).

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMonotoneOnFaces
declarations.doc: A function on simplices is monotone along faces of `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains
declarations.doc: Chains of dimension `p` of the sublevel subcomplex `K_a = {σ ∈ K : f σ ≤ a}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelCycles
declarations.doc: Cycles of dimension `p` of `K_a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelBoundaries
declarations.doc: Boundaries of dimension `p` of `K_b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti
declarations.doc: Persistent Betti number: the rank of `H_p(K_a) → H_p(K_b)`, computed as `dim Z_p(K_a) - dim (Z_p(K_a) ∩ B_p(K_b))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentHomology
declarations.doc: The persistent homology group in degree `p`, the image of `H_p(K_a) → H_p(K_b)`, realized as `Z_p(K_a) / (Z_p(K_a) ∩ B_p(K_b))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: `(D, e)` is the degree-`p` persistence diagram of the sublevel filtration of `f`: finite bars `[D.birth i, D.death i)` and essential bars `[e k, ∞)`, such that for `a ≤ b` the persistent Betti number counts the bars containing `[a, b]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains_mono
declarations.doc: Sublevel chains grow with the level.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains_congr
declarations.doc: Sublevel chains depend only on the sublevel set.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_congr
declarations.doc: Persistent Betti numbers depend only on the two sublevel sets.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_cast
declarations.doc: The persistent Betti number as an integer difference of dimensions.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSublevelDiagram.exists_fin
declarations.doc: A sublevel diagram indexed by arbitrary finite types can be reindexed by `Fin`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isSublevelDiagram_and_values
declarations.doc: Strengthened existence of sublevel diagrams: the bars can be chosen with endpoints that are values of `f` at simplices of `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.18, finite sublevel form: persistence diagrams of monotone sublevel filtrations of finite simplicial complexes exist. This is the interval decomposition of the finite-type persistence module `a ↦ H_p(K_a)`, read through its rank invariant. The proof uses only that the chain spaces of `K_a` grow with `a`; the bars are read off from the rank function at the critical values by inclusion–exclusion.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains_congr_fun
declarations.doc: Sublevel chains of two functions agree when the sublevel sets agree on `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_congr_fun
declarations.doc: Persistent Betti numbers of two functions agree when the two pairs of sublevel sets agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_forall_le_iff_le_of_ordered
declarations.doc: If `f` is ordered by `h` on `K` (`h σ ≤ h τ → f σ ≤ f τ`), every sublevel set of `f` on `K` is a sublevel set of `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_le_forall_le_iff_le_of_ordered
declarations.doc: Two-level version of `exists_forall_le_iff_le_of_ordered`, with ordered levels.

declarations.name: CKSD.relabelDiagram
declarations.doc: The finite part of the relabelling of a diagram along simplices `sb`, `sd`: the bar `i` becomes `[f (sb i), f (sd i))`, and bars of length zero are discarded.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSublevelDiagram.relabel
declarations.doc: Relabelling: let `f` be ordered by `h` on `K`. If the bars of a diagram of `h` have endpoints `h (sb i)`, `h (sd i)` and `h (se k)` at simplices of `K`, then the relabelled bars `[f (sb i), f (sd i))` (without those of length zero) and `[f (se k), ∞)` form a diagram of `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_le_of_ordered
declarations.doc: Bottleneck stability when the two functions are ordered by a common monotone function `h`. The diagrams of `f` and `g` are both relabellings of one diagram of `h`, and matching the bars with the same label costs at most `δ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.discordantPairs
declarations.doc: Pairs of simplices of `K` ordered oppositely by `f` and `g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMonotoneOnFaces.convexComb
declarations.doc: A convex combination of functions monotone along faces is monotone along faces.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_le_of_card_discordantPairs_le
declarations.doc: Bottleneck stability for `Fin`-indexed diagrams, by strong induction on the number of discordant pairs: without discordant pairs, `f` and `g` are both ordered by `f + g`; otherwise an intermediate convex combination `m` resolves one discordant pair and has fewer discordant pairs with both `f` and `g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_le_of_isSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.19, simplicial form: for monotone functions `f, g` on the simplices of a finite simplicial complex, the degree-`p` persistence diagrams of the sublevel filtrations (finite and essential parts) are within bottleneck distance `‖f - g‖_∞ = max_{σ ∈ K} |f σ - g σ|`. The statement for tame functions on triangulable spaces, with singular homology of sublevel sets, is not formalized; for piecewise-linear functions it reduces to this case.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_map_sublevelChains_le
declarations.doc: For `h` injective on `K`, passing from the level just below `h σ` to `h σ` adds at most the simplex `σ`, and only in dimension `σ.card - 1`; so the image of the chains under any linear map grows in dimension by at most one, and not at all in other dimensions.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelCycles_mono
declarations.doc: Sublevel cycles grow with the level.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelBoundaries_mono
declarations.doc: Boundaries grow with the level.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_birth_add_card_essential_le
declarations.doc: For `h` injective on `K`, a diagram of `h` in degree `p` has at most one bar (finite or essential) born at `h σ`, and none unless `σ` is a `p`-simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_death_le
declarations.doc: For `h` injective on `K`, a diagram of `h` in degree `p` has at most one finite bar dying at `h σ`, and none unless `σ` is a `(p + 1)`-simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_eq_zero_of_equiv
declarations.doc: Diagrams related by bijections preserving all points are at `q`-Wasserstein distance zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_eq_zero_of_isSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: Diagrams of the same function are at `q`-Wasserstein distance zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_le_of_ordered
declarations.doc: `q`-Wasserstein stability when the two functions are ordered by a common function `h` that is injective on `K`. The bars of the diagram of `h` have distinct endpoint simplices, and matching the relabelled bars with the same label costs at most `∑_{σ ∈ K} |f σ - g σ|^q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_injective_ordered
declarations.doc: Every function on simplices is ordered by a function injective on `K`: break ties by an enumeration of the simplices and take ranks.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_le_of_card_discordantPairs_le
declarations.doc: `q`-Wasserstein stability for `Fin`-indexed diagrams, by strong induction on the number of discordant pairs, as for the bottleneck distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_le_of_isSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.35, the finite-complex clause: for monotone functions `f, g` on the simplices of a finite simplicial complex `K` and `1 ≤ q < ∞`, the `q`-Wasserstein distance between the full degree-`p` diagrams is at most `(∑_{σ ∈ K} |f σ - g σ|^q)^{1/q}`. The clauses for tame Lipschitz functions on triangulable spaces with polynomially growing triangulations are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullSimplexComplex
declarations.doc: The full simplex on a finite vertex type: all nonempty vertex sets.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripsFiltrationValue
declarations.doc: The Rips filtration value of a simplex in the diameter-`2r` convention: `σ ∈ Rips(r)` exactly when `diam σ ≤ 2r`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMonotoneOnFaces_ripsFiltrationValue
declarations.doc: Diameters are monotone, so the Rips filtration is a monotone filtration of the full simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadraticEntropicCost
declarations.doc: Squared Euclidean cost in TauCeti's nonnegative extended-real convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadraticEntropicTransport
declarations.doc: Real entropic quadratic transport cost, used where the bounded-support cost is finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropicBarycentricMap
declarations.doc: Barycentric projection of a quadratic Gibbs coupling represented by a target dual potential. The denominator is explicit; applications supply a positive finite normalization integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadraticEntropicTransport_empirical_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.55: dimension-free mean-square and bias bounds for empirical entropic costs. The entropic-map estimation bound is not asserted here. Constants may depend on `ε` only.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinBarycenterEnergy
declarations.doc: Equal-weight Wasserstein barycenter energy, with the factor `1/2` normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinBarycenterGradient
declarations.doc: Candidate barycenter gradient represented by residual optimal transport maps.

declarations.name: CKSD.SatisfiesWassersteinKarcherEquation
declarations.doc: Karcher equation for a specified collection of optimal transport maps.

declarations.name: CKSD.displacementLaw
declarations.doc: Displacing a law by the vector field `v` for time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_wassersteinBarycenterEnergy_displacement
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.58, directional first variation of the equal-weight barycenter energy. The source is absolutely continuous, and each supplied map is optimal with its stated target.

declarations.name: CKSD.satisfiesWassersteinKarcherEquation_of_minimizer
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.58: a minimizing barycenter with the supplied optimal maps satisfies the Karcher equation.

declarations.name: CKSD.satisfiesWassersteinKarcherEquation_iff
declarations.doc: The Karcher equation says exactly that the average optimal map is the identity almost surely.

declarations.name: CKSD.mixedKernelDivergence
declarations.doc: The mixed divergence `⟨∇_x, ∇_y⟩ k(x, y) = ∑_j ∂_{x_j} ∂_{y_j} k(x, y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.langevinSteinKernel
declarations.doc: The Langevin Stein kernel of a score `b` and a kernel `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.kernelSteinDiscrepancySq
declarations.doc: Squared kernel Stein discrepancy of `μ`, in closed form.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsDistantlyDissipative
declarations.doc: Distant dissipativity of a score: `⟨b x - b y, x - y⟩ ≤ -κ ‖x - y‖²` once `‖x - y‖ ≥ R`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inverseMultiquadricKernel
declarations.doc: The inverse multiquadric kernel `(c² + ‖x - y‖²)^β`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoWeakly_of_kernelSteinDiscrepancySq_inverseMultiquadric_tendsto_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.72(b): let `P` have a positive continuously differentiable density `p` with score `b = ∇ log p` that is Lipschitz and distantly dissipative. For the inverse multiquadric kernel with `c > 0` and `β ∈ (-1, 0)`, every sequence of laws with square-integrable score whose kernel Stein discrepancy tends to zero converges weakly to `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_not_tendstoWeakly_of_kernelSteinDiscrepancySq_tendsto_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.72(d): for `d ≥ 3` and the standard Gaussian target (score `b x = -x`), let `k` be a `C²` kernel which, together with `∇_x k`, `∇_y k` and `⟨∇_x, ∇_y⟩ k`, is bounded, and whose decay function `γ(r)` (the supremum of `|k|`, `‖∇_x k‖` and `|⟨∇_x, ∇_y⟩ k|` over `‖x - y‖ ≥ r`) is `o(r^{-α})` with `α = (1/2 - 1/d)⁻¹`. Then some sequence of laws with finite second moments has kernel Stein discrepancy tending to zero without converging weakly to the standard Gaussian. This covers the Gaussian, Matérn and Wendland kernels. The `C²` hypothesis strengthens the source's continuity requirement on the listed derivatives. Clauses (a) and (c) are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.singularHomologyModule
declarations.doc: Degree-`n` singular homology of a topological space with coefficients in `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelSetFunctor
declarations.doc: The filtration of a space by the sublevel sets `{f ≤ t}` of a real function, as a functor from `ℝ` to topological spaces.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelHomologyModule
declarations.doc: The sublevel persistence module `t ↦ H_n({f ≤ t}; k)` of a real function.

declarations.name: CKSD.reach
declarations.doc: The reach of a set: the supremum of the radii `r` such that every point at distance less than `r` from the set has a unique nearest point in it.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsDistanceCriticalPoint
declarations.doc: A point outside `K` is critical for the distance function to `K` when it lies in the convex hull of its nearest points in `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.weakFeatureSize
declarations.doc: The weak feature size: the infimum of the positive critical values of the distance function, `∞` when there are none.

declarations.name: CKSD.offsetInclusion
declarations.doc: Inclusion of offsets of a set.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_deformationRetraction_offset_of_hausdorffDist_lt
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.22, deformation retraction of offsets. Let `M = j(N) ⊂ ℝ^D` be a compact smooth `d`-dimensional submanifold without boundary with reach at least `τ > 0`, and `P ⊆ M` finite and nonempty with `d_H(P, M) = ε < √(3/20) τ`. For `r ∈ (2ε, √(3/5) τ)` the offset `P^r` contains `M` and strongly deformation retracts onto it. By the nerve theorem the Čech complex of radius `r` then has the homotopy type of `M`; the nerve theorem is not part of this statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sample_size_hausdorffDist_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.22, the sampling bound. Let `M = j(N) ⊂ ℝ^D` be a compact smooth `d`-dimensional submanifold without boundary and `c > 0`. There are `C, ε₀ > 0` such that for every law `μ` concentrated on `M` with density at least `c` with respect to the `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure on `M` (the Riemannian volume), all `ε ∈ (0, ε₀)`, `δ ∈ (0, 1)` and `n ≥ C ε^{-d} (log(1/ε) + log(1/δ))`, an independent sample of size `n` is `ε`-close to `M` in Hausdorff distance with probability at least `1 - δ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nonempty_range_offsetHomology_equiv_of_weakFeatureSize
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.37, offsets: let `K ⊂ ℝ^D` be compact and nonempty with weak feature size at least `τ > 0`, and `P` finite and nonempty with `d_H(K, P) = ε < τ/4`. If `ε < i` and `i + 2ε ≤ j < τ - ε`, the image of `H_n(P^i) → H_n(P^j)` is isomorphic to `H_n(K^r)` for every `r ∈ (0, τ)`, in every degree `n` and over every field. Taking `τ = wfs(K)` when it is finite gives the source statement. The Čech-complex form follows by the nerve theorem and is not stated separately.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleRipsFiltrationValue
declarations.doc: The Rips filtration of a finite indexed sample, in the diameter-`2r` convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.nonempty_ripsPersistentHomology_equiv_of_weakFeatureSize
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.37, Rips complexes: let `K ⊂ ℝ^D` be compact and nonempty with weak feature size at least `τ > 0`, and `x` a finite sample with `d_H(K, {x_i}) < ε` for some `ε < τ/9`. If `2ε ≤ α ≤ (τ - ε)/4`, the image of `H_n(Rips(α/2)) → H_n(Rips(2α))` (diameter-`2r` parameter, simplicial homology over a field) is isomorphic to `H_n(K^r)` for every `r ∈ (0, τ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.manifoldCriticalPoints
declarations.doc: Critical points of a real function on a manifold modeled on `ℝ^m`: the points where the manifold derivative vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.manifoldCriticalCount
declarations.doc: The number of critical points of Morse index `q`, in `ℕ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelHomologyModule_bars_of_isMorse
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.34, diagrams of the sublevel persistence of a Morse function. Let `f` be a Morse function with distinct critical values on a closed smooth `m`-manifold and `k` a field, and for each degree `q` let `B q` be an interval decomposition of `t ↦ H_q({f ≤ t}; k)` into finitely many closed-open bars, finite ones `[(D q).birth i, (D q).death i)` and essential ones `[e q i, ∞)`. Then every endpoint is a critical value; the number `c_q` of index-`q` critical points is the number of degree-`q` bars plus the number of finite degree-`(q-1)` bars; there are exactly `β_q(M)` essential degree-`q` bars; and each critical value is an endpoint of exactly one bar. The homotopy-theoretic description (cell attachment at critical values) is not restated.

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_convexHull_farthest_of_isMin
declarations.doc: At a point `c` minimizing the largest squared distance to a nonempty finite set `S`, the point `c` lies in the convex hull of the farthest points of `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_dist_le_sqrt_two_mul_of_dist_le
declarations.doc: A finite set of diameter at most `2r` in a finite-dimensional real inner product space lies in a closed ball of radius `√2 r`, centered at a point minimizing the largest distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.cech_rips_inclusions
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.21, the Euclidean Čech/Rips inclusions, in the diameter-`2r` convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_distanceToMeasure_sub_le_wasserstein
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.24: stability of distance to a measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_empirical_wasserstein_rpow_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.40, all three bounded-support regimes on a unit ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_mem_support_preimage_of_support_eq_univ
declarations.doc: A continuous map from a compact space onto a law with full support takes the support of the source law onto the target space.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_measure_preserving_isometryEquiv_of_zero_distortion
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.43, the upgrade from a zero-distortion coupling to an isometry. The full-support assumption realizes the source's restriction to the supports.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_unique_gaussian_wasserstein_barycenter
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.46: the covariance equation and unique Gaussian barycenter of finitely many laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.wasserstein_uniform_cube_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.50, quantization lower bound for the uniform unit cube.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_wasserstein_gaussianSmoothing_empiricalMeasure_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.51, the parametric rate of Gaussian-smoothed empirical W1 on a bounded cube.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual_concave_differentiable_and_attains_max
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56: smooth semidiscrete dual, cell-mass equations and dual attainment.

declarations.name: CKSD.commute_cfcSqrt_right
declarations.doc: A matrix commuting with `B` commutes with its square root `CFC.sqrt B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_optimal_maps_compatible_iff_covariances_commute
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.57, the covariance-commutation criterion for compatibility with the standard Gaussian.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_two_map_toReal_sq_le
declarations.doc: The squared `2`-Wasserstein distance between the laws of `S` and `T` under `P` is at most the mean squared distance `∫ ‖S x - T x‖² dP`, by the coupling `(S, T)_# P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_norm_sub_smul_sub_sq
declarations.doc: Pointwise form of the descent identity: with `g = x - k⁻¹ ∑ Tᵢ`, moving `x` by `-τ g` changes the sum of squared distances to the `Tᵢ` by `-k (2τ - τ²) ‖g‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.wasserstein_energy_descent_of_averaged_transport
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.59, the energy-descent inequality for the averaged-transport update. The finite-step inequality holds for every real step size; the usual descent interpretation uses step sizes in `[0, 1]`. No convergence of the iteration is asserted.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_mul_wasserstein_sq_empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.47: let `μ` be concentrated on `[a, b]` with a density `f` continuous on `[a, b]` and bounded there between positive constants. For an i.i.d. sample of law `μ`, `n W₂²(μ_n, μ)` converges in distribution to `∫₀¹ B⁰(u)² / f(F⁻¹(u))² du`, where `B⁰(u) = W(u) - u W(1)` is the Brownian bridge built from any Brownian motion `W`; consequently `√n W₂(μ_n, μ)` is bounded in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.ballLegendreConjugate
declarations.doc: Legendre conjugate of a potential, with the supremum over the closed unit ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidualFunctional
declarations.doc: Semidual functional `∫ φ dμ + ∫ φ* dν`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ballSupCoveringNumber
declarations.doc: Covering number of a class of potentials in the supremum norm over the closed unit ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRegularPotentialClass
declarations.doc: Regularity class for transport-map estimation (Section 108.53): potentials bounded by `B` on the closed unit ball, ambient twice continuously differentiable at each point of that ball, with `½ I ≤ ∇²φ ≤ 2 I` there, and with sup-norm metric entropy `log N(ε, Φ) ≤ A ε^{-γ} log(1 + 1/ε)` for `0 < ε ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSemidualEstimator
declarations.doc: A semidual estimator: a map from paired samples to potentials in `Φ` minimizing the empirical semidual functional.

declarations.name: CKSD.transportMapRisk
declarations.doc: Squared `L²(μ)` error of the estimated transport map `∇φ̂`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_transportMapRisk_semidualEstimator_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.53, the parametric-rate bound for semidual estimators. Let `μ` be carried by a closed ball of radius `r ∈ [0, 1)` and `ν` by the closed unit ball, with `ν = (∇φ₀)_# μ` for `φ₀ ∈ Φ`. The regular class `Φ` has entropy exponent `γ ∈ [0, 1)`. Every semidual estimator from `n` independent pairs satisfies `E ‖∇φ̂ - ∇φ₀‖²_{L²(μ)} ≤ K n^{-1/2}`, where `K` is independent of `n` and may depend on `r`. The expectation is the lower Lebesgue integral of the measurable risk.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_transportMapRisk_semidualEstimator_le_of_poincare
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.53, the fast rate: if moreover `Φ` is convex and `μ` satisfies the Poincaré inequality `Var_μ(h) ≤ C_P ∫ ‖∇h‖² dμ` for continuously differentiable `h`, the risk of every semidual estimator is at most `K (log n / n)^{2/(2+γ)}`. The source is carried by a closed ball of radius `r ∈ [0, 1)`; the constant may depend on this interior margin. The minimax rate for Hölder maps and its wavelet estimator are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoWeakly
declarations.doc: Weak convergence of finite measures, tested against bounded continuous functions. Finiteness is part of the predicate, so totalized Bochner integrals cannot identify an infinite-mass law with the zero measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoWeakly.of_forall_integral_tendsto
declarations.doc: For finite measures, convergence of the bounded continuous integrals gives weak convergence.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoWeakly.iff_forall_integral_tendsto
declarations.doc: On finite measures, weak convergence is equivalent to convergence of test integrals.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoInDistribution
declarations.doc: Convergence in law of a sequence of random variables on one probability space.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoInProbabilityConst
declarations.doc: Convergence in probability to a constant; applications assume a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBoundedInProbability
declarations.doc: Uniform tightness in probability of a real sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: The empirical measure; the empty sample gives the zero measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleAverage
declarations.doc: The empirical average of the first `n` observations of a sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIndependentIdenticallyDistributed
declarations.doc: A measurable independent sequence with common law `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cdf
declarations.doc: The distribution function of a finite measure on the line.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity
declarations.doc: A real density, with measurability and nonnegativity made explicit.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance
declarations.doc: Centered second moment, used only with the stated second-moment hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.covariance
declarations.doc: Mathlib covariance with the measure-first statistical adapter used in this project.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest
declarations.doc: A real-valued randomized test.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUnbiasedEstimator
declarations.doc: Unbiasedness includes integrability under every parameter law.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSufficientStatistic
declarations.doc: Sufficiency: a single Markov kernel disintegrates every joint law of `(T,X)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCompleteStatistic
declarations.doc: Completeness of the family of laws of a statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBoundedlyCompleteStatistic
declarations.doc: Bounded completeness, with a global bound on the test function.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUniformlyMostPowerfulTest
declarations.doc: The level and power comparison defining a uniformly most powerful test.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest
declarations.doc: The uniformly most powerful unbiased property.

declarations.name: CKSD.RandomizedDecisionRule
declarations.doc: A randomized decision rule, using Mathlib's Markov kernels.

declarations.name: CKSD.risk
declarations.doc: Real risk, used below only for integrable or bounded losses.

declarations.name: CKSD.splitLogPartition
declarations.doc: Log partition function of a natural exponential family whose natural statistic is the pair `(T, S)`, with natural parameter `(η, ζ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.splitExponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: The natural exponential law with density `exp(η·T + ζ·S - A(η, ζ))` with respect to the base measure `ν`; it is a probability measure on the natural parameter space when `ν ≠ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.conditionalExponentialKernel
declarations.doc: The exponential tilt of a family of measures `ν_s` by the parameter `η`, normalized in each fibre: the kernel `s ↦ exp(η·t - A_s(η)) ν_s(dt)` with `A_s(η) = log ∫ exp(η·t) ν_s(dt)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.withDensity_exp_compProd_eq_fst_compProd
declarations.doc: Exponential tilting of a composition product. If `μ` is a finite measure and `κ` a Markov kernel, and the tilt of `μ ⊗ₘ κ` by `exp (a t + b s)` is finite, then this tilt is its first marginal composed with the fibrewise normalized tilt `s ↦ exp (a t - log ∫ exp (a t') κ s) κ s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.conditionalExponentialKernel_withDensity_exp_neg
declarations.doc: Tilting a kernel by `exp (-η₁ · t)` and then forming the conditional exponential kernel at `η` is the conditional exponential kernel of the untilted kernel at `η - η₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isFiniteMeasure_splitExponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: The split exponential law has finite total mass where its density is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.splitExponentialFamilyMeasure_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: Two split exponential laws differ by an exponential tilt in `(S, T)`; here `c` is the difference of the two log partition functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_kernel_conditional_exponential_family
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.43: conditional exponential families. For a natural exponential family with natural statistic `(T, S)` with values in Euclidean spaces, there is one s-finite kernel `s ↦ ν_s`, free of the parameter, such that at every natural parameter `(η, ζ)` the joint law of `(S, T)` is the law of `S` composed with the kernel `s ↦ exp(η·t - A_s(η)) ν_s(dt)`; that is, the conditional law of `T` given `S = s` has this density for almost every `s`, and it is free of `ζ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMinimalSplitStatistic
declarations.doc: Minimality of a split natural statistic `(T, S)` with real `T`: no nontrivial affine function `a T + b·S` is almost everywhere constant under the base measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest_conditional_two_sided
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.46, two-sided part: conditional tests with a nuisance parameter. In a minimal exponential family with real natural statistic `T`, nuisance statistic `S`, and natural parameter `(η, ζ)` ranging over an open convex set `U` on which the family is defined and which meets the hyperplane `η = η₀`, a test that rejects for values of `T` outside the conditional interval `[c₁(S), c₂(S)]`, accepts inside it, and has conditional size `α` and conditional first-moment constraint `E[Tφ | S] = α E[T | S]` at one point of the hyperplane, is UMPU of level `α` for `η = η₀` against `η ≠ η₀`. The randomization at the conditional critical points is unrestricted.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest_conditional_one_sided
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.46, one-sided part: in the setting of `isUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest_conditional_two_sided`, a test that rejects for `T > c(S)`, accepts for `T < c(S)`, and has conditional size `α` at one point of the hyperplane `η = η₀` is UMPU of level `α` for `η ≤ η₀` against `η > η₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_statistical_game_saddle_point
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.32: finite statistical games have a saddle point in rules and priors.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_admissible_bayes_risk_le_of_closed_convex
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.37, the closed-convex-risk-set form of the finite complete-class theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_equivariant_rule_risk_eq_average
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.39, the compact-group averaging theorem for a finite group with its uniform Haar measure and a bounded loss. The minimax consequences are not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_analytic_inverse_exponential_family_mean
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.42, the mean diffeomorphism in a minimal regular family. An analytic inverse is stated on the open convex-support interior.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_withDensity_comp
declarations.doc: Pushing forward a measure with a density that factors through `φ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.integral_eq
declarations.doc: Integrals against a law with a density are density-weighted integrals.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.integrable
declarations.doc: The density of a finite law is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_rao_blackwell_estimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.7: one parameter-independent Rao–Blackwell rule, with convex risk reduction at each parameter value, so the loss may depend on the parameter. The rule is `s ↦ ∫ δ dK(s)` for the kernel `K` witnessing sufficiency.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_of_isCompleteStatistic_of_isUnbiasedEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.8, uniqueness part: unbiased functions of a complete statistic agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_of_isSufficientStatistic_of_isBoundedlyCompleteStatistic
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.9: Basu's theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_div_information_le_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.10, scalar score-moment form of the information inequality. The derivative-under-integral assumptions give the displayed cross-moment identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.is_minimum_variance_unbiased_iff_covariance_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.12: covariance characterization of uniformly minimum variance unbiasedness.

declarations.name: CKSD.isSufficientStatistic_iff_exists_factorization
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.1: factorization on a standard Borel sample space and an arbitrary measurable statistic space.

declarations.name: CKSD.convex_laplace_integrability_domain
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.4, convexity part: the Laplace-integrability domain in a real inner-product space is convex.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCompleteStatistic_exponential_family
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.5: completeness of a natural statistic over a nonempty open parameter set.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihood_ratio_statistic_minimal_sufficient
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.2, minimal likelihood-ratio statistic for a countable parameter family.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_exponential_family_of_monotone_sufficient_statistics
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.6: the monotone Pitman–Koopman–Darmois characterization.

declarations.name: CKSD.analyticOnNhd_cumulant_and_fderiv_eq_moments
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.4, multivariate analyticity and first/second cumulant derivatives.

declarations.name: CKSD.mixtureWeight
declarations.doc: The weights `2^{-(n+1)}` used for countable mixtures.

declarations.name: CKSD.mixtureWeight_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The mixture weights are nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.tsum_mixtureWeight
declarations.doc: The mixture weights sum to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture
declarations.doc: The countable mixture `∑ 2^{-(n+1)} P (θs n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture_univ
declarations.doc: A countable mixture of probability measures has total mass one.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture_apply_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A measurable set is null for a countable mixture iff it is null for every component.

declarations.name: CKSD.absolutelyContinuous_countableMixture
declarations.doc: Each component of a countable mixture is absolutely continuous with respect to it.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_absolutelyContinuous_countableMixture
declarations.doc: Halmos–Savage lemma, density form: a family of laws with densities with respect to a σ-finite measure is dominated by one of its countable mixtures.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture_map_prodMk_eq_compProd
declarations.doc: A countable mixture of laws sharing a disintegrating kernel is disintegrated by that kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: The density of a countable mixture with respect to a dominating measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_prodMk_eq_compProd_of_withDensity_comp
declarations.doc: If `P = L.withDensity (r ∘ T)` and the joint law of `(T, X)` under `L` is disintegrated by `K`, then the joint law under `P` is also disintegrated by `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_withDensity_rnDeriv_comp_of_compProd
declarations.doc: If two finite laws `P ≪ L` have joint laws of `(T, X)` disintegrated by the same kernel, then `P` has a density with respect to `L` that is a function of `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_factorization_of_isSufficientStatistic
declarations.doc: Sufficiency implies a factorization of the densities (necessity half of GAPS 101.1).

declarations.name: CKSD.isSufficientStatistic_of_factorization
declarations.doc: A factorization of the densities implies sufficiency (sufficiency half of GAPS 101.1). The common kernel is the conditional distribution of the sample given `T` under a dominating countable mixture of the family.

declarations.name: CKSD.RealExponentialFamily
declarations.doc: A regular scalar natural exponential family on an open convex parameter domain.

declarations.name: CKSD.RealExponentialFamily.cumulant
declarations.doc: Log normalizer of a scalar exponential family.

declarations.name: CKSD.RealExponentialFamily.law
declarations.doc: The family law at a natural parameter.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSymmetricStatistic
declarations.doc: A statistic on a finite sample is symmetric under all coordinate permutations.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSymmetricallyComplete
declarations.doc: Completeness restricted to the symmetric sample statistics.

declarations.name: CKSD.isSymmetricallyComplete_of_complete_convex_family
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.13: completeness of permutation-invariant statistics in a convex complete model.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_orderStatistics_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.21: joint order-statistic density for an absolutely continuous law. The proof combines TauCeti's chamber formula `TauCeti.Probability.map_orderStatistics_pi` with TauCeti's product-density identity `TauCeti.pi_withDensity`.

declarations.name: CKSD.betaMeasure_nat_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: On the unit interval the beta density with integer shapes `j + 1` and `n - j` is the polynomial `n! / (j! (n - j - 1)!) u ^ j (1 - u) ^ (n - j - 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_orderStatistic_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.21: the marginal density of the zero-indexed `j`th order statistic. The proof compares distribution functions: TauCeti's `TauCeti.Probability.cdf_map_orderStatistic_pi_eq_regularizedIncompleteBeta` and `TauCeti.Probability.cdf_betaMeasure_eq` give the beta law of `F(X₍ⱼ₎)`, and TauCeti's probability integral transform `MeasureTheory.Measure.cdf_map_eq_volume_restrict` moves the beta density back along `F`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_setOf_sort_eq
declarations.doc: The set of samples with a prescribed sorting permutation is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.sorting_permutation_uniform_and_indep
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.21: ranks are uniform and independent of the sorted atomless sample. The proof refines the chamber decomposition of TauCeti's `TauCeti.Probability.map_orderStatistics_pi`: ties are null (`TauCeti.Probability.ae_eval_ne_eval_infinitePi`), and coordinate permutations preserve the product law and the order statistics (`TauCeti.orderStatistic_comp_perm`).

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLocationEquivariant
declarations.doc: Location-equivariance of a real estimator on a finite sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanEstimator
declarations.doc: The Pitman location estimator, using an improper Lebesgue prior.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_eq_lintegral_indicator_mul_lintegral_sub_const
declarations.doc: Orbit decomposition of Lebesgue integrals on `Fin n → ℝ` along the diagonal direction: the integral of `H` is the integral over `z`, weighted by the indicator of `z i₀ ∈ [0, 1]`, of the integral of `H` along the line `u ↦ z - u • 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_ofReal_sq_sub_mul_le
declarations.doc: Minimization of a weighted quadratic: for an integrable weight `w ≥ 0` with integrable first moment and positive mass, the weighted second moment `∫ (c - u)² w(u) du` is minimal at the weighted mean `c = ∫ u w / ∫ w`.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanGoodSet
declarations.doc: The samples at which the Pitman estimator is well defined: the normalizing and first-moment integrals exist and the normalizing integral is positive.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_prod_sub
declarations.doc: Joint measurability of the location likelihood `(x, u) ↦ ∏ f (x i - u)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_pitmanEstimator
declarations.doc: The Pitman estimator is measurable for a measurable density.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_pitmanGoodSet
declarations.doc: The Pitman good set is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.sub_const_mem_pitmanGoodSet
declarations.doc: The Pitman good set is invariant under diagonal translations.

declarations.name: CKSD.sub_const_mem_pitmanGoodSet_iff
declarations.doc: Membership in the Pitman good set is invariant under diagonal translations.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanEstimator_sub_const
declarations.doc: On the good set, the Pitman estimator is location-equivariant.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanEstimator_minimum_equivariant_risk_of_nonneg
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.40 for a nonnegative density: on the good set the Pitman estimator minimizes the equivariant squared-error risk.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanEstimator_minimum_equivariant_risk
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.40: the Pitman estimator minimizes equivariant squared-error risk. The normalizing and first-moment integrals are assumed to exist almost surely explicitly.

declarations.name: CKSD.intervalTest
declarations.doc: Interval-rejection test with arbitrary randomization at the endpoints.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ump_interval_test
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.50: the UMP test for the complement of an interval in a scalar exponential family.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_one_sided_test_risk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.53: essentially complete one-sided tests in the mutually equivalent, positive-density case. The threshold test matches the size of `φ` at `θ₀` (via TauCeti's quantile, `exists_threshold_test_integral_eq`); the two Neyman–Pearson steps of the Karlin–Rubin argument then compare powers below and above `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.most_powerful_of_mixture_null
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.54: a level-valid mixture-optimal test is most powerful of level `α` for the composite null. The least-favorability and concentration statements are not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.mean_scale_ratio_eq_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.56: ratio is maximal invariant on the reduced mean/positive-scale space.

declarations.name: CKSD.isAdmissibleRisk_of_blyth
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.58: Blyth's admissibility criterion in a class with continuous risks.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMoreInformative
declarations.doc: Finite-decision risk comparison, the decision side of Blackwell's theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMoreInformative_iff_isGarbling
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.62: Blackwell's comparison theorem for finite parameter, dominated experiments.

declarations.name: CKSD.james_stein_risk_eq_and_lt
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.57, strict James–Stein improvement in dimension at least three.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussianPDFReal_smul_one
declarations.doc: The isotropic Gaussian density `N(θ, v I)` in closed form: its value at `θ` times `exp (-‖x - θ‖² / (2v))`. Stated for TauCeti's `multivariateGaussianPDFReal`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_integration_by_parts
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.64: Gaussian integration by parts, in the continuously differentiable scope. The proof writes the law as a density against Lebesgue measure (TauCeti's `multivariateGaussian_eq_withDensity`) and applies Mathlib's `integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_exponential_family_mle_iff_mem_interior_convex_support
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.69: existence and uniqueness of a regular natural-exponential-family maximum. The domain is the full Laplace-integrability domain, not an arbitrary open subset of it. The criterion is the per-observation log likelihood.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponential_family_mle_unique_and_mean_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.69: a natural-family maximizer is unique and solves the mean equation.

declarations.name: CKSD.scheffe_contrast_supremum
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.60: the simultaneous-contrast supremum underlying Scheffé's method. This is the geometric identity; its Gaussian pivot uses the projection sampling laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_le_of_generalized_neyman_pearson
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.47: generalized Neyman–Pearson comparison, with signed multipliers.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_mul_exp_le_of_abs_sub_lt
declarations.doc: On `|η - η₀| < ε`, the derivative factor `|t| e^{η t}` is dominated by the two exponentials at `η₀ ± 2ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_integral_mul_exp
declarations.doc: Differentiation under the integral sign for a bounded multiple of an exponential family integrand, at an interior point of the Laplace-integrability set.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_chord_of_const_mul_exp
declarations.doc: A nonnegative multiple of `t ↦ exp (d t)` lies below its chord over `[c₁, c₂]` and above the extension of that chord outside the open interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest_of_two_tail_moment_constraints
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.45: the two-tail exponential-family test satisfying the two moment constraints is UMPU. The proof applies `integral_le_of_generalized_neyman_pearson` with the chord of the likelihood ratio through the critical points; for a competing unbiased test, the two moment constraints follow from the vanishing derivative of its power function at `η₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condExp_eq_const_of_similar_test
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.49: similar tests have Neyman structure under bounded completeness.

declarations.name: CKSD.invariant_iff_factors_through_maximal_invariant
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.55, algebraic part: invariant functions factor through a maximal invariant. No measurability of the factor is asserted without a measurable quotient hypothesis.

declarations.name: CKSD.Measure.ext_of_integral_exp_inner_eq
declarations.doc: Multivariate Laplace determinacy: two finite measures on a finite-dimensional real inner product space whose Laplace transforms `u ↦ ∫ exp ⟪u, t⟫` are finite and agree on a ball around the origin are equal.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_withDensity_ofReal
declarations.doc: Integrals against a measure with a nonnegative real density `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_withDensity_ofReal_iff
declarations.doc: Integrability against a measure with a nonnegative real density `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_map_withDensity_ofReal
declarations.doc: Integrals against the image under `T` of a measure with a nonnegative real density `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_map_withDensity_ofReal_iff
declarations.doc: Integrability against the image under `T` of a measure with a nonnegative real density.

declarations.name: CKSD.StatisticalModel

declarations.name: CKSD.StatisticalExperiment
declarations.doc: An experiment without a measurable structure on the parameter space.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsAncillaryStatistic
declarations.doc: The law of an ancillary statistic is the same at every parameter value.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMinimumVarianceUnbiasedEstimator
declarations.doc: An unbiased estimator with uniformly minimum variance in the square-integrable class.

declarations.name: CKSD.testPower
declarations.doc: Power at a parameter, for a real-valued randomized test.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasTestLevel
declarations.doc: Level of a test on a null parameter set, stated without a supremum of an empty set.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSimilarTest
declarations.doc: Similarity means equality of power on the specified parameter set.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasConfidenceCoverage
declarations.doc: Coverage of a confidence set, represented by its membership relation.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsAdmissibleRisk
declarations.doc: A risk vector is admissible in a class if no risk vector dominates it strictly.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBayesRule
declarations.doc: A Bayes rule minimizes the integrated risk for the supplied finite prior.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMinimaxRule
declarations.doc: A minimax rule minimizes worst-case risk. Applications require bounded risk vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsGarbling
declarations.doc: An experiment is a garbling of another if a common Markov kernel produces its laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihoodScore
declarations.doc: The scalar likelihood score for a real parameter at a specified observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisherInformation
declarations.doc: Fisher information as the second score moment; regularity hypotheses belong to theorems.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisherInformationMatrix
declarations.doc: Information matrix for a specified vector score.

declarations.name: CKSD.naturalParameterSpace
declarations.doc: The full domain of Laplace integrability of a natural statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.logPartition
declarations.doc: Log partition function of a natural exponential family.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: A natural exponential law, used on `naturalParameterSpace` with a nonzero base measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMinimalExponentialFamily
declarations.doc: Minimality means that no nonzero linear functional of the statistic is almost surely constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.confidenceSetOfTests
declarations.doc: A confidence set obtained by accepting the corresponding point-null test.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasConfidenceCoverage_confidenceSetOfTests
declarations.doc: The elementary test/confidence-set duality, in probability rather than density form.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisherInformation_nonneg
declarations.doc: Nonnegativity of the Fisher information.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUniformlyMostPowerfulTest.hasTestLevel
declarations.doc: Every UMP test has the asserted level.

declarations.name: CKSD.isGarbling_refl
declarations.doc: Garbling is reflexive.

declarations.name: CKSD.cdf_eq_mathlib
declarations.doc: The CDF adapter agrees with Mathlib for probability measures.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_eq_mathlib
declarations.doc: The centred-integral variance agrees with Mathlib for almost everywhere measurable variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_of_measurable_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: A bounded measurable real function is integrable for a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_mul_eq_integral_comp_mul_integral_kernel
declarations.doc: If the joint law of `(T, X)` under `μ` is the law of `T` composed with the Markov kernel `K`, then `∫ g(T) φ dμ = ∫ g(T) (∫ φ dK(T)) dμ` for bounded measurable `g` and `φ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_eq_integral_integral
declarations.doc: Integration against a mixture `P ∘ₘ Λ` of a Markov kernel: the integral is the average of the component integrals.

declarations.name: CKSD.comp_map_eq_of_map_prodMk_eq_compProd
declarations.doc: If the joint law of `(T, X)` under `μ` is `μ.map T ⊗ₘ K`, then `μ` is the mixture of `K` over the law of `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sub_mul_abs_le_of_convexOn
declarations.doc: A real convex function on the line is bounded below by `L 0 - c |t|` for some constant `c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.setIntegral_preimage_eq_integral_indicator_mul
declarations.doc: A set integral over a preimage `T⁻¹ B` as an integral against the indicator of `B` at `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_indicator_one_le_one
declarations.doc: The indicator of a set is bounded by one in absolute value.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_indicator_comp_mul_eq
declarations.doc: The bounded-function case of `integral_comp_mul_eq_integral_comp_mul_integral_kernel` with the indicator of a measurable set of statistic values.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_integral_kernel_eq_of_isBoundedlyCompleteStatistic
declarations.doc: For a boundedly complete sufficient statistic `T` with disintegrating kernel `K`, a bounded measurable `φ` whose expectation is `α` under every parameter satisfies `∫ φ dK(T) = α` almost surely under every parameter.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_neyman_pearson_test

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_le_integral_threshold_test_of_monotone_likelihood_ratio

declarations.name: CKSD.isUniformlyMostPowerfulTest_of_monotone_likelihood_ratio

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_zero_of_integral_eq_zero_of_pos_density

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_one_sub_of_isStatisticalTest

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_threshold_test_le_of_monotone_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: The reversed Neyman–Pearson step of the Karlin–Rubin theorem: if the density ratio `fb / fa` is a nondecreasing function of `T`, a one-sided test in `T` whose size under `Pb` is at most that of another test also has at most its power under `Pa`.

The proof projects the standardized sample onto the constants and their orthogonal complement, using TauCeti's `HasLaw.iIndepFun_orthogonalProjectionOnto_stdGaussian`, `HasLaw.norm_sq_orthogonalProjectionOnto_stdGaussian`, and `TauCeti.Probability.hasLaw_studentT_of_gaussian_chiSquared`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lai_robbins_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.49: the Lai–Robbins lower bound for exponential-family bandits. The base measure `λ` is σ-finite and not concentrated at one point, the natural parameters range over the open interval `(l, r)` on which `exp(θx)` is `λ`-integrable, and the policy is uniformly good: its regret is `o(n^α)` for every `α > 0` at every configuration. An optimal arm has the largest natural parameter `θ⋆`, and `liminf regret(n) / log n` is at least the Lai–Robbins sum, stated as eventual domination of every smaller constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.thompsonSeedLaw

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_thompson_regret_div_log
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.51, Thompson sampling: for Bernoulli arms with means in `(0,1)` and a unique optimal arm, Thompson sampling with uniform priors attains the Lai–Robbins constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.ucb1Policy

The independence comes from Mathlib's `iIndepFun_infinitePi` and `indep_iSup_of_disjoint`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_sum_sum_mul_banditPlayIndicator

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_gap_mul_le_sqrt

declarations.name: CKSD.ucb1Policy_of_le

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ucb1_banditRegret_le

declarations.name: CKSD.selfNormalizedDesign

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_exists_selfNormalized_gt_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.63, self-normalized bound (Abbasi-Yadkori–Pál–Szepesvári): with probability at least `1 - δ`, simultaneously for all `t ≥ 1`, `‖∑ᵢ Xᵢ εᵢ‖²_{Vₜ⁻¹} ≤ 2σ² log(det(Vₜ)^{1/2} det(V₀)^{-1/2} / δ)`. The noise `εₜ` is `𝓕ₜ`-measurable and conditionally `σ`-sub-Gaussian given `𝓕ₜ₋₁`, and `Xₜ` is `𝓕ₜ₋₁`-measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_linUCB_regret_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.63, LinUCB regret for a finite decision set. Actions `xₜ ∈ 𝒟` are `𝓕ₜ`-measurable and maximize `⟨μ̂ₜ, x⟩ + √βₜ ‖x‖_{Σₜ⁻¹}` for the ridge estimate `μ̂ₜ` with `Σₜ = λ I + ∑_{τ<t} x_τ x_τᵀ`, `λ = σ²/W²`; observations are `⟨μ⋆, xₜ⟩ + ηₜ` with `ηₜ` `𝓕ₜ₊₁`-measurable and conditionally `σ`-sub-Gaussian given `𝓕ₜ`. With probability at least `1 - δ`, for all `T`, the regret is at most `c max(σ, BW) √T (d log(1 + T B² W² / (d σ²)) + log(4/δ))`. The scale `max(σ, BW)` accounts for initial leverage when `λ = σ²/W²`. The minimax lower bound `d√T/2500` is not formalized here.

declarations.doc: The local polytope of a finite pairwise model.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsInteriorLocalBelief
declarations.doc: Strict positivity in the coordinates constrained by the local polytope.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLocalBeliefDirection
declarations.doc: Homogeneous local-polytope constraints describing its tangent directions.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteTableEntropy
declarations.doc: Shannon entropy of a real table, with `0 log 0 = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.betheEntropy
declarations.doc: Bethe entropy of local node and edge tables.

declarations.name: CKSD.betheFreeEnergy
declarations.doc: Bethe free energy, including the vertex and edge potential terms.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBetheStationary
declarations.doc: Stationarity of the Bethe energy along every direction preserving the local constraints.

declarations.name: CKSD.incomingMessageProduct
declarations.doc: Product of incoming messages at `i`, omitting the possible recipient `j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBeliefPropagationFixedPoint
declarations.doc: Belief-propagation fixed-point equations, allowing one positive scale for each message.

declarations.name: CKSD.beliefPropagationNode
declarations.doc: Normalized node belief induced by incoming messages.

declarations.name: CKSD.beliefPropagationEdge
declarations.doc: Normalized edge belief induced by messages entering its endpoints.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBetheStationary_iff_exists_beliefPropagationFixedPoint
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.19: Bethe stationary points in the positive local polytope are exactly BP beliefs.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_beliefPropagation_exact_on_tree
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.23: positive tree models have BP fixed points giving the exact node and edge marginals. The leaf-to-root implementation and the reconstruction theorem for arbitrary boundary beliefs are separate parts of the catalogue entry.

declarations.name: CKSD.beliefPropagation_tree_unique_up_to_scale
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.23: each directed-edge message in a positive tree model is unique up to positive scale.

declarations.name: CKSD.PairwiseGraphicalModel.weight_pos
declarations.doc: Every finite positive graphical-model configuration has positive weight.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsTriangulatedGraph
declarations.doc: A graph is triangulated: every cycle of length at least four has a chord, an edge of the graph between two of its vertices that is not an edge of the cycle.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMaximalCliqueFinset
declarations.doc: A finite set of vertices is a maximal clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsJunctionTree
declarations.doc: `T` on the enumeration `c` of cliques is a junction tree of `G`: `c` lists every maximal clique exactly once, `T` is a tree, and every clique on the path between two cliques contains their intersection.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasJunctionTree
declarations.doc: A graph has a junction tree.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasJunctionTree_iff_isTriangulated
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.27: a finite graph has a junction tree if and only if it is triangulated.

declarations.name: CKSD.jointMarginal
declarations.doc: Marginal table of a joint configuration mass on a finite set of vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.tableMarginal
declarations.doc: Marginal of a table on `C` to the subset `S`, given by its membership proof.

declarations.name: CKSD.junctionTreeProduct
declarations.doc: Junction-tree product formula: clique tables divided by separator tables, one separator factor per tree edge, the separator table being the marginal of the lower-indexed clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_joint_with_clique_marginals_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.27, marginal problem on a junction tree: nonnegative clique tables are the clique marginals of a joint probability law exactly when every table is normalized and adjacent tables agree on their separator; in that case the junction-tree product formula is such a law. The uniqueness of the Markov law is not formalized here.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgeSmoother
declarations.doc: Fixed-design ridge smoother for the objective `‖y - Aβ‖²/(2n) + λ‖β‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgePrediction
declarations.doc: Predicted values of a fixed-design ridge fit.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasKernelCriticalRadius
declarations.doc: Empirical kernel critical-radius inequality in terms of normalized Gram eigenvalues.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgePrediction_oracle_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.13: fixed-design kernel-ridge oracle bounds for a finite feature representation. The constants are universal. Both the expected bound and the Gaussian tail bound use the same critical radius. This does not formalize the eigenvalue-decay calculation for infinite RKHSs.

declarations.name: CKSD.kmeansSampleRisk
declarations.doc: Empirical `k`-means distortion of a finite sample, using an ordered center representation.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_kmeans_centers_of_compact
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.16: almost-sure consistency of compactly constrained empirical `k`-means minimizers. This scope assumes a fixed compact support containing all centers. The unbounded-support theorem under only a second moment requires an additional localization argument.

declarations.name: CKSD.kmeansRisk_comp_perm
declarations.doc: Permuting center labels leaves the population distortion unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgePrediction_zero
declarations.doc: A ridge smoother sends zero observations to zero predicted values.

declarations.name: CKSD.labelUniform
declarations.doc: The uniform law on `[0,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.labelledSample
declarations.doc: Labelled sample from features, label variables, and tie-breaking variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.knnRule
declarations.doc: The `k`-nearest-neighbour rule on a labelled sample with tie-breaking variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.knnExpectedError
declarations.doc: Expected error `𝔼 Lₙ` of the `k`-nearest-neighbour rule built from `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.bayesClassificationRisk
declarations.doc: Bayes risk `R* = 𝔼 min(η(X), 1 - η(X))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nearestNeighborAsymptoticRisk
declarations.doc: Asymptotic `1`-nearest-neighbour risk `L_NN = 𝔼[2η(X)(1 - η(X))]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_oneNN_expectedError
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.14 (Cover–Hart): for every distribution on `ℝ^d × {0,1}`, the expected error of the `1`-nearest-neighbour rule converges to `L_NN = 𝔼[2η(X)(1 - η(X))]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bayesRisk_le_nnRisk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.14, Cover–Hart inequalities `R* ≤ L_NN ≤ 2R*(1 - R*)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_tendsto_knn_expectedError
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.14, fixed odd `k`: the limits `L_kNN` of the expected errors exist, are nonincreasing over odd `k`, and satisfy `R* ≤ L_kNN ≤ R* + 1/√(k e)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_knn_expectedError_bayesRisk
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.14, universal consistency (Stone): if `kₙ → ∞` and `kₙ / n → 0`, the expected error of the `kₙ`-nearest-neighbour rule tends to the Bayes risk for every distribution.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_localAveraging_sq_error
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.20, Stone's theorem for response-independent local averaging (forests). The weights `w n i x xs u` are nonnegative, sum to one, and are jointly measurable functions of the query point `x`, the sample features `xs`, and independent randomness `u ∼ ν`, but not of the responses. Under the domination, localization, and vanishing-maximum conditions the estimate `mₙ(x) = ∑ᵢ wₙᵢ(x) Yᵢ` is consistent in `L²(P_X)` for the regression function `m`, characterized by `∫_{X ∈ s} Y = ∫_s m dP_X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.signedMargin
declarations.doc: Signed classification margin for Boolean labels, with `true` representing `+1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sSup_range_eq
declarations.doc: The supremum of a function on a finite nonempty type is attained.

declarations.name: CKSD.sSup_add_sSup_le_of_lipschitz
declarations.doc: One-coordinate contraction step: for an `L`-Lipschitz `φ` and `c ≥ 0`, `sup(a + cφ(u)) + sup(a - cφ(u)) ≤ sup(a + cLu) + sup(a - cLu)` over a finite index.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sSup_rademacher_comp_le
declarations.doc: Ledoux–Talagrand contraction for a finite class: composing the coordinates with an `L`-Lipschitz function multiplies the summed Rademacher suprema by at most `L`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_marginLoss_sub_le
declarations.doc: The ramp margin loss `min(1, max(0, 1 - u/ρ))` is `1/ρ`-Lipschitz.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginLoss_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: The ramp margin loss takes values in `[0,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginLoss_eq_one_of_nonpos
declarations.doc: The ramp margin loss dominates the zero-one loss of a nonpositive margin.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_margin_generalization_error_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.10: uniform expected-Rademacher margin bound for a finite class.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp_neg_le_one_sub_add_sq_div_two
declarations.doc: Second-order bound `exp(-x) ≤ 1 - x + x²/2` for `x ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sum_mul_sub_le_of_exponential_weights
declarations.doc: Deterministic exponential-weights bound with nonnegative estimated losses `ℓ̂`: if `p t i ∝ exp(-η ∑_{s<t} ℓ̂ s i)`, then `∑_{t<T} ∑ᵢ p t i ℓ̂ t i - ∑_{t<T} ℓ̂ t i⋆ ≤ log K / η + (η/2) ∑_{t<T} ∑ᵢ p t i ℓ̂ t i²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialWeights_succ
declarations.doc: Multiplicative update form of exponential weights: `p (t+1) i = p t i exp(-η ℓ̂ t i) / ∑ⱼ p t j exp(-η ℓ̂ t j)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_indicator_mul_eq_of_condExp
declarations.doc: Conditional-probability identity: if `P[1_{A = j} | 𝓕] = p` and `g` is bounded and `𝓕`-measurable, then `∫ 1_{A = j} g = ∫ p g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp3EstimatedCumulativeLoss
declarations.doc: Exp3 importance-weighted cumulative estimated loss.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp3_expected_regret_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.52: expected Exp3 regret against an oblivious loss sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_sum_exp_entropy_variational_formula
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.26, finite-state entropy variational formula for the log partition function.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_log_sum_exp_div_atTop
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.26, the zero-temperature limit of a finite log partition function.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_predictions_of_gradient_flow
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.30, finite-width tangent-kernel training dynamics for a differentiable model.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgeless_gaussian_risk_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.31, the underparameterized ridgeless risk with Gaussian noise.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_least_squares_gradient_descent
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.40, least-squares gradient descent and the preserved nullspace component.

declarations.name: CKSD.DenseNetParams
declarations.doc: Parameters of a dense network with hidden widths `w 1, …, w H` and scalar output.

declarations.name: CKSD.denseActivation
declarations.doc: Hidden activations of a dense network.

declarations.name: CKSD.denseNetOutput
declarations.doc: Scalar output of a dense network.

declarations.name: CKSD.denseParamCount
declarations.doc: Number of scalar parameters of the architecture, including biases.

declarations.name: CKSD.denseHiddenNeurons
declarations.doc: Number of hidden neurons of the architecture.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPiecewisePolynomial
declarations.doc: A real activation is piecewise polynomial: on each of the finitely many half-open pieces cut out by a finite set of breakpoints it agrees with a polynomial.

declarations.name: CKSD.BooleanClassShatters
declarations.doc: A class of Boolean functions shatters a finite set if it realizes every labelling of it.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_le_of_shatters_denseSignClass
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.35, VC dimension of network sign classifiers: for a fixed piecewise-polynomial activation there is `c` such that every finite set shattered by the sign classifiers of one dense architecture with `P ≥ 2` parameters and depth `L = H + 1` has at most `c (P L log P + P L²)` points. Architectures are layered and fully connected.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalRademacherComplexityOfSet
declarations.doc: Empirical Rademacher complexity of an arbitrary class of real functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.frobeniusSq
declarations.doc: Squared Frobenius norm of a real matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalRademacherComplexity_biasFree_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.35, norm-based capacity: bias-free networks of depth `L = H + 1` on the unit ball, with a `1`-Lipschitz positively homogeneous activation and all weight matrices of Frobenius norm at most `C`, have empirical Rademacher complexity at most `2^{L-1} C^L / √n`, independently of the widths.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderUnitCube
declarations.doc: The unit cube `[0,1]^d` in `Fin d → ℝ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.relu_depth_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.37, depth lower bound (Yarotsky): a `C²` function on `[0,1]^d` that is not affine there cannot be approximated uniformly within `ε` by ReLU networks with `H ≥ 1` hidden layers and at most `c ε^{-1/(2H)}` hidden neurons, for all small `ε`. The restriction to small `ε` is necessary, since constants approximate within any large `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.relu_eldan_shamir_separation
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.37, depth separation (Eldan–Shamir) for the ReLU: for `d ≥ C` there are a probability measure on `ℝ^d` and a function bounded by `2` computed by a two-hidden-layer ReLU network of width at most `C d⁵` and parameters at most `C d^C` in absolute value, at squared `L²` distance at least `c` from every one-hidden-layer ReLU network of width at most `c e^{cd}`. The logistic and Heaviside cases are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsInCompositionHolderBall
declarations.doc: Membership in the Hölder ball of smoothness `β ∈ (0,1]` and radius `K` on a domain.

declarations.name: CKSD.chainComp
declarations.doc: Composition `g (k-1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ g 0` of a chain of maps between coordinate spaces.

declarations.name: CKSD.compositionalHolderClass
declarations.doc: The compositional Hölder class of Schmidt-Hieber with smoothness indices in `(0,1]`: compositions `g q ∘ ⋯ ∘ g 0` with `g i : [a i, b i]^{d i} → [a (i+1), b (i+1)]^{d (i+1)}`, `[a 0, b 0] = [0,1]`, `|a i|, |b i| ≤ K`, each coordinate of `g i` depending on at most `t i` arguments and lying, as a function of those, in the Hölder ball of smoothness `β i` and radius `K`. The scalar output is the unique coordinate of `d (q+1) = 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.uniformDesignRegressionLaw
declarations.doc: Law of one observation `(X, f X + ε)` with `X` uniform on `[0,1]^d` and standard normal noise.

declarations.name: CKSD.compositionalHolder_minimax_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.29, minimax lower bound for compositional Hölder classes (Schmidt-Hieber), for smoothness indices in `(0,1]` and the uniform design on `[0,1]^d` (a density bounded above and below). With `β*ᵢ = βᵢ ∏_{j > i} βⱼ` and `φₙ = maxᵢ n^{-2β*ᵢ/(2β*ᵢ + tᵢ)}`, if `tᵢ ≤ min(d₀, …, dᵢ₋₁)`, then for all large `K` every measurable estimator has risk at least `c φₙ` at some member of the class. Risk is an extended nonnegative integral, allowing infinite risk for unrestricted estimators. The upper bound by sparse ReLU least squares is not formalized here.

declarations.name: CKSD.gpFirstLayerPreactivation
declarations.doc: Preactivation of one first-layer unit with parameters `θ = (weights, bias)` at input `y`, for `N(0, C_W/d)` weights and `N(0, C_b)` bias written as scaled standard normals.

declarations.name: CKSD.gpSecondLayerPreactivation
declarations.doc: Scalar output preactivation of a one-hidden-layer network of width `N` with independent standard normal parameters scaled to `N(0, C_b)` biases and `N(0, C_W / N)` output weights.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_wide_network_gaussian
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.39, Gaussian-process limit at initialization for one hidden layer: at finitely many inputs the output preactivations converge jointly in distribution, as the width tends to infinity, to the centered Gaussian vector with covariance `K²(x,x') = C_b + C_W 𝔼[σ(U)σ(U')]`, where `(U,U')` is the pair of preactivations of one first-layer unit at `x, x'`, centered Gaussian with covariance `K¹(x,x') = C_b + C_W ⟨x,x'⟩/d`. Deeper networks iterate this step.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStationaryPolicy
declarations.doc: A stationary randomized policy: each row is a probability vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyTransition
declarations.doc: State transition matrix under a stationary randomized policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyReward
