declarations.doc: Expected one-step reward under a stationary randomized policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyValue
declarations.doc: Discounted value `V^π = (I - γ P^π)⁻¹ r^π` of a stationary randomized policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyActionValue
declarations.doc: State-action value of a stationary randomized policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyAdvantage
declarations.doc: Advantage `A^π(i,b) = Q^π(i,b) - V^π(i)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyObjective
declarations.doc: Expected value `J(π) = ∑ᵢ ρ i V^π(i)` under an initial law.

declarations.name: CKSD.optimalObjective
declarations.doc: Optimal objective over stationary randomized policies.

declarations.name: CKSD.naturalPolicyGradientIterate
declarations.doc: Natural policy gradient iterates for the softmax parameterization started at `θ = 0`: `π⁽ᵗ⁺¹⁾(b | i) ∝ π⁽ᵗ⁾(b | i) exp(η A⁽ᵗ⁾(i,b) / (1 - γ))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_smul_mulVec_inv_mulVec
declarations.doc: The resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` is a right inverse on vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec_mulVec
declarations.doc: The resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` is a left inverse on vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec
declarations.doc: For a row-stochastic `H`, the resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` dominates the identity on nonnegative vectors: `v ≤ (I - γH)⁻¹ v`, and in particular the resolvent is positive.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec_mono
declarations.doc: The resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` is monotone on vectors for a row-stochastic `H`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec_const
declarations.doc: The resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` maps the constant `c` to the constant `c / (1 - γ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FiniteMarkovDecisionProcess.discount_mem_Ioo
declarations.doc: The discount of a finite model lies in the open unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyTransition_nonneg
declarations.doc: The state transition matrix of a stationary policy has nonnegative entries.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_policyTransition
declarations.doc: The state transition matrix of a stationary policy is row-stochastic.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyValue_eq_add
declarations.doc: Bellman equation `V^π = r^π + γ P^π V^π` of a stationary policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_policyAdvantage
declarations.doc: Averaging the advantage of `π` under the action law of a policy `π'`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_policyAdvantage_self
declarations.doc: The advantage of a stationary policy averages to zero under its own action law.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyValue_sub_eq
declarations.doc: Performance difference identity: `V^{π'} - V^π = (I - γ P^{π'})⁻¹ ā`, where `ā(i) = ∑_b π'(b | i) A^π(i,b)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyValue_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: Values of stationary policies with rewards in `[0,1]` lie in `[0, 1/(1-γ)]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_log_sub_log_nonneg
declarations.doc: Gibbs' inequality for positive probability vectors: `∑ p (log p - log q) ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_le_sum_mul_exp_policyAdvantage
declarations.doc: The normalizer `Z(i) = ∑_b π(b | i) exp(η A^π(i,b) / (1-γ))` of a natural policy gradient step from a stationary policy is at least `1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.naturalPolicyGradientIterate_pos
declarations.doc: Natural policy gradient iterates are stationary policies with positive entries.

declarations.name: CKSD.isStationaryPolicy_naturalPolicyGradientIterate
declarations.doc: Natural policy gradient iterates are stationary policies.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_naturalPolicyGradientIterate_succ
declarations.doc: Logarithmic form of the natural policy gradient step: `log π⁽ᵗ⁺¹⁾(b | i) = log π⁽ᵗ⁾(b | i) + η A⁽ᵗ⁾(i,b) / (1-γ) - log Z⁽ᵗ⁾(i)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyObjective_sub_le_of_log_update
declarations.doc: Mirror-descent bound behind natural policy gradient: if positive stationary policies `π⁽ᵗ⁾`, started from the uniform policy, satisfy the logarithmic update `A⁽ᵗ⁾(i,b) = (1-γ)/η (log π⁽ᵗ⁺¹⁾(b | i) - log π⁽ᵗ⁾(b | i) + log Z⁽ᵗ⁾(i))` with normalizers `Z⁽ᵗ⁾ ≥ 1`, then for rewards in `[0,1]` and every stationary comparator `π⋆`, `J(π⋆) - J(π⁽ᵀ⁾) ≤ log |A| / (η T) + 1 / ((1 - γ)² T)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.optimalObjective_sub_npg_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.61: convergence of natural policy gradient with softmax policies from `θ = 0`, for rewards in `[0,1]`, any initial law `ρ`, and any step `η > 0` (Agarwal–Kakade–Lee–Mahajan): `J⋆(ρ) - J(π⁽ᵀ⁾) ≤ log |A| / (η T) + 1 / ((1 - γ)² T)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FiniteMarkovBandit
declarations.doc: A finite Markov bandit: `K` arms on the common state space `Fin S`, each with a stochastic transition matrix and a reward function, and a discount `β ∈ (0,1)`. Only the played arm moves.

declarations.name: CKSD.gittinsRewardAndTime
declarations.doc: Expected discounted reward and discounted time until the first exit time `τ ≥ 1` from the continuation set `C`, for arm `k` started in each state.

declarations.name: CKSD.gittinsIndex
declarations.doc: The Gittins index of arm `k` in state `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditJointTransition
declarations.doc: Joint transition when arm `k` is played: only its coordinate moves.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditPolicyValue
declarations.doc: Discounted value of a stationary deterministic arm-selection rule on joint states.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditPolicyValue_le_of_gittins
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.51, Gittins index theorem for finite Markov bandits: always playing an arm of largest current Gittins index maximizes the expected discounted reward from every joint state. The comparison class is the stationary deterministic rules on joint states, which attain the optimum over all policies of this finite discounted model (GAPS 107.58). Countable state spaces are not covered.

declarations.name: CKSD.isDifferentiallyPrivate_compProd
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.65, basic composition of two adaptive private releases. The proof bounds the first release through the layer-cake formula for the truncated second-stage probability. The relation `R` is arbitrary, the exponential parameters are real, and the additive errors are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.tvDist_le_two_mul_totalVariationDistance
declarations.doc: Mathlib's total variation distance of probability measures (the `L¹` norm) is at most twice the event discrepancy `totalVariationDistance`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_sub_integral_le_mul_totalVariationDistance
declarations.doc: A measurable function with values in `[0, c]` has expectations under two probability measures differing by at most `c` times their total variation distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_measureReal_comp_sub_le_of_local_privacy
declarations.doc: For a pure `ε`-locally private Markov kernel `Q`, the output laws `Q ∘ₘ P₁` and `Q ∘ₘ P₂` differ on each event by at most `(e^ε - 1) · TV(P₁, P₂)` times the mass of that event under either output law.

declarations.name: CKSD.klFun_le_sq_sub_one
declarations.doc: The Kullback–Leibler function is dominated by the `χ²` integrand on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_le_ofReal_sq_of_abs_measureReal_sub_le
declarations.doc: If two probability measures satisfy `|μ A - ν A| ≤ δ ν A` for every event, then `KL(μ ‖ ν) ≤ δ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_comp_le_of_local_differential_privacy
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.75, the single-release KL contraction under local privacy.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_bernoulliMeasure_one_zero
declarations.doc: Integrals against the Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` on the real line.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_id_bernoulliMeasure_one_zero
declarations.doc: The Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` has mean `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bernoulliMeasure_one_zero_compl_Icc
declarations.doc: The Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` is supported by `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.kernel_apply_le_exp_mul_card
declarations.doc: Group privacy: a mechanism that is `ε`-differentially private for Hamming neighbours changes the probability of an event by at most the factor `exp(ε k)` between data sets that differ in at most `k` coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_mul_comp_le_centralMeanRisk
declarations.doc: A lower bound for the central mean risk on a set of releases far from the mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.centralMeanRisk_add_centralMeanRisk_ge
declarations.doc: Le Cam's two-point bound for Bernoulli laws `Ber(1, 0, a)` and `Ber(1, 0, b)` with `a < b`: the sum of the two risks is at least `((b - a)/2)²` times the sum of the error probabilities of the test that rejects `a` when the release exceeds `(a + b)/2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.klBerReal_le_sq_div
declarations.doc: The binary Kullback–Leibler divergence is at most the χ² divergence `(p - q)² / (q (1 - q))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_half_le_or_of_ofReal_le_add
declarations.doc: If a sum is at least `r`, one of the two terms is at least `r / 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.two_mul_measureReal_sub_le_tvDist
declarations.doc: The event bound from the total variation distance: `2 (Q A - Q' A) ≤ tvDist Q Q'`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bernoulli_centralMeanRisk_ge_inv
declarations.doc: The non-private part of the central lower bound: for every mechanism some Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` has mean squared error at least `1 / (192 n)`. The two laws `Ber(1/2)` and `Ber(1/2 + δ)` with `δ = 1/(2√n)` have product laws at Kullback–Leibler divergence at most `1` (Statlib's `klDiv_pi_const` and `klDiv_bernoulliMeasure_eq_klBerReal`), so by the Bretagnolle–Huber inequality (Statlib's `exp_neg_klDiv_le_two_sub_tvDist`) and data processing (`tvDist_comp_le`) no test separates them well.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_exp_mul_card_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The exponential moment of the number of nonzero coordinates under the product of Bernoulli laws: `∫ exp(ε #{i | dᵢ ≠ 0}) = (1 + q (e^ε - 1))ⁿ`, written as a lower integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_add_mul_exp_sub_one_pow_le_nine
declarations.doc: The exponential moment bound `(1 + q (e^ε - 1))ⁿ ≤ 9` when `q ε ≤ 1/n` and `ε ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bernoulli_centralMeanRisk_ge_private
declarations.doc: The private part of the central lower bound: for an `ε`-differentially private mechanism some Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` has mean squared error at least `min(1, 1/(nε))² / 72`. The two laws are `Ber(1, 0, 0) = δ₀` and `Ber(1, 0, q)` with `q = min(1, 1/(nε))`; by group privacy the release law under the second is at most `(1 + q(e^ε - 1))ⁿ ≤ 9` times the release law under the first.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_centralMeanRisk_ge
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66, central minimax lower bound: there is an absolute `c > 0` such that for `0 < ε ≤ 1` every `ε`-differentially private mechanism has mean squared error at least `c min(1, 1/n + 1/(nε)²)` for the mean of some law on `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.totalVariationDistance_bernoulliMeasure_le
declarations.doc: The total variation distance between `Ber(1, 0, a)` and `Ber(1, 0, b)` is at most `|a - b|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_mul_map_le_localMeanRisk
declarations.doc: A lower bound for the local mean risk on a set of estimates far from the mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bernoulli_localMeanRisk_ge
declarations.doc: The lower half of the local minimax rate: for `ε`-locally private release kernels and a measurable estimator, some Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` has mean squared error at least `min(1, 1/(nε²)) / 768`. The two laws are `Ber(1/2)` and `Ber(1/2 + δ)` with `δ = min(1/2, 1/(4ε√n))`; the release laws of one individual are at Kullback–Leibler divergence at most `16 ε² δ²` by the contraction under local privacy (GAPS 107.75, `klDiv_comp_le_of_local_differential_privacy`), and Le Cam's method concludes as in the central case.

declarations.name: CKSD.localLaplaceKernel
declarations.doc: The local Laplace release kernel: clip to `[-1,1]` and add Laplace noise of scale `2/ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMarkovKernel_localLaplaceKernel
declarations.doc: The local Laplace release kernel is a Markov kernel for positive `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isDifferentiallyPrivate_localLaplaceKernel
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66: the local Laplace release kernel is `ε`-locally differentially private.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_sq_sub_localLaplace_le
declarations.doc: Under a law supported by `[-1,1]`, the squared deviation of a local Laplace release from the mean has lower integral at most `4 + 8/ε²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_id_localLaplace
declarations.doc: Under a law supported by `[-1,1]`, a local Laplace release has mean equal to the mean of the law.

declarations.name: CKSD.localMeanRisk_localLaplace_mean_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66: on laws supported by `[-1,1]`, the sample mean of local Laplace releases has mean squared error at most `(4 + 8/ε²)/n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.localMeanRisk_minimax_order
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66, local minimax rate: there are absolute `c, C > 0` such that for `0 < ε ≤ 1` every noninteractive protocol with `ε`-locally private release kernels and every measurable estimator has mean squared error at least `c min(1, 1/(nε²))` for some law on `[-1,1]`, and some such protocol has error at most `C min(1, 1/(nε²))` for every law on `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsHammingNeighbor
declarations.doc: Data sets in `ℝⁿ` are neighbouring when they differ in at most one coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.clipUnit
declarations.doc: Clipping to `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.clippedMean
declarations.doc: Mean of a data set clipped to `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.laplaceMeanMechanism
declarations.doc: The clipped Laplace mean mechanism with noise scale `2 / (n ε)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.centralMeanRisk
declarations.doc: Mean squared error of a central mechanism for the mean of `P`, from `n` observations. It is a lower Lebesgue integral in `ℝ≥0∞`, so a mechanism with infinite error has risk `∞` rather than the junk value `0` of a non-integrable Bochner integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.localMeanRisk
declarations.doc: Mean squared error of a noninteractive local protocol with release kernels `Q` and estimator `est`, for the mean of `P`, as a lower Lebesgue integral in `ℝ≥0∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_clippedMean_sub_le
declarations.doc: Changing one coordinate moves the clipped mean by at most `2 / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.laplacePDF_le_exp_mul
declarations.doc: Shifting the location of a Laplace density by `δ` changes it by at most `e^{|δ|/b}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isDifferentiallyPrivate_laplaceMeanMechanism
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66: the clipped Laplace mean mechanism is `ε`-differentially private.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sub_laplaceMeasure
declarations.doc: Mean squared deviation of a Laplace law from a point: squared bias plus variance `2b²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_sq_sub_laplaceMeasure
declarations.doc: The squared deviation from a point is integrable under a Laplace law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_clippedMean_sub_sq_le
declarations.doc: On laws supported by `[-1,1]` the clipped sample mean has mean squared error at most `1/n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.centralMeanRisk_laplaceMeanMechanism_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66: on laws supported by `[-1,1]`, the clipped Laplace mean mechanism has mean squared error at most `1/n + 8/(n ε)²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMarkovKernel_laplaceMeanMechanism
declarations.doc: The clipped Laplace mean mechanism is a Markov kernel for positive `n` and `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_le_one_of_support
declarations.doc: The mean of a law supported by `[-1,1]` lies in `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_centralMeanRisk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66, central minimax upper bound: for `0 < ε ≤ 1` some `ε`-differentially private mechanism (the clipped Laplace mean, or the constant release `0` when `1` is the smaller rate) has mean squared error at most `8 min(1, 1/n + 1/(nε)²)` for every law on `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.clampUnitInterval
declarations.doc: A real number clamped to the unit interval, used as an edge probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.balancedLabelings
declarations.doc: Labellings of `Fin n` with exactly `n / 2` vertices in the group `true`.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockModelGraphProb
declarations.doc: Probability of the graph `G` under the two-group block model given the labelling `σ`: independent edges with probability `p` within and `q` between groups (both clamped).

declarations.name: CKSD.blockModelMass
declarations.doc: Joint mass of a labelling and a graph under the symmetric two-group block model.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockModelGraphLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the observed graph of the symmetric two-group block model.

declarations.name: CKSD.exactRecoveryProbability
declarations.doc: Probability that an estimator recovers the labelling exactly, up to a global flip.

declarations.name: CKSD.labelingOverlap
declarations.doc: Normalized overlap `|∑ᵢ σᵢ τᵢ| / n` of two labellings in `±1` coding.

declarations.name: CKSD.weakRecoveryProbability
declarations.doc: Probability that an estimator has overlap at least `ε` with the planted labelling.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_exactRecovery_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.41: the exact-recovery threshold of the logarithmic-degree two-group block model, for `a, b > 0`. Recovery up to a global flip with probability tending to one is possible exactly when `(√a - √b)² ≥ 2`. The polynomial-time achievability claim is not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_exactRecovery_iff_of_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.41, the case `b = 0`: exact recovery is possible exactly when `a > 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_weakRecovery_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.42: the Kesten–Stigum threshold for weak recovery in the sparse two-group block model with `p = a/n`, `q = b/n`, `a, b > 0`. The efficiency claim is not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockModel_binomialRandom_mutually_contiguous
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.42: below the Kesten–Stigum threshold the sparse block model and the binomial random graph with the same average degree are mutually contiguous, stated directly on sequences of events.

declarations.name: CKSD.componentSize
declarations.doc: Number of vertices in the connected component of `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.largestComponentSize
declarations.doc: Number of vertices of a largest connected component (zero for the empty vertex set).

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_tendsto_binomialRandom_components_le_log
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47, subcritical phase: for `p = c/n` with `0 ≤ c < 1`, all components have at most `C log n` vertices with probability tending to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_giant_component
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47, supercritical phase: for `p = c/n` with `c > 1`, the largest component has size `ζ n + o(n)` in probability, with `ζ ∈ (0,1)` the root of `1 - ζ = e^{-cζ}`, and any two distinct components have the smaller one of size at most `C log n` with probability tending to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_connectivity_threshold
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47, connectivity threshold: for `p = (log n + xₙ)/n`, connectivity has probability tending to one if `xₙ → ∞`, isolated vertices have probability tending to one if `xₙ → -∞`, and for constant `xₙ = x` the probability of connectivity tends to `exp(-e^{-x})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finitePermOfFin
declarations.doc: The permutation of `ℕ` acting as `σ` on the first `n` labels and fixing all others.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_finitePermOfFin_eq_on
declarations.doc: Every permutation of `ℕ` agrees on the first `n` labels with a permutation moving only finitely many labels.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_comap_eq_of_finitePerm_invariant
declarations.doc: A law on graphs on `ℕ` invariant under every permutation of finitely many labels is invariant under every permutation of `ℕ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_graphonMixture_of_finitePerm_invariant
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.43: a law on graphs on `ℕ` invariant under permutations of finitely many labels is a mixture of graphon models, with a unique mixing measure on TauCeti's unit-interval graphon space (graphons modulo cut distance zero). The all-permutations case is TauCeti's `InfiniteExchangeableGraphLaw.existsUnique_bind_infiniteSampleLawOnSpace`.

declarations.name: CKSD.infiniteSampleLaw_eq_iff_exists_measurePreserving
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.43, uniqueness in the attained form (Borgs–Chayes–Lovász): two graphons on the unit interval have the same joint sampling law exactly when they have almost everywhere equal pullbacks under two measure-preserving self-maps of the unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.ucb_regret_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.50: UCB1 regret, with prefix rewards and all tie choices explicit.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_asynchronous_stochastic_approximation
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.54, bounded-noise asynchronous stochastic approximation for a contraction. The tabular Q-learning application uses the Bellman operator and visited-pair steps.

declarations.name: CKSD.sSup_range_le_add
declarations.doc: Pointwise domination up to `c` passes to suprema over a nonempty finite index.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_eq_sSup_range
declarations.doc: The supremum over a nonempty finite index is attained.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_le_of_stochastic
declarations.doc: A probability average of values bounded by `c` is bounded by `c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bellman_fixed_point_and_greedy_policy
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.58, Bellman optimality, a greedy stationary policy, and the primal LP.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_mulVec_le_of_stochastic
declarations.doc: A row-stochastic matrix does not increase the sup norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_le_of_resolvent
declarations.doc: Resolvent bound `‖x‖ ≤ ‖(I - γH)x‖ / (1 - γ)` for a row-stochastic `H`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUnit_one_sub_smul
declarations.doc: `I - γH` is invertible for a row-stochastic `H` and `γ ∈ (0,1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.policy_value_resolvent_identity_and_error_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.59, the fixed-policy resolvent identity and sup-norm error bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_projected_fixed_point_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.60, deterministic projected-contraction error bound underlying TD(lambda).

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_reward_eq_of_map_eq
declarations.doc: All rewards of an arm have the mean of its first reward when they share one law.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_sum_sub_of_add_le_armSampleAverage
declarations.doc: The prefix sum of the centred rewards of one arm, rewritten from the prefix average.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_sum_sub_of_armSampleAverage_le
declarations.doc: The prefix sum of the centred losses of one arm, rewritten from the prefix average.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_add_le_armSampleAverage_le
declarations.doc: Hoeffding's inequality for an upper deviation of the prefix average of one arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_armSampleAverage_le_sub_le
declarations.doc: Hoeffding's inequality for a lower deviation of the prefix average of one arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_armSampleAverage
declarations.doc: Prefix averages of measurable rewards are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_succ
declarations.doc: The play count increases by one exactly at a play of the arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_mono
declarations.doc: Play counts are monotone in time.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_le
declarations.doc: The play count after `t` rounds is at most `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_lt_of_play
declarations.doc: A play of the arm at time `t` makes its count strictly larger at every later time.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_play_count_lt_le
declarations.doc: At most `ℓ` plays of an arm happen while its count is below `ℓ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_le_armPlayCount
declarations.doc: If the first `K` rounds play each arm once, then every arm has been played at least once by any time `t ≥ K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_le_add_card
declarations.doc: Plays during the initialization rounds: the count of an arm before its initial play is zero, so with `1 ≤ ℓ` all plays with count at least `ℓ` happen at times `t ≥ K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ucb_deviation_of_play
declarations.doc: The deterministic step of the UCB1 analysis: if a suboptimal arm `i` with gap `Δ` is played at a time `t ≥ K` after at least `ℓ` earlier plays, where `8 log t ≤ Δ² ℓ`, then either the average of the optimal arm lies below its mean by the confidence radius, or the average of arm `i` lies above its mean by the confidence radius.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_armPlayCount
declarations.doc: Play counts of a measurable arm process are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp_neg_two_mul_sqrt_sq_eq
declarations.doc: The Hoeffding bound at the UCB1 confidence radius: `exp(-2 s c²) = t⁻⁴` for `c = √(2 log t / s)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.natCast_mul_inv_pow_four_le
declarations.doc: `t · t⁻⁴ ≤ t⁻²` for `t ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_armPlayCount_le_of_ucb
declarations.doc: Expected play count of a suboptimal arm under UCB1 (Auer, Cesa-Bianchi and Fischer): for an arm `i` whose mean is below that of an arm `star` by `Δ > 0`, the expected number of plays of `i` during the first `T` rounds is at most `8 log T / Δ² + 3`. The reward table has independent entries in `[0,1]` almost surely, with a common law along each arm; the arm process plays each arm once during the first `K` rounds and afterwards an arm of maximal UCB1 index.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_armPlayCount
declarations.doc: Play counts of a measurable arm process are integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_comp_eq_sum_mul_armPlayCount
declarations.doc: A sum over rounds of a function of the arm played, regrouped by arms.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.TripleStatus
declarations.doc: Status of the middle vertex `b` of consecutive trail vertices `a, b, c`: if `b` is a collider (`a → b ← c`) it must satisfy `P`, otherwise it must satisfy `N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith
declarations.doc: A trail `q 0, …, q n` whose interior colliders satisfy `P` and whose interior noncolliders satisfy `N`. Repeated vertices are allowed.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.MemAncestorClosure
declarations.doc: A vertex lies in `C` or is an ancestor of a vertex of `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.ForwardReach
declarations.doc: A directed path from `v` to a vertex of `T` whose vertices after `v` avoid `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.trailAppend
declarations.doc: Concatenation of a trail `q₁` of length `n₁` with a trail `q₂`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_edge_self
declarations.doc: A directed acyclic graph has no loops.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_edge_of_edge
declarations.doc: A directed acyclic graph has no two-cycles.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.tripleStatus_of_edge_right
declarations.doc: The middle vertex of a triple is a noncollider when it has an arrow towards its right neighbour.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.tripleStatus_of_edge_left
declarations.doc: The middle vertex of a triple is a noncollider when it has an arrow towards its left neighbour.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.tripleStatus_comm
declarations.doc: The status of a triple does not depend on its orientation.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.trailAppend_of_le
declarations.doc: `trailAppend` agrees with the first trail up to its length.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.trailAppend_of_ge
declarations.doc: `trailAppend` agrees with the shifted second trail from the junction on.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.rev
declarations.doc: The reverse of a trail is a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.shift
declarations.doc: A suffix of a trail, shifted to start at `0`, is a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.trunc
declarations.doc: A prefix of a trail is a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.append
declarations.doc: Concatenation of two trails meeting at a vertex with admissible status is a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.snoc
declarations.doc: Extending a trail by one adjacent vertex, with an admissible status at the old endpoint, gives a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isTrailWith_of_forward
declarations.doc: A forward directed chain is a trail whose interior vertices are all noncolliders.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isDescendant_of_forward
declarations.doc: Along a forward directed chain every later vertex is a descendant of the first.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_forward_of_isDescendant
declarations.doc: A nonempty directed path is a forward chain.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.forwardReach_of_not_memAncestorClosure
declarations.doc: If `v` lies outside the ancestral closure of `C` and is `t ∈ T` or an ancestor of some `t ∈ T`, then a directed path from `v` reaches `T` avoiding `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.tripleStatus_of_loop
declarations.doc: Junction step of the shortening argument: cutting a loop `q i = q j` out of an active trail leaves an admissible status at the junction.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_injective_activeTrail
declarations.doc: An active trail can be shortened to an injective active trail with the same endpoints.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isActivePath_of_isTrailWith
declarations.doc: An injective active trail is an active path.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_collider_of_forward_backward
declarations.doc: On a trail that leaves `q i` along an outgoing arrow and arrives at `q j` against an arrow out of `q j`, some interior vertex `q m` with `i < m < j` is a collider descending from `q i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isTrailWith_of_isActivePath
declarations.doc: An active path, read as a function on `ℕ`, is an injective active trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_activeTrail_of_semiActive
declarations.doc: A trail between `A` and `B` whose noncolliders avoid `C` and whose colliders lie in a set `D` all of whose vertices outside the ancestral closure of `C` are ancestors of `A ∪ B` (or lie in it) can be modified into an active trail between `A` and `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.false_of_dSeparated_of_semiActiveTrail
declarations.doc: If `A` and `B` are d-separated by `C`, there is no trail between `A` and `B` whose noncolliders avoid `C` and whose colliders lie in a set `D` all of whose vertices outside the ancestral closure of `C` are ancestors of `A ∪ B` or lie in it.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm
declarations.doc: Quadratic form of a real matrix on Euclidean space.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleMean
declarations.doc: Mean of a finite Euclidean sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.scatterMatrix
declarations.doc: Centered scatter matrix of a finite Euclidean sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianNegLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: Negative Gaussian log-likelihood up to its constant term.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign
declarations.doc: Uniform sampling of exactly `n` units from `N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.populationMean
declarations.doc: Finite-population mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.populationVariance
declarations.doc: Finite-population variance with divisor `N-1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLatinSquare
declarations.doc: A Latin square on `Fin s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.OrthogonalLatinSquares
declarations.doc: Orthogonality of two Latin squares.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearCombinationCorrelation
declarations.doc: The correlation of `aᵀU` and `bᵀV` for covariance blocks `Suu`, `Suv`, `Svv`.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalCorrelationMatrix
declarations.doc: The whitened cross-covariance `Σ_UU^{-1/2} Σ_UV Σ_VV^{-1/2}`, whose singular values are the canonical correlations.

declarations.name: CKSD.PosDef.inv_sqrt_facts
declarations.doc: A real positive semidefinite matrix has a symmetric inverse square root whose square is the inverse.

declarations.name: CKSD.charpoly_canonicalCorrelationMatrix_mul_transpose
declarations.doc: The squared canonical correlations are the roots of the characteristic polynomial of `Σ_UU⁻¹ Σ_UV Σ_VV⁻¹ Σ_VU`.

declarations.name: CKSD.charpoly_canonicalCorrelationMatrix_transform
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.29: canonical correlations are unchanged by nonsingular linear transformations `U ↦ P U` and `V ↦ Q V`; the characteristic polynomial of `M Mᵀ`, whose roots are the squared canonical correlations, is invariant.

declarations.name: CKSD.PosDef.isUnit_det_inv_sqrt
declarations.doc: The inverse square root of a real positive definite matrix is invertible.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalCorrelationMatrix_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The whitened cross-covariance vanishes exactly when the cross-covariance does.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_elim_dotProduct_fromBlocks_mulVec
declarations.doc: The quadratic form of a block matrix on a block vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_dotProduct_mulVec_le_of_posSemidef_fromBlocks
declarations.doc: Cauchy–Schwarz for the cross block of a positive semidefinite block matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.PosDef.inv_sqrt_mul_mul_inv_sqrt
declarations.doc: A whitening identity: `Σ^{-1/2} Σ Σ^{-1/2} = 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_euclideanSpace_eq_sqrt_dotProduct
declarations.doc: The Euclidean norm as the square root of the dot product.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_dotProduct_le_dotProduct_self_mul
declarations.doc: Cauchy–Schwarz for the real dot product.

declarations.name: CKSD.dotProduct_mulVec_self_le
declarations.doc: The squared L2 operator-norm bound for a real matrix, in dot-product form.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_dotProduct_self_eq_one_and_mulVec_eq_norm
declarations.doc: The L2 operator norm of a real matrix with a nonempty column index is attained on a unit vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalCorrelationMatrix_whitening
declarations.doc: Whitening identities for canonical correlations: with `a = Σ_UU^{-1/2} x` and `b = Σ_VV^{-1/2} y`, the cross form becomes `xᵀ K y` and the variances become `‖x‖²`, `‖y‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_canonicalCorrelationMatrix_le_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.29: for a positive semidefinite joint covariance with positive definite diagonal blocks, the canonical correlations lie in `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isGreatest_linearCombinationCorrelation
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.29: the largest correlation between linear combinations `aᵀU` and `bᵀV` is the largest singular value (the L2 operator norm) of `Σ_UU^{-1/2} Σ_UV Σ_VV^{-1/2}`, and it is attained. The characterization of the subsequent canonical correlations under successive uncorrelatedness constraints is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.firstBlockSelection
declarations.doc: Selection of the first `p` coordinates of `ℝ^{p+q}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.secondBlockSelection
declarations.doc: Selection of the last `q` coordinates of `ℝ^{p+q}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_gaussian_blocks_iff_canonicalCorrelationMatrix_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.29: for a jointly Gaussian pair `(U, V)` with positive definite marginal covariances, `U` and `V` are independent exactly when all canonical correlations vanish.

declarations.name: CKSD.quantileCheckLoss
declarations.doc: Quantile-regression check loss, with the conventional left/right value zero at the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.quantileRegressionObjective
declarations.doc: Fixed-design quantile-regression objective.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsQuantileRegressionEstimator
declarations.doc: A quantile-regression estimate minimizes the check-loss objective.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialDispersionLogDensity
declarations.doc: An exponential-dispersion log density.

declarations.name: CKSD.glmInformationMatrix
declarations.doc: Generalized-linear-model information matrix for a specified diagonal weight vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.twoStageLeastSquares
declarations.doc: Two-stage least-squares coefficient, using the instrument projection.

declarations.name: CKSD.treatmentEffectInfluence
declarations.doc: Average-treatment-effect efficient influence function, with observed outcome as argument.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph
declarations.doc: Finite directed acyclic causal graph; acyclicity excludes every nonempty directed cycle.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.parents
declarations.doc: Parents of a vertex in a causal graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsDescendant
declarations.doc: Proper descendant relation in a causal graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsActivePath
declarations.doc: A path is active when each noncollider is unconditioned and each collider has an observed descendant.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.DSeparated
declarations.doc: Graphical d-separation by absence of an active path.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.MarkovEquivalent
declarations.doc: Two causal graphs are Markov equivalent if all their d-separation statements agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.Adjacent
declarations.doc: Undirected skeleton adjacency.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsUnshieldedCollider
declarations.doc: An unshielded collider is an inward-facing triple with nonadjacent endpoints.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.RespectsParents
declarations.doc: Local mass functions obey the parent restriction of a specified graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.directedFactorizationMass
declarations.doc: Recursive product mass from local conditional masses.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass
declarations.doc: Truncated factorization for an intervention on a finite set of vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.markovEquivalent_iff_skeleton_and_colliders
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.67: skeleton and unshielded colliders characterize Markov equivalence.

declarations.name: CKSD.quantileCheckLoss_nonneg
declarations.doc: Check loss is nonnegative for a probability level.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.markovEquivalent_refl
declarations.doc: Graphical Markov equivalence is reflexive.

declarations.name: CKSD.propensityScore
declarations.doc: The propensity score as a conditional expectation on the original sample space.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepFun_propensityScore
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.48: the propensity score is a balancing score, in the standard Borel setting.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepFun_of_propensityScore
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.48: ignorability descends from the covariates to their propensity score.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_finite_sample
declarations.doc: Every real statistic on the finite sample space has finite moments under a finite design.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sample_sum
declarations.doc: Integrating a sum over a random sample uses the first-order inclusion probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sample_pair_sum
declarations.doc: Integrating a double sum over a random sample uses joint inclusion probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.treatment_effect_identification_of_conditional_independence
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.47, finite-stratum potential-outcome identification under mean ignorability.

declarations.name: CKSD.doubly_robust_bias_identity
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.49, finite-stratum double-robustness bias identity. The causal identification and cross-fitting conclusions require the additional frameworks described in the source; this is the observable-moment identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.local_average_treatment_effect_eq_wald_ratio
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.50: the Wald ratio identifies the complier average effect.

declarations.name: CKSD.horvitz_thompson_mean_and_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.72, Horvitz–Thompson unbiasedness and exact design variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.horvitz_thompson_variance_estimator_unbiased
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.72, unbiased estimation of the Horvitz–Thompson design variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.horvitz_thompson_variance_eq_sen_yates_grundy
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.72, Sen–Yates–Grundy identity for a fixed-size sampling design.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_real_superset
declarations.doc: Under simple random sampling of `n` units, the probability that the sample contains a given set `B` of at most `n` units is `C(N - |B|, n - |B|) / C(N, n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_simpleRandomSampleDesign
declarations.doc: Simple random sampling of `n ≤ N` units is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_real_superset_eq_card
declarations.doc: Under simple random sampling, the probability that the sample contains `B` is the proportion of `n`-subsets containing `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_real_mem
declarations.doc: First-order inclusion probabilities of simple random sampling.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_real_mem_mem
declarations.doc: Second-order inclusion probabilities of simple random sampling for distinct units.

declarations.name: CKSD.populationVariance_eq_sum_sq
declarations.doc: The finite-population variance as a difference of sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sum_ite_eq_mul
declarations.doc: A double sum with one coefficient on the diagonal and another off it.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_sum_mean_and_variance
declarations.doc: Mean and design variance of a sample total under simple random sampling.

declarations.name: CKSD.simple_random_sample_mean_and_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.73, finite-population correction for a simple random sample mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.randomized_treatment_difference_mean_and_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.46, Neyman's exact design variance in a completely randomized experiment.

declarations.name: CKSD.neyman_allocation_optimal
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.73, the continuous Neyman allocation optimization.

declarations.name: CKSD.treatmentStratum
declarations.doc: Joint covariate-stratum and treatment event.

declarations.name: CKSD.stratumOutcomeMean
declarations.doc: Observed conditional outcome mean in a treatment stratum.

declarations.name: CKSD.stratumOutcomeVariance
declarations.doc: Observed conditional outcome variance in a treatment stratum.

declarations.name: CKSD.stratumPropensity
declarations.doc: Propensity in a finite observed covariate stratum.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteStrataTreatmentEffect
declarations.doc: Identified treatment-effect functional of an observed law with finite covariate strata.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteStrataTreatmentInfluence
declarations.doc: Treatment-effect influence function at the true finite-stratum nuisances.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_treatmentStratum
declarations.doc: Treatment strata are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_sum_treatmentStratum
declarations.doc: An integral splits over the finite partition into treatment strata.

declarations.name: CKSD.setIntegral_affine_centred
declarations.doc: Within one stratum, an affine function of the centred outcome integrates to its constant part, and its square to the constant part plus the scaled within-stratum variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_treatmentStratum
declarations.doc: Integral of a function of the stratum labels.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteStrataTreatmentInfluence_mean_and_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.56: mean zero and the variance formula for the treatment-effect influence function in finite strata. Positive joint stratum masses express overlap explicitly.

declarations.name: CKSD.setIntegral_withDensity_score_tilt
declarations.doc: Set integrals against a nonnegative linear score tilt of a measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_covariateStratum_eq_add
declarations.doc: The covariate stratum splits into its two treatment strata.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteStrataTreatmentInfluence_eqOn
declarations.doc: On each treatment stratum the influence function is affine in the outcome.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_finiteStrataTreatmentEffect_score_tilt
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.56: the treatment-effect influence function represents derivatives along bounded mean-zero score tilts of the observed law. The semiparametric convolution bound is not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsChordalGraph
declarations.doc: A chordal (decomposable) graph: every cycle of length at least four has a chord, an edge between two vertices of the cycle that are not consecutive on it.

declarations.name: CKSD.GraphSeparates
declarations.doc: `S` separates `A` from `B` in an undirected graph: every walk from `A` to `B` meets `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cliqueSeparator
declarations.doc: The separator `C_j ∩ (C₀ ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_{j-1})` of a sequence of cliques.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPerfectCliqueSequence
declarations.doc: A perfect sequence of the maximal cliques of `G`: every maximal clique occurs exactly once, and each separator is contained in an earlier clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUndirectedGlobalMarkovMass
declarations.doc: The undirected global Markov property for a probability mass function: separation of disjoint sets implies conditional independence.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_maximal_isClique_superset
declarations.doc: In a finite graph every clique lies in a maximal clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUndirectedGlobalMarkovMass_of_factorization
declarations.doc: The undirected global Markov property follows from a factorization of the mass function into factors each depending only on the coordinates in a clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.cliqueHistory
declarations.doc: The union `C₀ ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_{m-1}` of the first `m` cliques of a sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.graphSeparates_cliqueSeparator
declarations.doc: For a perfect sequence of the maximal cliques, the separator `S_j` separates the new vertices `C_j \ S_j` from the earlier vertices `(C₀ ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_{j-1}) \ S_j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.clique_factorization_of_isUndirectedGlobalMarkovMass
declarations.doc: For a perfect sequence of the maximal cliques, the global Markov property implies the clique factorization of the marginal masses.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUndirectedGlobalMarkovMass_iff_clique_factorization
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.36, discrete form: for a decomposable graph with a perfect sequence of its maximal cliques, a positive probability mass function is globally Markov exactly when `p(x) = ∏_C p_C(x_C) / ∏_S p_S(x_S)^{ν(S)}`, written here without division.

declarations.name: CKSD.principalBlock
declarations.doc: The block `B_{CC}` of a square matrix indexed by a finite set `C` of coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.padBlock
declarations.doc: `[B]^V`: a matrix indexed by `C`, padded with zeros to a `p × p` matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianConcentrationLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: The Gaussian log likelihood of a concentration matrix `K` for `n` observations with centred sum-of-squares matrix `ssd`, up to an additive constant and the factor `n / 2`: `log det K - tr(K ssd) / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.concentrationModel
declarations.doc: Concentration matrices of the Gaussian graphical model of `G`: positive definite with zero entries off the edges.

declarations.name: CKSD.isGreatest_gaussianConcentrationLogLikelihood_decomposable
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.36, Gaussian decomposable model: if every clique block of `ssd` is positive definite (which holds almost surely when `n > max_C |C|` for a Gaussian sample), the maximum likelihood estimator of the concentration matrix exists, is unique, and equals `n (∑_C [(ssd_C)⁻¹]^V - ∑_S ν(S) [(ssd_S)⁻¹]^V)`. The almost-sure existence criterion `n > max_C |C|` as a necessary condition is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_gaussianConcentration_mle
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.36, general graph: if `ssd` is positive definite, there is a unique positive definite `Σ̂` that agrees with `ssd / n` on the diagonal and on the edges and whose inverse vanishes off the edges, and `Σ̂⁻¹` is the unique maximizer of the likelihood over the concentration model. Convergence of iterative proportional scaling is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.kiefer_wolfowitz_equivalence
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.37, Kiefer–Wolfowitz equivalence for a finite design space.

declarations.name: CKSD.randomization_p_value_valid
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.38, conservative finite randomization p-values, including ties.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisher_inequality_of_balanced_incomplete_block_design
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.42, Fisher's inequality for nontrivial balanced incomplete blocks.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_orthogonal_latin_squares_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.44, the upper bound on a family of mutually orthogonal Latin squares.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_complete_orthogonal_latin_squares_of_equiv
declarations.doc: Over a finite field `F` identified with `Fin s`, the squares `(x, y) ↦ a x + y` for the nonzero elements `a` form a complete family of mutually orthogonal Latin squares.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_complete_orthogonal_latin_squares_of_isPrimePow
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.44, existence of a complete family at prime-power orders.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.parentFinset
declarations.doc: Parents of a vertex, as a finite set.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.nonDescendantFinset
declarations.doc: Nondescendants of a vertex other than the vertex itself and its parents.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.removeIncoming
declarations.doc: The graph with all arrows into `X` removed (`G_{\bar X}`).

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.removeOutgoing
declarations.doc: The graph with all arrows out of `Z` removed (`G_{\underline Z}`).

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.InterceptsDirectedPaths
declarations.doc: A directed path from a vertex of `X` to a vertex of `Y` has some vertex in `Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.BlocksBackdoorPaths
declarations.doc: Every back-door path from `X` to `Y`, that is, every path whose first arrow points into its initial vertex in `X`, is blocked by `W`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsBackdoorSet
declarations.doc: The back-door criterion for `Z` relative to `(X, Y)`: no vertex of `Z` is a descendant of a vertex of `X`, and `Z` blocks every back-door path from `X` to `Y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsFrontdoorSet
declarations.doc: The front-door criterion for `Z` relative to `(X, Y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsProbabilityMass
declarations.doc: A probability mass function on configurations.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLocalMassFamily
declarations.doc: Local conditional mass functions: each is a probability mass function in the state of its vertex, for every configuration of the other variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass
declarations.doc: Probability that the variables in `B` take the values of `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condMass
declarations.doc: Conditional probability that the variables in `B` take the values of `x`, given that the variables in `C` take the values of `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CondIndepMass
declarations.doc: Conditional independence of `X_A` and `X_B` given `X_C` for a mass function, in product form (no division).

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.RecursivelyFactorizes
declarations.doc: Recursive factorization `p(x) = ∏_v p(x_v | x_{pa(v)})`, with the conditional masses of `p` itself.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsLocalDirectedMarkov
declarations.doc: The local directed Markov property: each variable is conditionally independent of its nondescendants given its parents.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsGlobalDirectedMarkov
declarations.doc: The global directed Markov property: d-separation of disjoint sets implies conditional independence.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsFaithful
declarations.doc: A mass function is faithful to `G` when its conditional independences among disjoint sets are exactly the d-separations of `G`.

declarations.name: CKSD.overwriteOn
declarations.doc: Overwrite a configuration on `B` by values indexed by `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.doMarginalMass
declarations.doc: Interventional probability that the variables in `B` take the values of `y`, under `do(X = x)` given by the truncated factorization.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass
declarations.doc: Interventional conditional probability `P(y | do(x), w)`, all values read from `b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_adjacent_self
declarations.doc: No vertex is adjacent to itself in a directed acyclic graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.Adjacent.ne
declarations.doc: Adjacent vertices are distinct.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.Adjacent.symm
declarations.doc: Adjacency is symmetric.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.Adjacent.not_dSeparated
declarations.doc: Adjacent vertices are joined by an active path of length one, whatever is conditioned on.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsActivePath.rev
declarations.doc: The reverse of an active path is active.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.DSeparated.symm
declarations.doc: d-separation is symmetric.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isDescendant_of_isActivePath_parents
declarations.doc: A path leaving `u` along an outgoing arrow and active given the parents of `u` is a directed path out of `u`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_parents_of_not_isDescendant
declarations.doc: A vertex `u` is d-separated by its parents from every other vertex that is neither a parent nor a descendant of `u`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_eq_sum_ite_sum_update
declarations.doc: Splitting a sum over configurations according to the value at one coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_ite_prod_eq_sum_ite_prod_compl
declarations.doc: Summing out the coordinates of a set closed under children: the factors of the summed vertices disappear, the coordinates are frozen at those of `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_ite_mul_sum_ite_of_factor
declarations.doc: Conditional independence from a factorization `g = F * H` with `F` depending only on the coordinates in `R ∪ C` and `H` only on those outside `R`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepMass_directedFactorizationMass_of_dSeparated
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.62 (core step): a mass function that factorizes recursively along a directed acyclic graph, with local masses respecting the parents, satisfies the global directed Markov property: d-separation of disjoint sets implies conditional independence.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_parents_of_not_adjacent
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: two nonadjacent distinct vertices of a directed acyclic graph are d-separated by the parents of one of them.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.adjacent_iff_forall_not_dSeparated
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: two distinct vertices are adjacent if and only if no set of other vertices d-separates them.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isCollider_iff_not_mem_of_dSeparated
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: in a skeleton path `u - v - w` with distinct endpoints, if `S` d-separates `u` and `w`, then `u → v ← w` exactly when `v ∉ S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.skeleton_and_colliders_eq_of_isFaithful
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: the conditional independences of a mass function faithful to two directed acyclic graphs determine the skeleton and the unshielded colliders; hence (by GAPS 105.67) the Markov equivalence class. The statement on the PC algorithm is not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.nonAncestorPart
declarations.doc: The vertices of `Z` that are not ancestors of any vertex of `W` in `G_{\bar X}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.augment
declarations.doc: The graph augmented by an intervention indicator `none` with an arrow into each vertex of `Z`; the original vertices are `some v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.augment_edge_some
declarations.doc: Arrows between original vertices of the augmented graph are the arrows of the graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.augment_edge_none
declarations.doc: The intervention indicator points exactly into the vertices of `Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.augment_not_edge_to_none
declarations.doc: No arrow points into the intervention indicator.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isDescendant_of_augment
declarations.doc: Descendants among the original vertices of the augmented graph are descendants in the graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.augmentedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Local masses on the augmented graph: the indicator `none` is uniform on `{s₀, s₁}`; when it equals `s₁` the vertices of `Z` are set to the values of `b`, otherwise all vertices follow the local masses after `do(X = b)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isLocalMassFamily_augmentedLocalMass
declarations.doc: The augmented local masses form a local mass family.

declarations.name: CKSD.respectsParents_augmentedLocalMass
declarations.doc: The augmented local masses respect the parents of the augmented graph of `G_{\bar X}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.directedFactorizationMass_augmentedLocalMass
declarations.doc: The recursive product of the augmented local masses: the indicator mass times the law under `do(X ∪ Z)` (indicator `s₁`) or under `do(X)` (any other value).

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_option_pi
declarations.doc: Splitting a sum over configurations of `Option V` into the value at `none` and the configuration on `V`.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_augmented
declarations.doc: Marginal masses of the augmented mass, at a point with indicator value `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.transGen_removeIncoming_nonAncestorPart
declarations.doc: A directed path of `G_{\bar X}` ending in `W` survives the removal of the arrows into the vertices of `Z` that are not ancestors of `W` in `G_{\bar X}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_isDescendant_removeIncoming_mem
declarations.doc: In `G_{\bar X}` no vertex is a proper ancestor of a vertex of `X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_augment_of_rule_three
declarations.doc: The graph-theoretic step of rule 3: if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X, \overline{Z(W)}}`, then `Y` and the intervention indicator are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in the augmented graph of `G_{\bar X}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass_rule_three
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.64, rule 3 of the do-calculus (insertion and deletion of actions): if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X, \overline{Z(W)}}`, then `P(y | do(x), do(z), w) = P(y | do(x), w)`. The conditioning events have positive interventional probability. The completeness of the three rules for identifiability is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_congr_point
declarations.doc: A marginal mass depends only on the values of the point at the fixed coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_nonneg
declarations.doc: Marginal masses of a nonnegative mass function are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_anti
declarations.doc: Marginal masses decrease when more coordinates are fixed.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_union_of_support
declarations.doc: Fixing coordinates on which the mass is concentrated does not change a marginal mass.

declarations.name: CKSD.overwriteOn_of_notMem
declarations.doc: `overwriteOn` leaves the coordinates outside the overwritten set unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.overwriteOn_self
declarations.doc: `overwriteOn` with the values of the configuration itself does nothing.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_eq_sum_overwriteOn
declarations.doc: The law of total probability: a marginal mass is the sum, over the values of a disjoint set `Z` of variables, of the marginal masses with `Z` fixed as well.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_congr
declarations.doc: Interventional masses depend only on the intervention values on the intervened set.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_empty
declarations.doc: The empty intervention leaves the recursive product mass unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Local masses after the intervention `do(X = b)`: point masses at the values of `b` on `X`, the original local masses elsewhere.

declarations.name: CKSD.isLocalMassFamily_intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Intervened local masses form a local mass family.

declarations.name: CKSD.respectsParents_intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Intervened local masses respect the parents in the graph with the arrows into `X` removed.

declarations.name: CKSD.directedFactorizationMass_intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: The truncated factorization is the recursive product of the intervened local masses.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Intervening on `X` after intervening on `Z` is intervening on `X ∪ Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_nonneg
declarations.doc: Interventional masses are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_support
declarations.doc: The interventional mass under `do(X = a)` is concentrated on the configurations that agree with `a` on `X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.directedFactorizationMass_nonneg
declarations.doc: Recursive product masses are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_empty_directedFactorizationMass
declarations.doc: A recursive product of local masses has total mass one.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_empty_interventionMass
declarations.doc: An interventional mass has total mass one.

declarations.name: CKSD.div_eq_div_of_condIndepMass
declarations.doc: Conditional independence `Y ⊥ Z | X ∪ W`, for a mass concentrated on one value of `X`, in quotient form: `P(y | z, w) = P(y | w)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.doMarginalMass_eq_marginalMass_of_nonDescendant
declarations.doc: The interventional marginal of variables that are neither in `X` nor descendants of `X` equals their observational marginal.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsActivePath.mono
declarations.doc: An active path in a subgraph is active in the graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_removeOutgoing_of_blocksBackdoorPaths
declarations.doc: If every back-door path from `X` to `Y` is blocked by `W`, then in any subgraph with the arrows out of `X` removed, `Y` and `X` are d-separated by `W`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_isDescendant_of_blocksBackdoorPaths
declarations.doc: If every back-door path from `X` to `Z` is blocked by the empty set, then no vertex of `X` is a descendant of a vertex of `Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_isDescendant_removeIncoming_of_intercepts
declarations.doc: If `Z` intercepts all directed paths from `X` to `Y`, then in the graph with the arrows into `Z` removed no vertex of `Y` is a descendant of a vertex of `X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass_union_eq_of_dSeparated
declarations.doc: Action/observation exchange (rule 2 of the do-calculus) under the single positivity condition `P(z, w | do(x)) > 0`: if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X \underline Z}`, then `P(y | do(x), do(z), w) = P(y | do(x), z, w)`. The proof compares both sides with the mass in which the children of `Z` read the fixed values of `b` on `Z`; that mass factorizes along `G_{\bar X \underline Z}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_univ
declarations.doc: The marginal mass on all variables is the mass itself.

declarations.name: CKSD.CondIndepMass.mono_right
declarations.doc: The decomposition property of conditional independence: `A ⊥ B | C` implies `A ⊥ B' | C` for `B' ⊆ B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_marginalMass_insert_update
declarations.doc: Summing the marginal mass of `insert v C` over the values of `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.marginalMass_eq_prod_condMass_of_isLocalDirectedMarkov
declarations.doc: Under the local directed Markov property, the marginal mass of an ancestral set is the product of the conditional masses of its vertices given their parents.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.recursivelyFactorizes_of_isLocalDirectedMarkov
declarations.doc: The local directed Markov property implies recursive factorization.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_localMass_of_recursivelyFactorizes
declarations.doc: A recursively factorizing probability mass function is the recursive product of a local mass family respecting the parents.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.recursivelyFactorizes_tfae
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.62: for a probability mass function on finitely many finite-valued variables, recursive factorization along a directed acyclic graph, the local directed Markov property, and the global (d-separation) Markov property are equivalent. Discrete-variable form: densities with respect to counting measure on a finite product.

declarations.name: CKSD.doMarginalMass_eq_backdoor
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.63, back-door formula for discrete variables: if `Z` satisfies the back-door criterion relative to `(X, Y)`, then `P(y | do(x)) = ∑_z P(y | x, z) P(z)` for the law factorizing recursively along `G` with local masses `localMass`. The conditioning events `{X = x, Z = z}` are assumed to have positive probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.doMarginalMass_eq_frontdoor
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.63, front-door formula for discrete variables: if `Z` satisfies the front-door criterion relative to `(X, Y)`, then `P(y | do(x)) = ∑_z P(z | x) ∑_{x'} P(y | x', z) P(x')`. The conditioning events `{X = x}` and `{X = x', Z = z}` are assumed to have positive probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass_rule_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.64, rule 1 of the do-calculus (insertion and deletion of observations): if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X}`, then `P(y | do(x), z, w) = P(y | do(x), w)`. The conditioning event `{Z = z, W = w}` has positive interventional probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass_rule_two
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.64, rule 2 of the do-calculus (action/observation exchange): if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X \underline Z}`, then `P(y | do(x), do(z), w) = P(y | do(x), z, w)`. The event `(z,w)` has positive probability under `do(x)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_norm_sq_add_stdGaussian
declarations.doc: The squared length of a shifted finite-dimensional standard Gaussian has noncentral chi-squared law.

declarations.name: CKSD.nestedFStatistic
declarations.doc: The F statistic of the nested projection models `P₀ ≤ P₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNestedModelInvariantTest
declarations.doc: A test is invariant under rescaling, translation within the smaller model space, and the orthogonal maps that commute with both projections.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_nestedFStatistic_eq_noncentralF
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.16: under the larger model the F statistic has the noncentral F law with `r₁ - r₀` and `n - r₁` degrees of freedom and noncentrality `δ² = ‖(P₁ - P₀) μ‖² / σ²`; hence the power of any test based on it depends on `(μ, σ²)` only through `δ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.strictMono_noncentralF_upper_tail
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.16: the power `P(F > c)` of the F test with critical value `c > 0` is strictly increasing in the noncentrality `δ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fTest_isUniformlyMostPowerful_invariant
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.16: among level-`α` tests invariant under rescaling, translation within the smaller model space, and orthogonal maps of the hypothesis and residual spaces, the F test with critical value `c` (the upper `α` point of the central F law) is uniformly most powerful. The parameter is `(μ, σ²)` with `P₁ μ = μ` and `σ² > 0`; the null hypothesis is `P₀ μ = μ`. The average-power optimality among similar tests is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.factorCovariance
declarations.doc: Covariance of an orthogonal factor model with diagonal unique variances.

declarations.name: CKSD.factorLikelihoodCriterion
declarations.doc: Gaussian covariance criterion for a factor model, up to a constant and sample-size factor.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNormalizedFactorLoading
declarations.doc: Normalized loadings have distinct decreasing positive weighted column squared lengths.

declarations.name: CKSD.factorColumnSigns
declarations.doc: A signed relabeling that changes only factor-column signs.

declarations.name: CKSD.loadingSignDistance
declarations.doc: Distance between two loading matrices modulo factor-column signs, in operator norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.factorCovariance_mul_orthogonal
declarations.doc: Orthogonal rotations of factors do not change their implied covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.normalizedFactorLoading_eq_up_to_signs
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.35: normalized nondegenerate loadings are identified up to column signs once both their common covariance and the diagonal unique covariance are specified.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_factor_mle_of_compact
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.35: consistency of factor maximum likelihood on a compact identified parameter set. Compactness and uniform positive unique variances are explicit restrictions of this formulation; the unrestricted parameter-space and asymptotic-normality assertions are not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent
declarations.doc: The observed-history event `{L̄_k = l̄_k, Ā_{k-1} = ā_{k-1}}` for a covariate record `l`: the covariates up to time `k` take the recorded values and the treatments before time `k` follow the regime `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: The regime-adherent past `{L̄_{k-1} = l̄_{k-1}, Ā_{k-1} = ā_{k-1}}` before time `k`; it is the whole space for `k = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_congr
declarations.doc: History events depend only on the recorded covariates up to the current time.

declarations.name: CKSD.gRegimeEvent_congr
declarations.doc: Regime-adherent pasts depend only on the recorded covariates before the current time.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_subset_gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: The history event at time `k` is contained in the regime-adherent past before `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_snoc
declarations.doc: Appending the next covariate value splits the regime-adherent past.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_gHistoryEvent
declarations.doc: History events are measurable when the coordinate events are.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: Regime-adherent pasts are measurable when the coordinate events are.

declarations.name: CKSD.prod_div_succ_mul_eq_prod_div
declarations.doc: Telescoping of sequential weights: for real weights with the zero pattern of probabilities of nested events, the inverse treatment weights times the final probability equal the product of the conditional covariate probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_sum_gInverseWeight
declarations.doc: Inverse-probability-weighted representation over the first `n` time points. If at each time `k < N` the potential outcome is mean-exchangeable with the treatment given the observed history, and regime-adherent continuations of histories of positive probability have positive probability, then for `n ≤ N` the mean of `Ya` is the sum over covariate records of the inverse treatment weights times the integral of `Ya` over the regime-adherent event.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_potentialOutcome_eq_gFormula
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.65: the longitudinal g-formula for discrete covariates. Covariates `L t` take values in a finite type and treatments `A t` in any type, at times `t = 0, …, T`; `l` ranges over covariate records `(l_0, …, l_T)`, `Ya` is the potential outcome under the regime `a` and `Y` the observed outcome. Consistency is `Y = Ya` whenever the observed treatments follow the regime. Sequential exchangeability is used in its mean form, `E[Ya 1{A_t = a_t} | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}] = E[Ya | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}] P(A_t = a_t | …)`, written without division; it is implied by `Ya ⊥ A_t | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}`. Sequential positivity is the uniform lower bound `δ` on `P(A_t = a_t | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1})`. The `t = 0` factor of the product is `P(L_0 = l_0)`, since the regime-adherent past before time `0` is the whole space. The iterated-conditional-expectation form and the general kernel form are not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialDispersionLaw
declarations.doc: The exponential dispersion law with cumulant `b`, dispersion `φ`, and natural parameter `θ`, relative to the dominating measure `ν`.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalGLMInformation
declarations.doc: The canonical-link information matrix `J = E[x xᵀ b''(⟪x, β⟫)]` of one covariate draw.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalGLMLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: The canonical-link log likelihood of the first `n` observations, up to terms free of `β`, with the dispersion kept.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCanonicalGLMRoot
declarations.doc: `β` solves the canonical-link likelihood equations for the first `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_canonicalGLM_root
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.3, canonical-link form: for independent and identically distributed pairs `(xᵢ, Yᵢ)` whose response given the covariate is exponential-dispersion with natural parameter `⟪x, β⟫`, with covariates bounded by `R`, smooth cumulant function, natural parameter space all of `ℝ`, and nonsingular `J = E[x xᵀ b''(⟪x, β⟫)]`, every consistent root `β̂` of the likelihood equations satisfies `√n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, φ J⁻¹)`, and `φ̂^{-1/2} J^{1/2} √n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, I_p)` for every consistent `φ̂`. Restrictions of scope: canonical link (`g = (b')⁻¹`), bounded covariates, and natural parameter space `ℝ`; the general twice-differentiable link is not covered.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_canonicalGLM_deviance
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.3, deviance test for nested canonical-link models with known dispersion: if the true coefficient lies in a subspace `L`, `β̂` is a consistent root of the full likelihood equations and `β̃` a consistent maximizer of the likelihood over `L`, then the scaled deviance difference `2 (ℓₙ(β̂) - ℓₙ(β̃))` converges in distribution to chi-squared on `p - dim L` degrees of freedom. Hypotheses as in `tendstoInDistribution_canonicalGLM_root`.

declarations.name: CKSD.otherCoordinates
declarations.doc: All coordinates except two selected indices.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_otherCoordinates
declarations.doc: The coordinate conditioning map is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsGaussianConcentrationModel
declarations.doc: A nondegenerate Gaussian covariance belongs to a concentration graph if missing edges correspond to zero entries of its precision matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasGaussianPairwiseMarkovProperty
declarations.doc: Gaussian pairwise Markov property relative to an undirected graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_condIndepFun_iff_precision_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.26: a missing precision entry is equivalent to conditional independence of the corresponding Gaussian coordinates given all remaining coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel
declarations.doc: Parameters of a reduced finite Gaussian mixture: all components are nondegenerate, distinct, and have positive weight. Laws and densities use the upstream TauCeti construction.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.law
declarations.doc: Probability law of a reduced Gaussian mixture, using TauCeti's finite mixture.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.density
declarations.doc: Real Gaussian-mixture density, using TauCeti's canonical continuous density.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.logLikelihood
declarations.doc: Log likelihood of a reduced Gaussian mixture at a finite observed sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.density_nonneg
declarations.doc: The canonical mixture density is nonnegative, by TauCeti.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.hasDensity
declarations.doc: The mixture's real density agrees with its law in CKSD's density interface, using TauCeti.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianMixtureModel_identifiable
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.6: finite nondegenerate Gaussian mixtures are identifiable up to relabeling, including equality of the number of distinct positive-weight components.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianMixtureModel_logLikelihood_unbounded
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.6: two Gaussian components already give an unbounded likelihood when their covariances are unconstrained. The sample and ambient dimension are both nonempty.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_sampleMean_scatterMatrix_wishart_and_hotelling
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.22, normal sample mean/covariance independence and Hotelling's exact law.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_det_le_trace_sub_card_and_eq_iff
declarations.doc: The spectral inequality `log det A ≤ tr A - dim` for a positive-definite real matrix, with equality exactly at the identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_det_add_trace_mul_inv_minimum_unique
declarations.doc: The Gaussian covariance criterion `log det C + tr(S C⁻¹)` is uniquely minimized at `C = S` when both covariance matrices are positive definite.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm_eq_dotProduct
declarations.doc: The Euclidean quadratic form agrees with the coordinate dot product.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sub_sampleMean_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A nonempty finite sample has zero sum of deviations from its sample mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_matrixQuadraticForm_sub_eq
declarations.doc: Centering a quadratic sum at the sample mean separates its location error.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_matrixQuadraticForm_sub_sampleMean_eq_trace
declarations.doc: A centered quadratic sum is the trace pairing of the scatter matrix and its coefficient.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm_pos
declarations.doc: A positive-definite real matrix has a positive quadratic form on every nonzero vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianNegLogLikelihood_minimum_unique
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.28, the full-rank Gaussian covariance likelihood has a unique minimum.

declarations.name: CKSD.wishart_determinant_law
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.31, determinant law obtained from Bartlett's decomposition.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_sample_correlation_student_law
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.32, exact correlation t law for independent standard-normal coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCovarianceMatrix
declarations.doc: Sample covariance with the maximum-likelihood divisor `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.symmetricMatrixEigenvalues
declarations.doc: Ordered Hermitian eigenvalues, with an explicit zero convention outside the Hermitian locus.

declarations.name: CKSD.wilksLambda
declarations.doc: Wilks's determinant ratio for error and hypothesis scatter matrices.

declarations.name: CKSD.sphericityRatio
declarations.doc: The sphericity likelihood ratio before taking its sample-size power.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockIndependenceRatio
declarations.doc: The determinant ratio for independence of two consecutive coordinate blocks.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateHypothesisRoots
declarations.doc: Roots of a positive-error multivariate hypothesis, computed after symmetric whitening.

declarations.name: CKSD.lawleyHotellingTrace
declarations.doc: Lawley–Hotelling trace statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.pillaiTrace
declarations.doc: Pillai trace statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.royLargestRoot
declarations.doc: Roy's largest root, with the value zero for a zero-dimensional response space.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCovarianceMatrix_isHermitian
declarations.doc: Sample covariance is Hermitian, including an empty sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_wilksLambda_wishart_eq_beta_product
