declarations.doc: GAPS 105.23: the exact Wilks product law for independent Wishart error and hypothesis matrices. This is the distributional core; the linear-model projection reduction and Bartlett correction are separate assertions of the catalogue family.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_gaussian_sample_covariance_eigenvalue
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.24: central limit theorem for a simple eigenvalue of a centered Gaussian sample covariance with divisor `n`. Multiplicities in other population eigenvalues are allowed.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sphericity_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.33: Wilks's chi-squared limit for sphericity in fixed dimension. The second-order Bartlett approximation is outside this first-order limit statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_block_independence_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.33: the first-order likelihood-ratio limit for two independent Gaussian blocks.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_eigenvalues₀_eq_iff
declarations.doc: Two real symmetric matrices have the same ordered eigenvalues exactly when they have the same characteristic polynomial.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateHypothesisRoots_eq_iff_charpoly_eq
declarations.doc: Generalized roots are the ordered eigenvalues of the whitened hypothesis matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateHypothesisRoots_eq_iff_congruent
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.34: generalized roots classify scatter-matrix pairs under simultaneous congruence. This is the algebraic maximal-invariant assertion for response transformations.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_det_one_add_and_trace_mul_inv_one_add
declarations.doc: For a real symmetric matrix `M` with nonnegative eigenvalues, the determinant of `1 + M` and the trace of `M (1 + M)⁻¹` in terms of the eigenvalues.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_sum_eigenvalues₀_eq
declarations.doc: Sums over the ordered eigenvalues agree with sums over the matrix-indexed eigenvalues.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_prod_eigenvalues₀_eq
declarations.doc: Products over the ordered eigenvalues agree with products over the matrix-indexed eigenvalues.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariate_test_statistics_eq_roots
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.34: the determinant, Lawley–Hotelling, and Pillai statistics in generalized roots.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_inner_of_covariance_eq
declarations.doc: With uncorrelated coordinates of common variance `v`, the variance of `⟪b, Y⟫` is `v ‖b‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_projection_le_of_unbiased
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.1, scalar Gauss–Markov comparison by projecting an unbiased coefficient.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_projection_residual_law_and_indepFun
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.2, residual chi-squared law and projection independence.

declarations.name: CKSD.nested_gaussian_projection_fisher_law
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.10, exact null F law for nested Gaussian projection models.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_matrixQuadraticForm_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.15, Craig–Sakamoto criterion for centered quadratic forms.

declarations.name: CKSD.expectedQuantileCheckLoss
declarations.doc: Expected check loss for a scalar location candidate.

declarations.name: CKSD.quantileCheckLoss_eq_add_max
declarations.doc: The check loss as a linear part plus a negative part.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_quantileCheckLoss
declarations.doc: Measurability of the check loss.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_quantileCheckLoss_sub
declarations.doc: The check loss at a translated location is integrable when the law has a first moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_add_mul_sub_indicator
declarations.doc: A constant multiple of a centred indicator is integrable under a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_add_mul_sub_indicator
declarations.doc: Integral of an integrable function plus a constant multiple of a centred indicator.

declarations.name: CKSD.minimizes_expectedQuantileCheckLoss_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.5: expected check-loss minimizers are precisely the distributional quantiles. This characterization allows atoms; finite first moment makes every displayed risk finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.weightedDesignMoment
declarations.doc: Normalized weighted design second-moment matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_quantile_regression
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.5: fixed-design quantile-regression central limit theorem. The density bounds, uniform local continuity, design limits, and maximal leverage condition are all explicit. No identical-distribution assumption is imposed on the responses.

declarations.name: CKSD.InstrumentalVariableObservation
declarations.doc: Structural observation in an instrumental-variable model: regressor, instrument, error.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentSecondMoment
declarations.doc: Second moment of the instruments.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentRegressorMoment
declarations.doc: Cross second moment between instruments and regressors.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentErrorMoment
declarations.doc: Instrument-score covariance in the correctly specified structural model.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentalVariableSampleEstimator
declarations.doc: Two-stage least-squares sample estimator under the structural equation.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentalVariableCovariance
declarations.doc: Asymptotic two-stage least-squares covariance from the population instrument moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_twoStageLeastSquares
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.55: consistency of two-stage least squares under second-moment and rank conditions.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_twoStageLeastSquares
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.55: heteroscedasticity-robust two-stage least-squares central limit theorem. Square integrability of the instrument-error product is explicit, as required for its CLT.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsLinearSEMMatrix
declarations.doc: A coefficient matrix of a linear structural equation model along `G`: the coefficient of `X_k` in the equation of `X_j` is nonzero exactly when `k → j` is an edge.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearSEMLaw
declarations.doc: The law of the solution `X = (1 - B)⁻¹ N` of a linear structural equation model with independent noises of laws `ν j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNonGaussianPositiveDensityLaw
declarations.doc: A real law is non-Gaussian with a strictly positive density.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordinateRestriction
declarations.doc: Restriction of a vector to the coordinates in `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_coordinateRestriction
declarations.doc: Coordinate restrictions are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsFaithfulLaw
declarations.doc: A law on `V → ℝ` is faithful to `G` when, for disjoint `A`, `B`, `C`, the coordinates in `A` and `B` are conditionally independent given those in `C` exactly when `A` and `B` are d-separated by `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.RespectsParentsReal
declarations.doc: The structural functions of an additive-noise model respect the parents of `G`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsAdditiveNoiseLaw
declarations.doc: The law of an additive-noise model `X_j = f_j(X_{pa(j)}) + N_j` with independent noises of laws `ν j`: the image of the noise law under a measurable solution map of the equations.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsNonlinearInParents
declarations.doc: Each structural function is nonlinear in each of its parent arguments: along every line in the direction of a parent coordinate it is not affine.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.edge_eq_of_linearSEMLaw_eq_of_nonGaussian
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, linear non-Gaussian models: if two linear structural equation models along `G` and `H`, with nonzero coefficients on the edges and independent non-Gaussian noises with strictly positive densities, have the same law, then `G = H`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.edge_eq_of_linearSEMLaw_eq_of_equalVariance
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, linear Gaussian models with equal noise variances: if two linear structural equation models along `G` and `H`, with nonzero coefficients on the edges and independent Gaussian noises of one common positive variance within each model, have the same law, then `G = H`. The noise means are arbitrary.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.edge_eq_of_additiveNoiseLaw_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, nonlinear additive Gaussian-noise models: if two additive-noise models along `G` and `H`, with three times continuously differentiable structural functions that respect the parents and are nonlinear in each parent argument, and independent Gaussian noises of positive variances, have the same law, then `G = H`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_linearGaussianSEM_iff_markovEquivalent
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, linear Gaussian models with unrestricted variances identify only the Markov equivalence class: for a linear Gaussian model along `G` whose law is faithful to `G`, a directed acyclic graph `H` carries a linear Gaussian model (nonzero edge coefficients, positive noise variances) with the same law faithful to `H` exactly when `H` is Markov equivalent to `G`. Faithfulness to both graphs makes the equivalence class the precise answer.

declarations.name: CKSD.totalVariationDistance
declarations.doc: Total variation in the statistical convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.kolmogorovSmirnovStatistic
declarations.doc: Kolmogorov–Smirnov discrepancy, using a countable determining set.

declarations.name: CKSD.kernelDensityEstimator
declarations.doc: Kernel density estimator in one dimension.

declarations.name: CKSD.restrictedL1Norm
declarations.doc: Coordinatewise L1 norm restricted to a set of coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparsity
declarations.doc: Support size of a finite-dimensional vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.bestSparseL1Error
declarations.doc: The best `s`-term L1 approximation error.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: A restricted-isometry bound, expressed without taking an infimum over constants.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergCount
declarations.doc: Benjamini–Hochberg rejection count, including the zero-rejection case.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_toEuclideanCLM_le_of_rowSum_le
declarations.doc: Schur test for a symmetric matrix: the Euclidean operator norm is at most any bound on the absolute row sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_thresholded_covariance_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.52, deterministic sparse-row bound for hard covariance thresholding.

declarations.name: CKSD.euclideanCovarianceMatrix
declarations.doc: Population covariance in Euclidean coordinates, using Mathlib's covariance adapter.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCovarianceMatrix
declarations.doc: The sample-centred empirical covariance matrix, with divisor `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.leadingRayleighValue
declarations.doc: Largest Rayleigh value of a real matrix; the intended spectral interpretation is symmetric. The empty unit sphere in dimension zero gives the usual real `sSup ∅ = 0` convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.leading_empirical_covariance_eigenvalue_asymptotics
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.30: leading empirical covariance eigenvalue expansion and CLT in finite dimension. The Gaussian variance formula is not needed for this non-Gaussian fourth-moment version.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_leading_empirical_eigenvector_error
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.30: the root-`n` bound for a measurably chosen leading empirical eigenvector. Its sign is fixed by nonnegative inner product with the population eigenvector.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCovarianceMatrix_zero
declarations.doc: The empirical covariance of the empty sample is the zero matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCovarianceMatrix_isSymm
declarations.doc: An empirical covariance matrix is symmetric, for every sample including the empty one.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_kolmogorovSmirnovStatistic_gt_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.1, finite-sample Dvoretzky–Kiefer–Wolfowitz–Massart bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_kernelDensityEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.4, pointwise bias-corrected kernel-density central limit theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_integral_abs_kernelDensityEstimator_sub
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.5, one-dimensional universal almost-sure L1 consistency.

declarations.name: CKSD.minimizer_mem_span_of_feature_vectors
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.8, representer theorem in its Hilbert feature-vector formulation.

declarations.name: CKSD.natCast_mul_sum_perm_apply
declarations.doc: Summing `f (σ i)` over all permutations: `n * ∑_σ f (σ i) = n! * ∑_k f k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.natCast_mul_sum_perm_apply_mul_apply
declarations.doc: Summing `a (σ i) a (σ j)` over permutations for `i ≠ j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.linear_rank_statistic_mean_and_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.14, the exact mean and variance under uniform ranks.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteEmpiricalCDF
declarations.doc: Empirical distribution function of a finite sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.cramerVonMisesStatistic
declarations.doc: Cramér–von Mises statistic, with the factor `n` normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.twoSampleKolmogorovSmirnovStatistic
declarations.doc: Two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic, without the asymptotic scaling factor.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_finiteEmpiricalCDF_uncurry
declarations.doc: The finite empirical distribution function is jointly measurable in the sample and the argument.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_cdf_of_isFiniteMeasure
declarations.doc: The distribution function `t ↦ P (-∞, t]` of a finite measure is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_cramerVonMisesStatistic
declarations.doc: The Cramér–von Mises statistic is a measurable function of the sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_cramerVonMisesStatistic_eq_uniform
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.17: finite-sample distribution-freeness of the Cramér–von Mises statistic. The reference law `U` is the uniform probability law on the unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteEmpiricalCDF_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: The finite empirical distribution function takes values in `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_rat_finiteEmpiricalCDF_eq
declarations.doc: Two finite empirical distribution functions take at every real point the same pair of values as at some rational point slightly to the right.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_finiteEmpiricalCDF
declarations.doc: The finite empirical distribution function at a fixed point is measurable in the sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_twoSampleKolmogorovSmirnovStatistic
declarations.doc: The two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic is a measurable function of the two samples.

declarations.name: CKSD.bddAbove_range_abs_finiteEmpiricalCDF_sub
declarations.doc: The range defining the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic is bounded above by one.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteEmpiricalCDF_quantile_comp
declarations.doc: Composing a sample in `(0, 1)` with the quantile function of `P` turns its empirical distribution function into the original one evaluated along the CDF of `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_twoSampleKolmogorovSmirnovStatistic_eq_uniform
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.17: finite-sample distribution-freeness of the two-sample KS statistic. The reference law `U` is the uniform probability law on the unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_unit_eigenvector_rayleigh_le
declarations.doc: A self-adjoint operator on a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space has a unit eigenvector whose eigenvalue dominates the Rayleigh quotient.

declarations.name: CKSD.leading_eigenvector_residual_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.54: residual perturbation bound, with the gap specified by a Rayleigh bound. The probabilistic spiked-covariance bound is outside this deterministic statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.precisionNeighbourhood
declarations.doc: The neighbourhood `N(j) = {k ≠ j | Θ j k ≠ 0}` of a vertex in the graph of a matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.principalSubmatrix
declarations.doc: The principal submatrix of a matrix on a set of indices.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIncoherentAt
declarations.doc: Incoherence at vertex `j`: every `k ∉ S ∪ {j}` has `‖Σ_{k S} (Σ_{S S})⁻¹‖₁ ≤ 1 - α`. When `S` avoids `j` this is the incoherence of the covariance of the coordinates other than `j` with respect to `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.RowSumNormLE
declarations.doc: The bound `‖A‖_{∞→∞} ≤ b` on the maximal absolute row sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.nodeLassoObjective
declarations.doc: The lasso objective for regressing coordinate `j` on the other coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNodeLassoEstimate
declarations.doc: `β` is a neighbourhood-lasso estimate for vertex `j`: it has zero `j`-th coefficient and minimizes the node lasso objective among such coefficient vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.andRuleEdge
declarations.doc: The "and" rule: `{j, k}` is an estimated edge when each lies in the other's estimated neighbourhood; `B j` are the coefficients of the regression of coordinate `j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.orRuleEdge
declarations.doc: The "or" rule: `{j, k}` is an estimated edge when one lies in the other's estimated neighbourhood.

declarations.name: CKSD.neighbourhoodSelection_graph_recovery
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.53, neighbourhood selection: with universal constants, under incoherence, the row-sum bound, unit-bounded variances, maximal degree `m`, and `n ≥ c₁ m log p`, the "or" rule includes no false edge and the "and" rule includes every edge with `|Θ j k| ≥ 7 b λ max (Θ j j) (Θ k k)`, with the stated probability; since the "and" edges are "or" edges, both rules have both properties. The edge condition bounds the regression coefficients `-Θ j k / Θ j j` and `-Θ k j / Θ k k` below by `7 b λ`; this is the bound proved by Wainwright (2019), Theorem 11.12, whose statement puts `|Θ j k|` in its place although `Θ j j ≥ 1` is not bounded above. The lasso estimates `B x j` are arbitrary minimizers.

declarations.name: CKSD.centeredSampleCovariance
declarations.doc: The second-moment matrix `n⁻¹ ∑ xᵢ xᵢᵀ` of a centered sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.graphicalLassoObjective
declarations.doc: The graphical lasso objective `tr(Θ S) - log det Θ + λ ∑_{j ≠ k} |Θ j k|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsGraphicalLassoEstimate
declarations.doc: `Θ` is a graphical lasso estimate: a positive definite minimizer of the objective.

declarations.name: CKSD.graphicalLasso_frobenius_error_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.53, graphical lasso: the Frobenius error bound under `σ`-sub-Gaussian centered coordinates and at most `m` nonzero entries per row of `Θ = Σ⁻¹`. The estimator `T x` is required to be a graphical lasso estimate whenever one exists; the operator norm is the Euclidean one.

declarations.name: CKSD.leastConcaveMajorant
declarations.doc: Least concave majorant on `[0, ∞)` of a real function, as the infimum of the values of its concave majorants; the empty-set convention `sInf ∅ = 0` is never used for bounded functions such as distribution functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.grenanderEstimator
declarations.doc: The Grenander estimator at `x`: the left slope of the least concave majorant of the empirical distribution function of the first `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNonincreasingDensity
declarations.doc: A nonincreasing probability density on `[0, ∞)`, vanishing on the negative half-line.

declarations.name: CKSD.twoSidedBrownianPath
declarations.doc: The path of two-sided Brownian motion built from two one-sided paths: `B₁` on the nonnegative half-line and `B₂` reflected on the negative half-line.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsChernoffArgmax
declarations.doc: `Z` is a realization of Chernoff's random variable `argmax (W(t) - t ^ 2)` for the two-sided Brownian motion `W` built from independent Brownian motions `B₁` and `B₂`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsConcaveMajorant
declarations.doc: A concave majorant of `F` on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.leastConcaveMajorant_le
declarations.doc: The least concave majorant lies below every concave majorant on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_leastConcaveMajorant
declarations.doc: A function bounded above on `[0, ∞)` lies below its least concave majorant there.

declarations.name: CKSD.concaveOn_leastConcaveMajorant
declarations.doc: The least concave majorant of a function bounded above on `[0, ∞)` is concave there.

declarations.name: CKSD.ConcaveOn.monotoneOn_of_bddBelow
declarations.doc: A concave function on `[0, ∞)` that is bounded below is monotone there.

declarations.name: CKSD.ConcaveOn.chord_le
declarations.doc: A concave function lies above its chord between two points.

declarations.name: CKSD.ConcaveOn.le_chord_of_le
declarations.doc: A concave function lies below the extension of its chord to the right.

declarations.name: CKSD.ConcaveOn.le_chord_of_ge
declarations.doc: A concave function lies below the extension of its chord to the left.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sample_grid
declarations.doc: The ordered distinct values of a positive sample, together with the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_le_of_partialSum_nonpos
declarations.doc: Summation by parts: a nonincreasing nonnegative weight sequence preserves nonpositivity of all partial sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_count_mul_div_slope_le
declarations.doc: The discrete core of the Grenander likelihood inequality: on the grid of a cumulative sum diagram with least concave majorant values `G`, slopes `s`, and counts `N`, weights `1 / s` integrate a nonincreasing nonnegative sequence `b` against the counts by at most `n` times its Riemann sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.concaveOn_affine
declarations.doc: An affine function is concave on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.leastConcaveMajorant_eq_affine
declarations.doc: The least concave majorant is affine on any interval where the majorized function is constant except possibly at the right endpoint.

declarations.name: CKSD.leastConcaveMajorant_eq_of_slope_lt
declarations.doc: At a strict kink of the least concave majorant on a grid of constancy intervals, the majorant touches the majorized function.

declarations.name: CKSD.grenanderEstimator_isMaximumLikelihood
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.11: the Grenander estimator is a nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator among nonincreasing densities on `[0, ∞)`. Scope: a fixed sample of `n ≥ 1` positive observations; the estimator is extended by zero to the nonpositive half-line, and the likelihood is the product of density values at the observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_grenanderEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.11: the cube-root limit law of the Grenander estimator at an interior point. The density `f` is a version vanishing on the negative half-line, positive and nonincreasing on `[0, ∞)`, and differentiable at `x₀ > 0` with negative derivative (which gives continuity at `x₀`); the limit is the law of `|4 f(x₀) f'(x₀)| ^ (1/3) Z` for Chernoff's `Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_hilbert_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.29, the separable-Hilbert-space CLT, characterized by scalar variances.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_sum_inner_smul_sq
declarations.doc: Pythagoras for the projection onto the span of an orthonormal family.

declarations.name: CKSD.pca_reconstruction_risk_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.31, finite-dimensional PCA minimizes expected reconstruction error about any specified center: no projection onto the span of `k` orthonormal vectors has risk below the tail eigenvalue sum. Attainment by the leading eigenvectors, uniqueness, and the Hilbert-space case are not asserted.

declarations.name: CKSD.restrictedL1Norm_convex_comb
declarations.doc: The coordinatewise L1 norm is convex along segments.

declarations.name: CKSD.lasso_cone_and_error_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.34, deterministic lasso prediction/L1 bounds and the cone condition.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergCount_le_and_le_card
declarations.doc: The Benjamini–Hochberg count `R` is at most `m` and satisfies its defining inequality `R ≤ #{j : x j ≤ R α / m}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_benjaminiHochbergCount
declarations.doc: Every `k ≤ m` satisfying the Benjamini–Hochberg inequality is at most the count.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergCount_update_zero
declarations.doc: Setting one p-value to zero: the Benjamini–Hochberg count does not decrease, it is at least one, and it is unchanged whenever the modified p-value is rejected by either count.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochberg_rejection_div_eq_sum
declarations.doc: Leave-one-out decomposition of a Benjamini–Hochberg rejection: the contribution of hypothesis `i` to the false discovery proportion splits over the value `k` of the count computed with `x i` replaced by zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_benjaminiHochbergCount
declarations.doc: The Benjamini–Hochberg count is a measurable function of the p-values.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjamini_hochberg_false_discovery_rate_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.37, FDR control for mutually independent p-values.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLogConcaveDensity
declarations.doc: An upper semicontinuous log-concave probability density on `ℝ^d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logLikelihoodFunctional
declarations.doc: The log-likelihood functional `∫ log f dP`, with value `⊥` when it equals `-∞`; it is intended for densities bounded above, such as log-concave densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLogConcaveProjection
declarations.doc: `f` is a log-concave projection of `P`: it maximizes `∫ log f dP` over `𝓕_d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tentFunction
declarations.doc: The tent function with heights `y` at the points `x`: the least concave function on the convex hull of the points with value at least `y i` at `x i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.densityHellingerSq
declarations.doc: Squared Hellinger distance `∫ (√f - √g) ^ 2` between two densities on `ℝ^d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.densityHellingerRisk
declarations.doc: Expected squared Hellinger loss of a density estimator from `n` independent observations with density `f₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logConcaveUpperRate
declarations.doc: The log-concave rate: `n ^ (-4/5)` for `d = 1` and `n ^ (-2/(d+1)) log n` for `d ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logConcaveLowerRate
declarations.doc: The log-concave minimax lower rate: `n ^ (-4/5)` for `d = 1` and `n ^ (-2/(d+1))` for `d ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_isLogConcaveProjection
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.28: existence and uniqueness of the log-concave projection, with its positivity set between the interior of the convex support of `P` and that support. The convex support is the closed convex hull of the support of `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_logConcaveMLE_tent
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.28: the log-concave maximum likelihood estimator of affinely spanning data is unique, vanishes outside the convex hull `C_n` of the data, and its logarithm is a tent function on `C_n`. Affine spanning of `ℝ^d` forces `n ≥ d + 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logConcaveMLE_hellingerRisk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.28: the worst-case squared Hellinger risk of the log-concave maximum likelihood estimator. The estimator `T` is required to be the maximum likelihood estimator on affinely spanning samples, which have probability one; the constant depends only on `d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logConcave_minimax_hellingerRisk_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.28: the minimax lower bound for log-concave density estimation in squared Hellinger distance, with a constant independent of the dimension. Estimators are jointly measurable functions of the sample and the evaluation point.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_measureReal_sub_le_totalVariationDistance
declarations.doc: Every measurable event difference is bounded by statistical total variation.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_cam_two_point_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.39: Le Cam's two-point lower bound with the statistical TV normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_mul_neg_log_sub_log_two_le_klDiv
declarations.doc: Binary data processing for one event: if `KL(P, Q)` is finite, then `P(A) log (1 / Q(A)) - log 2 ≤ KL(P, Q)`. Uses Statlib's chain rule for an event and the binary Kullback-Leibler formula.

declarations.name: CKSD.fano_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.40: Fano's bound in its finite-reference-KL form.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_pow_hammingCard_eq
declarations.doc: Exponential moment of the Hamming distance to a fixed binary word: `∑_y x ^ d(c, y) = (1 + x) ^ m`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_hamming_packing
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.45: a separated binary packing containing zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.assouad_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.46, TV version of Assouad's lemma for binary-valued estimators.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSequenceLaw
declarations.doc: Gaussian sequence observation law with noise standard deviation `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sequenceSquaredError
declarations.doc: Squared sequence error, taking value infinity when the difference is not square summable.

declarations.name: CKSD.sequenceEllipsoid
declarations.doc: Weighted ellipsoid; the radius convention is `sum (a_j theta_j)^2 ≤ R`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sobolevEllipsoid
declarations.doc: Sobolev ellipsoid indexed from frequency one.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSequenceMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Minimax squared risk over measurable Gaussian-sequence estimators.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSequenceLinearMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Linear minimax risk with coordinatewise shrinkage estimators.

declarations.name: CKSD.pinskerWeight
declarations.doc: Pinsker's positive-part shrinkage weights.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_gaussianSequenceMinimaxRisk_div_linear
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.9: asymptotic equivalence of arbitrary and linear minimax risks on an ellipsoid.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatson
declarations.doc: Nadaraya–Watson estimator; the value when all weights vanish is zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.regressionPredictionError
declarations.doc: Squared regression prediction error under the feature law.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator
declarations.doc: An isotonic least-squares estimator is a minimizer over the monotone cone.

declarations.name: CKSD.lassoObjective
declarations.doc: The lasso objective, with the `1/(2n)` squared-error normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLassoEstimator
declarations.doc: A lasso estimate minimizes the lasso objective.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasCompatibility
declarations.doc: Compatibility lower bound on the specified sparsity cone.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBasisPursuitEstimator
declarations.doc: Basis pursuit with a norm-bounded residual.

declarations.name: CKSD.softThreshold
declarations.doc: Scalar soft thresholding.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparseGaussianLaw
declarations.doc: Gaussian finite-dimensional sparse estimation experiment.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparseGaussianMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Minimax squared risk over the `s`-sparse vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparseGaussianMinimaxRisk_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.33: minimax sparse Gaussian rate with universal constants.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsHolderRegressionFunction
declarations.doc: A Hölder ball of order at most one on a specified domain.

declarations.name: CKSD.sequenceSquaredError_self
declarations.doc: Any sequence has zero squared error against itself, including nonsummable sequences.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatson_zero_bandwidth
declarations.doc: A zero bandwidth gives the unweighted mean when the kernel is nonzero at the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicCone
declarations.doc: Cone of nondecreasing finite real vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteVectorVariation
declarations.doc: Variation of a finite real vector, including the empty-vector value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicGaussianRisk
declarations.doc: Gaussian isotonic regression risk, divided by sample size.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicUnitBall
declarations.doc: The bounded monotone class used in the isotonic minimax lower bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicGaussianMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Gaussian isotonic minimax risk on the bounded monotone class.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockAverage
declarations.doc: Mean response over a contiguous block of indices.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicLeastSquares
declarations.doc: Isotonic least squares in its explicit max–min block-average form.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_isIsotonicRegressionEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.27: existence and uniqueness of the isotonic least-squares fit.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator.sum_mul_sub_nonpos
declarations.doc: Variational inequality for isotonic least squares: the residual of the fit has nonpositive inner product with every monotone direction `φ - θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator.suffix_sum_props
declarations.doc: Suffix sums of the isotonic residual are nonpositive, vanish at `0`, and vanish at every jump of the fit.

declarations.name: CKSD.isIsotonicRegressionEstimator_isotonicLeastSquares
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.27: the max–min block-average formula is the isotonic least-squares fit.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicGaussianRisk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.27: the adaptive variation risk bound for Gaussian isotonic least squares. The more general independent finite-variance-error version is not asserted here.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicGaussianMinimaxRisk_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.27: no estimator improves the Gaussian bounded-isotonic minimax rate.

declarations.name: CKSD.projectionModelFit
declarations.doc: Orthogonal least-squares fit within a selected linear model.

declarations.name: CKSD.penalizedModelCriterion
declarations.doc: Penalized empirical residual criterion for linear model selection.

declarations.name: CKSD.selectedProjectionRisk
declarations.doc: Normalized prediction risk of a selected projection fit in Gaussian regression.

declarations.name: CKSD.selectedProjectionRisk_oracle_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.35: the countable-model oracle inequality for penalized least squares. The prior weights, dimension penalty, and empirical minimizer are explicit.

declarations.name: CKSD.convex_isotonicCone
declarations.doc: The isotonic cone is convex.

declarations.name: CKSD.projectionModelFit_of_mem
declarations.doc: The fitted value is unchanged when the response already lies in the selected model.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatsonSample
declarations.doc: The finite-sample Nadaraya–Watson predictor formed from paired observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_nadarayaWatson_prediction_error_probability
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.7: universal prediction consistency of the Nadaraya–Watson estimator. The regression mean is given as a version of conditional expectation, with its `L²` property explicit. The kernel has upper and positive local lower ball bounds.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderRegressionClass
declarations.doc: Measurable functions on the line with a Hölder increment bound on the unit interval. There is no bound on an additive constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignRegressionLaw
declarations.doc: Fixed-design Gaussian regression law with noise standard deviation `σ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignRegressionRisk
declarations.doc: Mean integrated squared error of a predictor under the fixed-design Gaussian experiment.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderRegressionMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Fixed-design Hölder minimax mean integrated squared risk over jointly measurable estimators.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignLocalConstant
declarations.doc: Box-kernel local-constant regression on the fixed design.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderRegressionMinimaxRisk_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.22: the fixed-design `L²` Hölder minimax rate for orders at most one. This states both bounds; sup-norm risk and higher local-polynomial orders are not asserted.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_linear_gaussian
declarations.doc: Mean squared error of a linear statistic of independent Gaussian observations with common variance `v`: the variance `v ∑ aᵢ²` plus the squared bias.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_fixedDesign_window_ge
declarations.doc: On the grid `(i + 1) / n`, a window of half-width `h ≥ 1 / n` around a point of `[0, 1]` contains at least `n min(h, 1) / 2` design points.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignLocalConstant_risk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.22: a box-kernel local-constant estimator attains the `L²` rate for `0<β≤1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderDensityClass
declarations.doc: Hölder probability density class on the line, for smoothness orders at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.densityLaw
declarations.doc: The probability law represented by a real density.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteKernelDensityEstimator
declarations.doc: A finite-sample kernel density estimator at a specified point.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderDensityPointwiseMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Pointwise minimax risk for density estimation on a Hölder class.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sampleMean_sub_le
declarations.doc: Mean squared error of a sample mean under a product law: bias squared plus at most the second moment divided by the sample size.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_of_mem_holderDensityClass
declarations.doc: A Hölder probability density of order `β ∈ (0, 1]` is bounded by `1 / 2 + L`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_densityLaw
declarations.doc: The law with a probability density is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_densityLaw
declarations.doc: Integrals against a density law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_densityLaw_iff
declarations.doc: Integrability against a density law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_sub_div
declarations.doc: Change of variables `u = (x - y) / h` on the line.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteKernelDensityEstimator_risk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.26: the kernel upper bound for pointwise Hölder density risk with `0<β≤1`. The moment condition is the order-zero kernel condition appropriate in this range.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderDensityPointwiseMinimaxRisk_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.26: the matching pointwise minimax lower bound for Hölder orders at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatson_nonneg
declarations.doc: A Nadaraya–Watson predictor is nonnegative when observations and weights are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatson_const
declarations.doc: A nonempty normalized set of kernel weights reproduces a constant response.

declarations.name: CKSD.restrictedL1Norm_add_compl
declarations.doc: The coordinatewise L1 norm splits over complementary coordinate sets.

declarations.name: CKSD.restrictedL1Norm_le_add_sub
declarations.doc: A restricted reverse triangle bound for coordinatewise L1 norms.

declarations.name: CKSD.nullspace_property_iff_basis_pursuit_unique
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.48, equivalence between the nullspace property and unique basis pursuit.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparsity_smul_add_smul_le
declarations.doc: The support of `a • x + b • y` has at most `2 s` elements when `x` and `y` are `s`-sparse.

declarations.name: CKSD.inner_apply_le_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: Restricted orthogonality from the restricted isometry property: for `s`-sparse vectors with disjoint supports, `|⟪A x, A y⟫| ≤ δ ‖x‖ ‖y‖` when `A` has the RIP of order `2 s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nullspace_property_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.48, restricted-isometry sufficient condition for exact sparse recovery.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_decreasing_blocks
declarations.doc: Blocks of coordinates of size `s` in order of decreasing absolute value: `ℓ j` is the index of the block containing coordinate `j`. Blocks have at most `s` elements, a block followed by a nonempty block is full, and all block indices are smaller than `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sqrt_sum_sq_le_lifting
declarations.doc: Square-root lifting: if at most `s` values lie in `[m, M]` with `0 ≤ m`, and `m = 0` unless there are exactly `s` of them, then their Euclidean norm is at most their sum divided by `√s` plus `√s (M - m) / 4`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_sqrt_of_forall_two_mul_le
declarations.doc: If `2 lam c ≤ lam ^ 2 D + 1` for every real `lam`, then `c ≤ √D`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inner_apply_le_sqrt_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: Sharpened restricted orthogonality: if `‖A x‖² = (1 + t) ‖x‖²`, then for `s`-sparse vectors with disjoint supports `|⟪A x, A y⟫| ≤ √(δ² - t²) ‖x‖ ‖y‖` when `A` has the RIP of order `2 s` with constant `δ > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_le_sum_of_dominates
declarations.doc: A sum of nonnegative values over a set `S` is at most the sum over a set `B` that dominates its complement, provided `S ⊆ B` or `S` has at most as many elements as `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripNullspaceRho
declarations.doc: The robust null space constant `ρ(δ) = δ / (√(1 - δ²) - δ / 4)` of the restricted isometry analysis of basis pursuit.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripNullspaceTau
declarations.doc: The robust null space constant `τ(δ) = √(1 + δ) / (√(1 - δ²) - δ / 4)` written as `4 √(1 - δ²) / ((4 √(1 - δ²) - δ) √(1 - δ))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripNullspace_constants
declarations.doc: The constants of the robust null space property: for `0 ≤ δ < 4 / √41`, `0 ≤ ρ(δ) < 1` and `τ(δ) > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.robust_nullspace_property_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.49, robust null space property: if `A` has the RIP of order `2 s` with constant `δ < 4 / √41`, then `‖v_S‖₂ ≤ ρ(δ) / √s ‖v_{Sᶜ}‖₁ + τ(δ) ‖A v‖` for every `v` and every set `S` of at most `s` coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.sqrt_add_le_sqrt_add_sqrt
declarations.doc: The square root is subadditive on nonnegative reals.

declarations.name: CKSD.basis_pursuit_error_bound_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.49: stable basis pursuit, with constants depending only on the RIP bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.airyLeadingAsymptotic
declarations.doc: The leading term `s ^ (-1/4) exp (-(2/3) s ^ (3/2)) / (2 √π)` of the Airy function as `s → ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsHastingsMcLeodSolution
declarations.doc: The Hastings–McLeod solution of Painlevé II: a twice continuously differentiable solution of `q'' = s q + 2 q ^ 3` with `q(s) ~ Ai(s)` as `s → ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tracyWidomOneCDF
declarations.doc: The Tracy–Widom distribution function `F₁` of the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble, built from a Hastings–McLeod solution `q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.standardGaussianMatrixLaw
declarations.doc: The law of an `n × p` matrix with independent standard normal entries.

declarations.name: CKSD.largestSampleCovarianceEigenvalue
declarations.doc: The largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance `n⁻¹ XᵀX` of an `n × p` data matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.johnstoneCenter
declarations.doc: Johnstone's centering `(√(n-1) + √p) ^ 2 / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_largestSampleCovarianceEigenvalue_tracyWidom
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.38: Johnstone's Tracy–Widom limit for the largest eigenvalue of a white Wishart matrix as `n, p → ∞` with `p / n → y ∈ (0, ∞)`, in the form of convergence of distribution functions to the continuous limit `F₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.standardGaussianArrayLaw
declarations.doc: The law of a doubly infinite array of independent standard normal variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.spikedDataMatrix
declarations.doc: The `n × p` spiked data matrix with covariance `diag(α, 1, …, 1)` read off a standard normal array.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_largestEigenvalue_spiked_subcritical
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.38, subcritical spike: for `1 < α ≤ 1 + √y` the largest sample covariance eigenvalue converges almost surely to the bulk edge `(1 + √y) ^ 2`. Scope: diagonal spiked covariance on the array coupling described in the module header.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_largestEigenvalue_spiked_supercritical
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.38, supercritical spike: for `α > 1 + √y` the largest sample covariance eigenvalue converges almost surely to `α + y α / (α - 1)`. Scope: diagonal spiked covariance on the array coupling described in the module header.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleAutocovariance
declarations.doc: Sample autocovariance using the sample mean and divisor `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.riskSetSize
declarations.doc: The risk-set cardinality at the `i`th observed time.

declarations.name: CKSD.nelsonAalenEstimator
declarations.doc: Nelson–Aalen estimator, expressed as a sum over individual observed failures.

declarations.name: CKSD.kaplanMeierEstimator
declarations.doc: Kaplan–Meier product, with one factor for each individual observed failure.

declarations.name: CKSD.brownianBridgeSupremum
declarations.doc: Supremum of the absolute Brownian bridge on the unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.cusumBridgeStatistic
declarations.doc: Standardized maximum of a finite partial-sum bridge.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_cusumBridgeStatistic
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.39: the iid finite-variance CUSUM statistic converges to the Brownian-bridge supremum.

declarations.name: CKSD.cusumBridgeStatistic_zero
declarations.doc: At sample size zero, the standardized CUSUM statistic uses division-by-zero value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.coxRiskMean
declarations.doc: The Cox risk-set average `ē(u) = 𝔼[Y(u) Z e^{β·Z}] / 𝔼[Y(u) e^{β·Z}]`, with `Y(u) = 1{min(T,C) ≥ u}`, for a law of `(Z, T, C)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.coxInformation
declarations.doc: The Cox information `𝓘 = 𝔼 ∫_0^τ (Z - ē(u))^{⊗2} dN(u)`, with `N` jumping at an observed failure `T ≤ C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.coxPartialLikelihood_asymptotics
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.30: consistency and asymptotic normality of the maximum partial-likelihood estimator in the Cox model, with the partial likelihood restricted to failures in `[0, τ]`, bounded covariates, conditionally independent censoring, `P(min(T,C) ≥ τ) > 0`, and positive definite information. The estimator is any measurable choice that maximizes the partial likelihood whenever a maximizer exists. The efficiency and log-rank interpretations are not restated.

declarations.name: CKSD.jumpIntegral
declarations.doc: The pathwise Lebesgue–Stieltjes integral `∫_(0,t] H dN = ∑_{0 < s ≤ t} ΔN(s) H(s)` of a pure-jump path with finitely many jumps on `(0, t]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCountingPath
declarations.doc: A counting path: starts at `0`, nondecreasing, right-continuous, integer-valued, with jumps of size at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCountingProcessWithIntensity
declarations.doc: A `k`-variate counting process without simultaneous jumps, with nonnegative predictable locally integrable intensities `λ_h` for which `N_h - ∫_0^· λ_h` are martingales.

declarations.name: CKSD.countingMartingaleTransform
declarations.doc: The counting-process martingale transform `M_j(t) = ∑_h ∫_0^t H_{jh} (dN_h - λ_h ds)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_countingMartingaleTransform
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.34: Rebolledo's central limit theorem for counting-process martingale transforms, in finite-dimensional form: under convergence in probability of the predictable variations to a continuous deterministic `V` with positive-semidefinite increments and the Lindeberg condition, the values of `M^{(n)}` at finitely many times in `[0, τ]` converge jointly in law to those of the continuous Gaussian martingale with covariance `V(s ∧ t)`. Restrictions: the compensated counting processes are martingales rather than local martingales, all processes live on one probability space, and weak convergence in `D[0,τ]^k` is replaced by convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions.

declarations.name: CKSD.pastSigmaAlgebra
declarations.doc: The past σ-algebra `σ(X_s : s ≤ t)` of a real process on `ℤ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.futureSigmaAlgebra
declarations.doc: The future σ-algebra `σ(X_s : s ≥ t)` of a real process on `ℤ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.strongMixingCoefficient
declarations.doc: The strong mixing coefficient `α(k) = sup |P(A ∩ B) - P(A) P(B)|` over `A ∈ σ(X_s : s ≤ 0)`, `B ∈ σ(X_s : s ≥ k)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockMean
declarations.doc: The mean of the block `x_i, …, x_{i+b-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.movingBlockBootstrapLaw
declarations.doc: The moving-block bootstrap law of `√(ℓb) (X̄*_n - 𝔼* X̄*_n)` given data `x_0, …, x_{n-1}`, for block length `b` and `ℓ = ⌊n/b⌋` blocks with starting indices uniform on `n - b + 1` positions.

declarations.name: CKSD.movingBlockBootstrap_consistent
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.11: consistency of the moving-block bootstrap for the mean of a strictly stationary strongly mixing sequence with `𝔼|X|^{2+δ} < ∞` and `∑ α(k)^{δ/(2+δ)} < ∞`: the autocovariances are absolutely summable, `√n (X̄_n - μ) ⇒ N(0, σ²_∞)`, and the Kolmogorov distance between the bootstrap law and the law of `√n (X̄_n - μ)` tends to `0` in probability, for block lengths `b → ∞` with `b/n → 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.kernelGram
declarations.doc: The Gram matrix `(k i j)_{i,j<n}` of a covariance kernel on the first `n` indices.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearPredictionError
declarations.doc: The error `ψ - ∑_i a_i h_i` of the best linear predictor of `ψ` from the first `n` coordinates, computed as if the covariance were `k`, with cross-covariances of `ψ` taken under the law `Q` whose coordinate covariance is `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.stein_linearPrediction_equivalent_gaussian
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.21: Stein's theorem on asymptotically efficient prediction under equivalent Gaussian laws. The coordinates are linearly independent under `k₀`, the laws `P₀` and `P₁` are centred Gaussian with covariances `k₀` and `k₁`, and `ψ` ranges over the closed linear span `H` of the coordinates in `L²(P₀)`. Uniformly over `ψ ∈ H` with nonzero `P₀`-error, the relative excess error of the `k₁`-predictor and the relative misstatement of its error tend to zero; the exchanged roles are the same statement applied to `(k₁, P₁, k₀, P₀)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.distributionUpperEndpoint
declarations.doc: Right endpoint of a real distribution, allowed to be infinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.thresholdExcessLaw
declarations.doc: The conditional law of the excess over a threshold.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasExtremeValueDomainOfAttraction
declarations.doc: Membership in the domain of attraction of the unit-scale generalized extreme-value law.

declarations.name: CKSD.thresholdParetoDiscrepancy
declarations.doc: Uniform discrepancy over all nonnegative excesses, including the terminal jump, against a fitted generalized Pareto law.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasExtremeValueDomainOfAttraction_iff_pareto_excesses
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.47: Pickands–Balkema–de Haan equivalence, allowing finite upper endpoints.

declarations.name: CKSD.tailQuantile
declarations.doc: Tail quantile of order `1-1/t`, used for `t>1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasRegularlyVaryingTail
declarations.doc: Positive regularly varying tail of index `-1/γ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasSecondOrderTailQuantile
declarations.doc: Second-order regular variation of the tail quantile, with an eventually constant-sign remainder.

declarations.name: CKSD.hillEstimator
declarations.doc: Hill estimator from the largest `k` observations. It is zero outside `1≤k<n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_hillEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.49: Hill central limit theorem under second-order regular variation.

declarations.name: CKSD.hillEstimator_zero
declarations.doc: The Hill estimator of order zero uses the explicitly specified zero convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.thresholdExcessLaw_generalizedPareto
declarations.doc: TauCeti's exact Pareto threshold stability in the excess-law interface.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_binomial_poissonMeasure
declarations.doc: Poisson limit of the binomial law tested against bounded functions: if `n p_n → τ`, then `∫ f d Bin(n, p_n) → ∫ f d Po(τ)`. The pointwise limit of the probabilities is Mathlib's `tendsto_choose_mul_pow_of_tendsto_mul_atTop`; the bound `C (sup_n n p_n)^k / k!` allows Tannery's theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_univ_fin_eq_card_filter_range
declarations.doc: Counting indices in `Fin n` and in `range n` agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_card_exceedances_binomial
declarations.doc: The number of exceedances of a level among the first `n` iid observations is binomial, by TauCeti's Poisson-binomial law of counts of independent events.

declarations.name: CKSD.cdf_sInf_setOf_le_cdf
declarations.doc: The generalized quantile `sInf {t | c ≤ F t}` of a level `c ∈ (0, 1)` satisfies `c ≤ F(sInf …)`, by right continuity, and `F t < c` below it.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_forall_le_eq_pow
declarations.doc: The probability that the first `n` iid observations do not exceed `c` is `F(c)^n`, written as `(1 - (1 - F(c)))^n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_maximum_of_regularly_varying_tail
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.46, the regularly varying positive-tail sufficient condition for a Fréchet limit.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_maximum_and_exceedance_count_of_tail_limit
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.48 (independent scope) and GAPS 106.50, finite-intensity exceedance limit; also the independent part of 106.48.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_prodMk_of_indepFun_of_indepFun_prodMk
declarations.doc: If `X` is independent of `Y` and the pair `(X, Y)` is independent of `Z`, then `X` is independent of the pair `(Y, Z)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.iIndepFun_of_indepFun_finPrefix
declarations.doc: A sequence of random variables is mutually independent when each term is independent of the vector of its predecessors.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_prodMk_left_of_indepFun_prodMk
declarations.doc: If `A` is independent of the pair `(B, C)` and `B` is independent of `C`, then the pair `(A, B)` is independent of `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_apply_prefix_of_indepFun
declarations.doc: In a family consisting of an initial value `x₀`, a sequence `w`, and a mutually independent sequence `v`, with `x₀` independent of `(w, v)` and `w` independent of `v`, the term `v t` is independent of `x₀`, the whole sequence `w`, and the terms `v i` with `i < t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_apply_prefix_of_indepFun'
declarations.doc: In the setting of `indepFun_apply_prefix_of_indepFun`, with `w` mutually independent, the term `w t` is independent of `x₀`, the terms `w i` with `i < t`, and the whole sequence `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_toEuclideanLin_multivariateGaussian_zero
declarations.doc: A matrix image of a centered multivariate Gaussian vector is centered Gaussian with the congruent covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_toEuclideanLin_add_of_indepFun
declarations.doc: For independent centered Gaussian vectors `ε` and `v`, the combination `A₁ ε + A₂ v` is centered Gaussian with covariance `A₁ S₁ A₁ᵀ + A₂ S₂ A₂ᵀ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_toEuclideanLin_add_of_indepFun
declarations.doc: Two linear combinations `A₁ ε + A₂ v` and `B₁ ε + B₂ v` of independent centered Gaussian vectors are independent when their cross-covariance `A₁ S₁ B₁ᵀ + A₂ S₂ B₂ᵀ` vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianShiftKernel
declarations.doc: The Gaussian location kernel `m ↦ N(m, S)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianShiftKernel_apply
declarations.doc: The Gaussian shift kernel at `m` is the Gaussian law with mean `m` and covariance `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_multivariateGaussianPDF_uncurry
declarations.doc: The multivariate Gaussian density is jointly measurable in the mean and the point.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_prodMk_add_eq_compProd
declarations.doc: If `Z` has law `N(0, S)` and is independent of `Y`, then the joint law of `Y` and `g(Y) + Z` is the composition of the law of `Y` with the Gaussian kernel `y ↦ N(g y, S)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDistrib_add_eq_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: If `Z` has law `N(0, S)` and is independent of `Y`, then the conditional law of `g(Y) + Z` given `Y = y` is `N(g y, S)` for almost every `y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_withDensity_comp_measurableEquiv
declarations.doc: Transport of a measure with density along a measurable equivalence.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs
declarations.doc: The hypotheses of the Kalman filter theorem: positive-semidefinite noise and initial covariances, a Gaussian initial state, independent Gaussian white noises independent of the initial state, and nonsingular innovation covariances.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.predCov_posSemidef'
declarations.doc: Every predicted covariance is positive semidefinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.aemeasurable_indepFun_predErr
declarations.doc: The prediction error and the observation record at time `t` are jointly almost everywhere measurable, and the observation noise at time `t` is independent of them.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.aemeasurable_indepFun_filtErr
declarations.doc: The filtering error at time `t` and the observation record up to time `t` are jointly almost everywhere measurable, and the state noise at time `t` is independent of them.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.measurement_update
declarations.doc: Measurement update. If the prediction error at time `t` has law `N(0, P_{t|t-1})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_{t-1}`, then the innovation has law `N(0, Σ_t)`, the filtering error has law `N(0, P_{t|t})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_t`, and the innovation is independent of `y_0, …, y_{t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.time_update
declarations.doc: Time update. If the filtering error at time `t` has law `N(0, P_{t|t})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_t`, then the prediction error at time `t + 1` has law `N(0, P_{t+1|t})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.predErr_hasLaw_indepFun
declarations.doc: The prediction errors: at every time `t`, `x_t - x_{t|t-1}` has law `N(0, P_{t|t-1})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_{t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.condDistrib_state
declarations.doc: Conditionally on `y_0, …, y_t`, the state `x_t` is Gaussian with the filtered mean and covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.condDistrib_state_succ
declarations.doc: Conditionally on `y_0, …, y_t`, the state `x_{t+1}` is Gaussian with the predicted mean and covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.hasLaw_innovation
declarations.doc: The innovation at time `t` has law `N(0, Σ_t)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.indepFun_innovation_obsPrefix
declarations.doc: The innovation at time `t` is independent of `y_0, …, y_{t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.iIndepFun_innovation

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.map_obsPrefix_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: The law of `(y_0, …, y_{n-1})` has density the product of the one-step predictive densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.kalmanFilter
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.7: the Kalman filter for a finite-dimensional time-varying linear Gaussian state-space model with positive-semidefinite noise and initial covariances, independent Gaussian white noises independent of the Gaussian initial state, and nonsingular innovation covariances. Conditionally on `y_0, …, y_t`, the state `x_t` is Gaussian with the filtered mean and covariance and `x_{t+1}` with the predicted ones; the innovations `y_t - H_t x_{t|t-1}` are independent with laws `N(0, Σ_t)`; and the density of `(y_0, …, y_{n-1})` is the product of the one-step predictive densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel
declarations.doc: Coefficients of a time-varying linear Gaussian state-space model with state dimension `d` and observation dimension `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovCovOf
declarations.doc: Innovation covariance `H_t C H_tᵀ + R_t` for a predicted covariance `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.gainOf
declarations.doc: Kalman gain `C H_tᵀ (H_t C H_tᵀ + R_t)⁻¹` for a predicted covariance `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtCovOf
declarations.doc: Filtered covariance `C - K_t H_t C` for a predicted covariance `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predCov
declarations.doc: Predicted covariances `P_{t|t-1}`, with `P_{0|-1}` the initial covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovCov
declarations.doc: Innovation covariances `Σ_t = H_t P_{t|t-1} H_tᵀ + R_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.gain
declarations.doc: Kalman gains `K_t = P_{t|t-1} H_tᵀ Σ_t⁻¹`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtCov
declarations.doc: Filtered covariances `P_{t|t} = P_{t|t-1} - K_t H_t P_{t|t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predMean
declarations.doc: Predicted means `x_{t|t-1}` as functions of the observations, with `x_{0|-1}` the initial mean and `x_{t+1|t} = F_t x_{t|t}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtMean
declarations.doc: Filtered means `x_{t|t} = x_{t|t-1} + K_t (y_t - H_t x_{t|t-1})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.state
declarations.doc: The state process `x_0 = x₀`, `x_{t+1} = F_t x_t + w_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.observationProcess
declarations.doc: The observation process `y_t = H_t x_t + v_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.extendObservations
declarations.doc: Extension of a finite observation record `y_0, …, y_{n-1}` by zeros.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_extendObservations_apply
declarations.doc: A zero-extended observation record is measurable in each coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.extendObservations_of_lt
declarations.doc: The zero extension of a finite record returns the recorded values.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predMean_congr
declarations.doc: The predicted mean at time `t` depends only on the observations before time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtMean_congr
declarations.doc: The filtered mean at time `t` depends only on the observations up to time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predMean_succ
declarations.doc: The time update of the mean: `x_{t+1|t} = F_t x_{t|t}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_predMean
declarations.doc: The predicted mean is a measurable function of a measurably parametrized observation sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_filtMean
declarations.doc: The filtered mean is a measurable function of a measurably parametrized observation sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.state_congr
declarations.doc: The state at time `s` is unchanged by a change of sample space that preserves the initial state and the state noises before time `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_state
declarations.doc: The state process is measurable when the initial state and the noises are.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_observationProcess
declarations.doc: The observation process is measurable when the state and the observation noise are.

declarations.name: CKSD.extendObservations_snoc
declarations.doc: Appending a value to a finite record does not change its zero extension below the old length.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovDensity
declarations.doc: The product of the one-step predictive densities `∏_{i<n} φ(y_i; H_i x_{i|i-1}, Σ_i)` of an observation record `(y_0, …, y_{n-1})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_predMean_extendObservations
declarations.doc: The predicted mean computed from a zero-extended record is measurable in the record.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_filtMean_extendObservations
declarations.doc: The filtered mean computed from a zero-extended record is measurable in the record.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_innovDensity_factor
declarations.doc: Each one-step predictive density factor is measurable in the record.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_innovDensity
declarations.doc: The product of predictive densities is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovDensity_snoc
declarations.doc: The product of predictive densities factors over the last observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.posSemidef_mul_mul_transpose
declarations.doc: A real congruence `A S Aᵀ` of a positive-semidefinite matrix is positive semidefinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.gain_mul_innovCov
declarations.doc: With a nonsingular innovation covariance, `K_t Σ_t = P_{t|t-1} H_tᵀ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtErr_innovation_cross
declarations.doc: The cross-covariance of the filtered error and the innovation vanishes: `(I - K_t H_t) P_{t|t-1} H_tᵀ - K_t R_t = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtCov_eq_joseph
declarations.doc: Joseph form of the filtered covariance: with a nonsingular innovation covariance, `(I - K_t H_t) P (I - K_t H_t)ᵀ + K_t R_t K_tᵀ = P - K_t H_t P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predCov_posSemidef
declarations.doc: Under positive-semidefinite noise and initial covariances and nonsingular innovation covariances, every predicted covariance is positive semidefinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtCov_posSemidef
declarations.doc: Under the hypotheses of `predCov_posSemidef`, every filtered covariance is positive semidefinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovCov_posDef
declarations.doc: Under the hypotheses of `predCov_posSemidef`, every innovation covariance is positive definite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.obsProc
declarations.doc: The observation process `y_t = H_t x_t + v_t` driven by `x₀`, `w`, and `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.obsPrefix
declarations.doc: The observation record `(y_0, …, y_{n-1})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predErr
declarations.doc: The prediction error `x_t - x_{t|t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtErr
declarations.doc: The filtering error `x_t - x_{t|t}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovation
declarations.doc: The innovation `y_t - H_t x_{t|t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovation_eq
declarations.doc: The innovation is `H_t (x_t - x_{t|t-1}) + v_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtErr_eq

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predErr_succ
declarations.doc: The prediction error at time `t + 1` is `F_t (x_t - x_{t|t}) + w_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.obsPrefix_succ_eq
declarations.doc: The observation record up to time `t` is obtained from the record before time `t` and the innovation at time `t` by appending `e_t + H_t x_{t|t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.obsProc_congr

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predErr_obsPrefix_congr
declarations.doc: The prediction error and the observation record at time `t` are unchanged by a change of sample space that preserves the initial state and the noises before time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtErr_obsPrefix_congr
declarations.doc: The filtering error at time `t` and the observation record up to time `t` are unchanged by a change of sample space that preserves the initial state, the state noises before time `t`, and the observation noises up to time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_obsProc
declarations.doc: The observation process is measurable for measurable inputs.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_obsPrefix
declarations.doc: The observation record is measurable for measurable inputs.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_predErr
declarations.doc: The prediction error is measurable for measurable inputs.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_filtErr
declarations.doc: The filtering error is measurable for measurable inputs.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.exists_predErr_obsPrefix_eq_comp
declarations.doc: The prediction error and the observation record at time `t` are a measurable function of the initial state, the state noises, and the observation noises before time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.exists_filtErr_obsPrefix_eq_comp
declarations.doc: The filtering error at time `t` and the observation record up to time `t` are a measurable function of the initial state, the state noises before time `t`, and the observation noises.

declarations.name: CKSD.integratedIntensity

declarations.doc: GAPS 106.44, the pathwise comparison underlying the false-alarm waiting-time bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihoodRatioProcess_zero

declarations.doc: The bridge is pinned at its right endpoint.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_stopped_sum_and_integral_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.37, Wald's stopped-sum identity under the past/future independence condition.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_mul_measure_exists_le_supermartingale_le_one
declarations.doc: Finite-horizon maximal bound `c · P(max_{k ≤ n} M_k ≥ c) ≤ 1` for a nonnegative supermartingale with `M_0 ≤ 1`, by optional stopping at the capped hitting time of `[c, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_iSup_supermartingale_ge_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.38: infinite-horizon Ville inequality, including a supremum not attained.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_of_measurable_biSup
declarations.doc: Functions measurable with respect to the σ-algebras generated by disjoint index sets of an independent family are independent.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_biSup_sum
declarations.doc: A finite partial sum over indices in `S` is measurable for the σ-algebra generated by `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_biSup_le
declarations.doc: The σ-algebra generated by a subfamily of measurable functions is coarser than the ambient one.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_mul_measureReal_exists_le_abs_sum_le
declarations.doc: **Kolmogorov's maximal inequality** for independent, centred, square-integrable variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_shift
declarations.doc: For independent standardized variables, a block sum of length `n` has second moment `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_mul_measureReal_exists_le_abs_sum_shift_le
declarations.doc: Kolmogorov's maximal inequality for a block of `r` standardized independent variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_sum_randomIndex_sub
declarations.doc: Anscombe's comparison: when `N n / n → k` in probability, the partial sum at the random index `N n` differs from the partial sum at `⌈k n⌉` by `o_P(√⌈k n⌉)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_mul_sub_self
declarations.doc: If `W n` converges in law and `R n → 1` in probability, then `R n W n - W n → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityConst_sqrt_ceil_div
declarations.doc: If `N n / n → k > 0` in probability, then `√(⌈k n⌉ / N n) → 1` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_randomIndex
declarations.doc: Evaluating a sequence of measurable functions at a measurable random index is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sqrt_mul_sampleAverage_sub
declarations.doc: The standardized sample average at a fixed sample size is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_random_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.42: Anscombe's theorem for an observation-dependent random sample size.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearProcess
declarations.doc: The two-sided linear process `X_t = ∑_j ψ_j Z_{t-j}`, as a pointwise series.

declarations.name: CKSD.transferFunction
declarations.doc: The transfer function `∑_j ψ_j e^{-ijx}` of a two-sided filter.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearProcessSpectralDensity
declarations.doc: The spectral density `σ² |∑_j ψ_j e^{-ijx}|² / (2π)` of a linear process with innovation variance `σ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.periodogram
declarations.doc: The periodogram `I_n(x) = (2πn)⁻¹ |∑_{t<n} X_t e^{-itx}|²` of `X_0, …, X_{n-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nearestFourierFrequency
declarations.doc: The Fourier frequency `2πk/n` nearest to `x`, with `k` the rounded value of `nx/(2π)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLagWindow
declarations.doc: A lag window: an even function with `w 0 = 1`, `|w| ≤ 1`, vanishing outside `[-1,1]`, continuous at `0` and continuous on `[-1,1]` off a finite set (this contains the piecewise continuous windows).

declarations.name: CKSD.lagWindowEstimator
declarations.doc: The lag-window spectral estimator `(2π)⁻¹ ∑_{|h| ≤ r} w(h/r) γ̂(h) e^{-ihx}`, written with `γ̂(-h) = γ̂(h)` as a cosine sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_periodogram_div_spectralDensity
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.6: periodogram ordinates at Fourier frequencies nearest to fixed frequencies in `(0, π)`, divided by the spectral density, converge jointly in law to independent standard exponential variables, for a linear process with absolutely summable coefficients and iid innovations of finite positive variance. The non-consistency corollary is not restated.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_lagWindowEstimator_moments
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.6: asymptotic mean and variance, and mean-square consistency, of a lag-window spectral estimator for a linear process with `∑ |ψ_j| |j|^{1/2} < ∞` and iid innovations with finite fourth moment, when the truncation point `r` satisfies `r → ∞` and `r/n → 0`. The window is assumed continuous at `0` (see `IsLagWindow`).

declarations.name: CKSD.infDist_past_sq_eq_kolmogorov
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.16: Kolmogorov's (Szegő's) formula for the one-step prediction error of a centred weakly stationary sequence from its infinite past. Here `X` lies in a complex inner-product space, `⟪X s, X t⟫ = γ(t - s)`, the spectral measure `F` lives on `(-π, π]`, and `f` is the density of its absolutely continuous part. The value `0` is taken exactly when `log f` fails to be integrable or `f` vanishes on a set of positive measure, i.e. when `∫ log f = -∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.arPolynomial
declarations.doc: The autoregressive polynomial `φ(z) = 1 - ∑_{i=1}^p φ_i z^i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.maPolynomial
declarations.doc: The moving-average polynomial `θ(z) = 1 + ∑_{j=1}^q θ_j z^j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaSpectralShape
declarations.doc: The ARMA spectral shape `g(x; β) = |θ(e^{-ix})|² / |φ(e^{-ix})|²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lastArCoefficient
declarations.doc: The last autoregressive coefficient `φ_p`, read as `0` when `p = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lastMaCoefficient
declarations.doc: The last moving-average coefficient `θ_q`, read as `0` when `q = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaAdmissibleParameters
declarations.doc: Causal, invertible, identifiable ARMA(p,q) parameters: `φ(z) θ(z) ≠ 0` on the closed unit disc, no common zeros, and `(φ_p, θ_q) ≠ (0,0)` (vacuous for `p = q = 0`).

declarations.name: CKSD.whittleObjective
declarations.doc: The Whittle objective `n⁻¹ ∑_j I_n(ω_j) / g(ω_j; β)` over the Fourier frequencies `ω_j = 2πj/n`, `0 ≤ j < n`; by `2π`-periodicity this equals the sum over `(-π, π]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaAsymptoticInformation
declarations.doc: The asymptotic information matrix `W(β) = (4π)⁻¹ ∫_{-π}^{π} ∇ log g ∇ log gᵀ` of ARMA estimation.

declarations.name: CKSD.whittleEstimator_asymptotics
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.17, Whittle-estimator case: for a causal invertible ARMA(p,q) process with iid, not necessarily Gaussian, innovations of variance `σ² > 0`, every measurable approximate minimizer of the Whittle objective over the admissible parameters (to within `(n+1)⁻²`) is strongly consistent, the Whittle innovation-variance estimator `2π · min` converges almost surely to `σ²`, and `√n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, W(β)⁻¹)`. The process is any `L²`-bounded solution of the ARMA equations, which is the stationary causal solution. The Gaussian maximum-likelihood and least-squares estimators, and the autoregressive identity `W⁻¹ = σ² Γ_p⁻¹`, are not covered.

declarations.name: CKSD.spectralRandomField
declarations.doc: Spectral random-phase field for a spectral measure of total real mass `mass`.

declarations.name: CKSD.twoPointPhaseLaw
declarations.doc: The phase law of the random field, uniform on the two points `{0, π}`; its first circular moment `𝔼 e^{iφ}` vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_exp_twoPointPhaseLaw
declarations.doc: The first circular moment of the two-point phase law vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.normalizedSpectralMeasure
declarations.doc: The spectral measure normalized to a probability measure, with the Dirac mass at the origin for the zero measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.real_mul_integral_normalizedSpectralMeasure
declarations.doc: Integrating against the spectral measure is the total mass times integrating against the normalized spectral measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.spectralRandomField_eq
declarations.doc: The random-phase field factors into a frequency part and a phase part.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_spectralRandomField
declarations.doc: The random-phase field has constant modulus `√mass`.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_spectralRandomField
declarations.doc: The random-phase field is jointly continuous in location and randomness.

declarations.name: CKSD.spectralRandomField_mul_star
declarations.doc: The product `f(x) f(y)^*` of the random-phase field depends only on the frequency and on `x - y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_stationary_field_of_spectral_measure
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.24: a finite spectral measure is realized by a mean-square continuous stationary field. This concerns the Fourier/random-field assertion, not Matérn differentiability.

declarations.name: CKSD.logLikelihoodPartialSum
declarations.doc: Partial sums of iid log-likelihood increments.

declarations.name: CKSD.rangePartialSum
declarations.doc: Partial sums of a finite coordinate vector indexed by `range n`, truncated at `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_rangePartialSum
declarations.doc: Truncated partial sums of a finite coordinate vector are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.rangePartialSum_restrict
declarations.doc: Up to the length of the vector, truncated partial sums of the restriction of a sequence are its partial sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_stopped_exponential_eq_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.41: Wald's fundamental stopped exponential identity at a first exit time. The finite-valued time `N` is a measurable version of the almost surely finite first exit. Its existence is a hypothesis; no separate increment-sign or boundary-sign assumptions are needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_nelsonAalenEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.28, fixed-time Nelson–Aalen CLT for absolutely continuous failure times.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_kaplanMeierEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.29, fixed-time Kaplan–Meier CLT under independent censoring.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_of_measurable_iSup
declarations.doc: A function measurable with respect to `σ(ε_s : s ∈ S)` is independent of `ε_k` for `k ∉ S`, for an independent family `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_of_measurable_pastSigmaAlgebra
declarations.doc: A function of the strict past `σ(ε_s : s < t)` of an independent sequence is independent of `ε_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_pastSigmaAlgebra_of_le

declarations.name: CKSD.pastSigmaAlgebra_mono

declarations.name: CKSD.pastSigmaAlgebra_le
declarations.doc: The past σ-algebras of a measurable process are sub-σ-algebras.

declarations.name: CKSD.garchCoeff

declarations.name: CKSD.garchTerm

declarations.name: CKSD.garchTerm_nonneg
